## Adapter Specification Summary

### **LEPTOS ADAPTERS**

#### **1. Heading (Leptos) — `/spec/leptos-components/utility/heading.md`**

**Public API:**
```rust
#[component] pub fn Heading(...) -> impl IntoView
```

**Props:** Full parity with core. Accepts `Children` (line 151).

```rust
#[component]
pub fn Highlight() -> impl IntoView {
    let props = highlight::Props::default();
    let api = highlight::Api::new(props);
    let locale = use_locale();

    view! {
        <span ..api.root_attrs()>
            {api.chunks(&locale).into_iter().map(|chunk| {
                let attrs = api.chunk_attrs(chunk.highlighted);
                if chunk.highlighted {
                    Either::Left(view! { <mark ..attrs>{chunk.text}</mark> })
                } else {
                    Either::Right(view! { <span ..attrs>{chunk.text}</span> })
                }
            }).collect_view()}
        </span>
    }
}
```

- Chunk wrappers remain explicit so identity is preserved (line 180)
- Consolidation rules stable across rerenders (line 181)
- Root sets `dir="auto"` via core API; adapters don't duplicate (line 148)

### Standalone Function
**File:** `highlight/mod.rs:343-412`

```rust
pub fn highlight_chunks<'a>(props: &'a Props, locale: &Locale) -> Vec<HighlightChunk<'a>>
```

**Behavior:**
- Returns empty vec if `text` is empty
- Returns single non-highlighted chunk if `query` is empty or all empty strings
- Performs locale-aware Unicode case folding when `ignore_case = true`
- Merges overlapping **and adjacent** ranges before returning
- All-or-nothing fuzzy matching: if any query char missing, that query contributes zero ranges
- Handles fold expansions: `ß → ss`, Turkish dotted/dotless I, Greek final sigma, Lithuanian
- Adapters never see back-to-back highlighted chunks

## Key Nuances by Component

### Heading
- **No state machine** — purely an attribute mapper
- **Context-driven:** resolves level from `Props::level` (explicit override) or `HeadingContext` (context level)
- **Two helper modules:** `heading_level_provider` and `section` for managing context
- **Native element optimization:** `root_attrs(is_native_heading_element)` omits redundant ARIA when using `<h1>`-`<h6>`

### Landmark
- **No state machine** — purely an attribute mapper with localization
- **Requires `Env` + localized `Messages`:** `Api::new(props, env, messages)`
- **Two categories requiring accessible names:** `Role::Form` and `Role::Region` (emits debug warning if missing)
- **Special case:** `Role::Search` prefers fallback element (`prefers_generic_fallback_element()`)
- **Mutually exclusive labeling:** `aria-labelledby` takes precedence over `aria-label` (spec requirement)

### Highlight
- **Standalone function contract:** `highlight_chunks(props, locale)` is the spec-defined entry point
- **No `id` field:** chunks are sequential output, not a single DOM node
- **Parametric anatomy:** chunk attributes depend on `highlighted` boolean (not in `Part` enum)
- **ICU4X-gated:** module lives under `feature = "i18n"`
- **Case folding:** per Unicode TR21 (fold, not transform) — handles Turkic, German, Greek, Lithuanian specially
- **Overlap/adjacency merging in core:** adapters always receive contiguous chunks
- **BiDi-aware:** `dir="auto"` on root for correct paragraph direction detection

---

## Adapter Wiring Checklist

1. **Heading:**
   - Construct `Api::new(props, context)` with resolved heading level
   - Call `api.root_attrs(is_native_heading_element)` for native `<h1>`-`<h6>` or fallback `<div>`
   - Render element at `api.resolved_level()` (1-6)

2. **Landmark:**
   - Construct `Api::new(props, env, messages)` with localized messages
   - Choose element based on `role` (native semantic or fallback)
   - Call `api.root_attrs(is_native_landmark_element)` to apply attributes
   - Handle `prefers_generic_fallback_element()` for `Role::Search`

3. **Highlight:**
   - Construct `Api::new(props)`
   - Call `api.root_attrs()` on root `<span>`
   - Iterate `api.chunks(locale)` and render each chunk as `<mark>` (if `highlighted`) or `<span>` (if not)
   - Spread `api.chunk_attrs(chunk.highlighted)` onto each chunk element

## Summary Report: Leptos Adapter Component Patterns for ars-ui

Based on my thorough exploration of the `ars-ui` workspace, here are the comprehensive patterns for implementing Leptos adapter components:

### **1. Directory Structure**

```
/crates/ars-leptos/src/
  ├── lib.rs                 # Main adapter facade, re-exports
  ├── prelude.rs             # User-facing re-exports only
  ├── use_machine.rs         # Core hook (use_machine, UseMachineReturn)
  ├── attrs.rs               # AttrMap → Leptos attribute conversion
  ├── callbacks.rs            # Event callback utilities (emit, emit_map)
  ├── controlled.rs           # Controlled prop synchronization
  ├── id.rs                  # Hydration-safe ID generation
  ├── as_child.rs            # AsChild pattern for attribute forwarding
  ├── provider.rs            # ArsProvider context setup
  ├── prelude.rs             # Public re-exports
  ├── utility/               # Utility components (stateless)
  │   ├── mod.rs
  │   ├── button.rs          # Interactive button with machine
  │   ├── separator.rs       # Simple prop-only (no machine)
  │   ├── visually_hidden.rs # Simple prop-only (no machine)
  │   ├── dismissable.rs     # Complex stateful
  │   └── error_boundary.rs  # Leptos-specific error boundary
  └── navigation/
      └── tabs.rs            # Complex stateful

/crates/ars-leptos/tests/
  ├── separator.rs           # SSR tests (no wasm)
  ├── visually_hidden.rs     # SSR tests (no wasm)
  ├── separator_wasm.rs      # Browser tests

/crates/ars-test-harness-leptos/src/
  └── lib.rs                 # Test harness backend (LeptosHarnessBackend, render())
```

---

### **2. Simple Utility Component Pattern (No State Machine)**

Used for **stateless** utility adapters like `Separator` and `VisuallyHidden`.

**File: `src/utility/separator.rs`**

```rust
//! Leptos Separator adapter.
//!
//! Renders the framework-agnostic `Separator` root attributes onto either an
//! adapter-owned `<hr>` node or a consumer-owned root through [`SeparatorAsChild`].

pub use ars_components::utility::separator::{Api, Part, Props};
use ars_core::HtmlAttr;
pub use ars_i18n::Orientation;
use leptos::{children::TypedChildren, prelude::*, tachys::view::add_attr::AddAnyAttr};

use crate::{as_child::AsChildAttrs, attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs};

// Step 1: Compute root attributes from props
fn root_attrs(
    id: Option<String>,
    orientation: Orientation,
    decorative: bool,
) -> Vec<crate::LeptosAttribute> {
    let mut props = Props::new().orientation(orientation).decorative(decorative);

    if let Some(id) = id.clone() {
        props = props.id(id);
    }

    let mut attrs = Api::new(props).root_attrs();

    if let Some(id) = id {
        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, id);
    }

    attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(attrs)  // Convert to Leptos attrs
}

// Step 2: Adapter-owned root component
#[component]
pub fn Separator(
    /// Optional component instance ID.
    #[prop(optional, into)]
    id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,

    /// Separator orientation.
    #[prop(optional)]
    orientation: Orientation,

    /// Whether the separator is decorative and hidden from the accessibility tree.
    #[prop(optional)]
    decorative: bool,
) -> impl IntoView {
    let id = id.map(Oco::into_owned);
    let attrs = root_attrs(id, orientation, decorative);

    view! { <hr {..attrs} /> }
}

// Step 3: AsChild variant (forwards attrs to single child root)
#[component]
pub fn SeparatorAsChild<T>(
    #[prop(optional, into)]
    id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,

    #[prop(optional)]
    orientation: Orientation,

    #[prop(optional)]
    decorative: bool,

    /// Child root that receives the separator root attrs.
    children: TypedChildren<T>,
) -> impl IntoView
where
    View<T>: AddAnyAttr,
    <View<T> as AddAnyAttr>::Output<Vec<crate::LeptosAttribute>>: IntoView,
{
    let id = id.map(Oco::into_owned);

    children.into_inner()()
        .add_any_attr(AsChildAttrs::from(root_attrs(id, orientation, decorative)).into_inner())
}
```

**Key patterns:**
- Use `attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs()` (not `attr_map_to_leptos()`) for stateless utilities
- Two component variants: adapter-owned root + `AsChild` variant
- Prop conversion → `Api::new()` → `.root_attrs()` → conversion to Leptos attrs
- No `use_machine`, no context, no event handlers

---

### **3. Attribute Conversion & Spreading**

**Helper: `attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs()`**

Converts `AttrMap` (from `Api::root_attrs()`) to `Vec<LeptosAttribute>` for spreading with `{..attrs}`:

```rust
// From attrs.rs
pub fn attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(map: AttrMap) -> Vec<LeptosAttribute> {
    let strategy = use_style_strategy();  // Read from ArsProvider context
    let result = attr_map_to_leptos(map, &strategy, Some("element-id"));
    result.attrs
}
```

**For strategy-aware conversions (with CSSOM/Nonce styles):**

```rust
let strategy = use_style_strategy();
let result = attr_map_to_leptos(api.root_attrs(), &strategy, Some("element-id"));

// Use result.attrs to spread
// Handle result.cssom_styles or result.nonce_css as needed
```

---

### **4. Re-Export Pattern**

**File: `src/lib.rs`**

```rust
pub mod utility;
pub use utility::{separator, visually_hidden, button, dismissable, client_only};
pub use attrs::{attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs, LeptosAttrResult};
pub use use_machine::{UseMachineReturn, use_machine};
// ... (other public items)
```

**File: `src/prelude.rs`** (end-user facing only)

```rust
// Module re-exports (users reach via module qualifier)
pub use crate::utility::{separator, visually_hidden};

// NOT in prelude: adapter internals like use_machine, EphemeralRef, attr_map_to_leptos
// Those are public via crate::use_machine but not re-exported in prelude
```

### **5. SSR Testing Pattern**

**File: `tests/separator.rs`**

```rust
//! SSR tests for the Leptos Separator adapter.

#![cfg(all(not(target_arch = "wasm32"), feature = "ssr"))]

use ars_i18n::Orientation;
use ars_leptos::utility::separator::{Separator, SeparatorAsChild};
use leptos::prelude::*;

#[test]
fn separator_renders_horizontal_semantic_root() {
    let html = view! { <Separator id="sep-horizontal" /> }.to_html();

    // Assert HTML structure and key attributes
    assert!(html.trim_start().starts_with("<hr"));
    for fragment in [
        r#"id="sep-horizontal""#,
        r#"data-ars-scope="separator""#,
        r#"data-ars-part="root""#,
        r#"role="separator""#,
        r#"aria-orientation="horizontal""#,
    ] {
        assert!(html.contains(fragment), "missing {fragment}: {html}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn separator_as_child_forwards_attrs_without_wrapper() {
    let html = view! {
        <SeparatorAsChild id="sep-menu" orientation=Orientation::Vertical>
            <div class="menu-separator"></div>
        </SeparatorAsChild>
    }
    .to_html();

    // Verify child root is not wrapped
    assert!(html.trim_start().starts_with("<div"));
    assert!(!html.contains("<hr"), "unexpected wrapper hr: {html}");
}
```

**Key testing strategy:**
- Run SSR `.to_html()` tests (no wasm needed)
- Verify component renders correct HTML element
- Check all ARIA attributes, data-* attributes are present
- Test both adapter-owned and AsChild variants
- Verify no unintended wrappers

**File: `crates/ars-test-harness-leptos/src/lib.rs`**

For more complex tests requiring browser interaction or state changes:

```rust
use ars_test_harness_leptos::{LeptosHarnessComponent, render, mount_with_locale};

struct MyFixture;

impl LeptosHarnessComponent for MyFixture {
    type Machine = my_machine::Machine;
    
    fn mount(self, container: web_sys::HtmlElement) -> MountedLeptosHarness<Self::Machine> {
        // Mount fixture and return (service, rerender closure, mount state)
        let service = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Service::new(props, &env, &messages)));
        let version = RwSignal::new(0);
        let mount_handle = mount_to(container, move || {
            view! { <MyComponent service=Arc::clone(&service) version /> }
        });
        MountedLeptosHarness::new(
            service,
            move || version.update(|v| *v += 1),
            mount_handle,
        )
    }
    
    fn mount_with_locale(self, container: web_sys::HtmlElement, locale: Locale) -> MountedLeptosHarness<Self::Machine> {
        // Same as mount but with ArsProvider locale wrapper
    }
}

#[wasm_bindgen_test]
async fn test_behavior() {
    let harness = render(MyFixture).await;
    harness.send(MyEvent::Toggle).await;
    assert_eq!(harness.state(), "Open");
}
```

**Harness test utilities:**
- `render()` — mount fixture into isolated container
- `mount_with_locale()` — wrap with ArsProvider
- `.send()` — send event to machine
- `.query()` / `.query_selector()` — DOM queries
- `.advance_time()` — drive fake timers
- `.flush()` — await reactivity

### **7. Use Machine Hook Overview** (for stateful components)

**Core pattern (used in button, dialog, etc.):**

```rust
let machine = use_machine::<MyMachine>(props);
let UseMachineReturn { state, send, service, context_version } = machine;

// For reactive attributes:
let data_state = machine.derive(|api| api.data_state().to_string());

// For callbacks:
send.run(MyEvent::Toggle);
```

**With reactive props:**
```rust
let machine = use_machine_with_reactive_props::<MyMachine>(props_signal);
```

**API access patterns:**
- `machine.derive(|api| ...)` — reactive memo of derived values
- `machine.with_api_snapshot(|api| ...)` — one-shot read (no reactivity)
- `machine.with_api_ephemeral(|api_ref| ...)` — ephemeral read in event handlers

### **8. Heading, Landmark, Highlight Specifications**

All three target **stateless** utility components (no state machine):

#### **Heading**
- **Props:** `id`, `level: Option<Level>`
- **Context:** `HeadingContext { level }` (incremented by `Section`)
- **Api:** `resolved_level()`, `root_attrs(is_native_heading_element)`
- **Adapter:** Render `<h1>`-`<h6>` based on resolved level
- **Anatomy:** `<h1>`-`<h6>` root only, no child parts

#### **Landmark**
- **Props:** `id`, `role: Role`, `labelledby_id: Option<String>`
- **Messages:** `label()` message function
- **Api:** `root_attrs(is_native_landmark_element)`, `has_accessible_name()`, `missing_accessible_name_warning_needed()`
- **Adapter:** Render semantic `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<aside>`, `<footer>`, or `<div role="...">` 
- **Anatomy:** Single root element, no child parts

#### **Highlight**
- **Props:** `query: Vec<String>`, `text: String`, `ignore_case`, `match_strategy: MatchStrategy`
- **No machine, no context**
- **Api:** `root_attrs()`, `chunk_attrs(highlighted)`, `chunks(locale)`
- **Free function:** `highlight_chunks(props, locale) → Vec<HighlightChunk>`
- **Adapter:** Render `<span>` root + per-chunk `<mark>` (highlighted) or `<span>` (not)
- **Anatomy:** Root + dynamic chunk elements

---

### **9. Key Takeaways for Implementation**

1. **Stateless utilities use helper function pattern:**
   - Extract prop fields → `Api::new()` → `.root_attrs()` → `attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs()` → spread

2. **Two component variants always:**
   - Adapter-owned root (e.g., `<hr>`, `<span>`, `<h1>`)
   - `AsChild` variant (forwards attrs to single child)

3. **Re-export in `lib.rs` + `prelude.rs`:**
   - User-facing `prelude` only exports component modules and config types
   - Implementation details (use_machine, attrs, etc.) public but not in prelude

4. **Testing:**
   - SSR `.to_html()` tests for structure and attributes
   - Optional wasm tests for browser interaction (button clicks, state changes)
   - Use `ars_test_harness_leptos::render()` for fixtures with machines

5. **Accessibility:**
   - Check spec for required ARIA roles, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, data attributes
   - Native semantic HTML elements (h1-h6, nav, main, header) suppress redundant `role` attr
   - Fallback elements (div, span) must include explicit `role` and aria attributes

6. **No stateful complexity needed:**
   - `Heading`: context-only (provided by `HeadingLevelProvider`)
   - `Landmark`: prop + env-provided messages
   - `Highlight`: pure props → free function computation

---

### **10. Spec Foundation References**

- **§3 use_machine Hook:** Reactive machine creation, derive() pattern, context_version tracking
- **§3.1 EphemeralRef:** Prevents storing borrowed Api references in signals
- **§3.2 Component IDs & Hydration:** use_id() for deterministic IDs, hydration-safe
- **§4 AttrMap → Leptos Attributes:** attr_map_to_leptos(), strategy-aware style handling
- **§5 Standard Component Pattern:** Root component + child parts + context passing
- **§6 Slots Pattern:** Named `#[slot]` attribute for compound layouts
- **§7 SSR:** Effects gated behind `#[cfg(not(feature = "ssr"))]`, hydration handling
- **§8 API Naming:** `is_*()` for booleans, `value()` / `selected_items()` for others
- **§9 Callback Naming:** `on_<property>_change` for values, `on_<action>` for discrete events

This pattern ensures consistency across all Leptos adapters and full SSR/hydration support.

## 2. MINIMAL UTILITY ADAPTER PATTERN (Separator Example)

This is the **canonical pattern for stateless utility adapters**. The Separator adapter takes zero-state props and renders attributes from the framework-agnostic API.

### File: `crates/ars-dioxus/src/utility/separator.rs`

```rust
//! Dioxus Separator adapter.

pub use ars_components::utility::separator::{Api, Part, Props};
use ars_core::HtmlAttr;
pub use ars_i18n::Orientation;
use dioxus::prelude::*;

use crate::{as_child::AsChildRenderProps, attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs};

// Step 1: Helper function that builds root attrs from props using the core API
fn root_attrs(id: Option<&str>, orientation: Orientation, decorative: bool) -> Vec<Attribute> {
    let mut props = Props::new().orientation(orientation).decorative(decorative);

    if let Some(id) = id {
        props = props.id(id);
    }

    let mut attrs = Api::new(props).root_attrs();

    if let Some(id) = id {
        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, id);
    }

    attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(attrs)
}

// Step 2: Props struct — ALWAYS explicit #[derive(Props)]
#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct SeparatorProps {
    /// Optional component instance ID.
    #[props(optional, into)]
    pub id: Option<String>,

    /// Separator orientation.
    #[props(default = Orientation::Horizontal)]
    pub orientation: Orientation,

    /// Whether the separator is decorative and hidden from the accessibility tree.
    #[props(default = false)]
    pub decorative: bool,
}

// Step 3: AsChild variant Props
#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct SeparatorAsChildProps {
    /// Optional component instance ID.
    #[props(optional, into)]
    pub id: Option<String>,

    /// Separator orientation.
    #[props(default = Orientation::Horizontal)]
    pub orientation: Orientation,

    /// Whether the separator is decorative and hidden from the accessibility tree.
    #[props(default = false)]
    pub decorative: bool,

    /// Render callback that owns the child root and spreads `Separator` attrs.
    pub render: Callback<AsChildRenderProps, Element>,
}

// Step 4: Adapter-owned root component
#[component]
pub fn Separator(props: SeparatorProps) -> Element {
    let attrs = root_attrs(props.id.as_deref(), props.orientation, props.decorative);

    rsx! {
        hr { ..attrs }
    }
}

// Step 5: As-child variant component
#[component]
pub fn SeparatorAsChild(props: SeparatorAsChildProps) -> Element {
    let attrs = root_attrs(props.id.as_deref(), props.orientation, props.decorative);

    props.render.call(AsChildRenderProps { attrs })
}
```

**Key Points:**
1. **Props are always explicit**: `#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]` — never use bare function parameters
2. **Two variants**: one adapter-owned root (e.g., `<hr>`), one `AsChild` for consumer-provided roots
3. **`root_attrs` helper**: encapsulates the pattern of `Props::new()` → `Api::new()` → `root_attrs()`
4. **`attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs()`**: converts core `AttrMap` to Dioxus `Vec<Attribute>`
5. **ID passthrough**: optional user-provided ID is set on the HTML element

---

## 3. VISUALLY_HIDDEN PATTERN: Complex AsChild with Class Merging

VisuallyHidden is more complex because the AsChild variant must merge the hidden class with child-provided classes without duplicating them.

### Key differences from Separator:

1. **Template cache** for efficient class merging during SSR:
```rust
static TEMPLATE_CACHE: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<TemplateKey, Template>>> =
    LazyLock::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
```

2. **AsChild implementation handles class merging**:
```rust
#[component]
pub fn VisuallyHiddenAsChild(props: VisuallyHiddenAsChildProps) -> Element {
    let mut attrs = root_attrs(props.id.as_deref(), props.is_focusable, true);
    let hidden_class = (!props.is_focusable)
        .then(|| take_attr(&mut attrs, "class"))
        .flatten();

    props
        .render
        .call(AsChildRenderProps { attrs })
        .map(|vnode| merge_root_attrs(vnode, hidden_class))
}
```

3. **The `merge_root_attrs()` function** modifies the returned VNode's template to inject the hidden class into static class attributes when possible.

**This pattern is used when:**
- The adapter must inject its own CSS classes
- The consumer's root may also have classes
- You need efficient SSR without duplicate `class=` attributes

---

## 4. BUTTON ADAPTER PATTERN: Stateful Component with Machine

The Button adapter is more complex because it uses the state machine pattern. Here's the architecture:

### File: `crates/ars-dioxus/src/utility/button.rs` (excerpt)

```rust
use ars_components::utility::button::{self, Api};
pub use ars_components::utility::button::{FormEncType, FormMethod, FormTarget, Messages, Size, Type, Variant};
use dioxus::prelude::*;
use crate::{as_child::AsChildRenderProps, attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs, use_machine, use_stable_id};

#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct ButtonProps {
    /// Optional component instance ID. When absent, the adapter generates one.
    #[props(optional, into)]
    pub id: Option<String>,

    /// Whether the button is disabled.
    #[props(default = false)]
    pub disabled: bool,

    /// Whether the button is in loading state.
    #[props(default = false)]
    pub loading: bool,

    /// Visual style variant.
    #[props(optional, into)]
    pub variant: Option<Variant>,

    /// Visual size token.
    #[props(optional, into)]
    pub size: Option<Size>,
    
    // ... more props ...
}

#[component]
pub fn Button(props: ButtonProps) -> Element {
    // 1. Build core Props from Dioxus Props
    let core_props = build_core_props(&props);
    
    // 2. Use the machine hook — this is the KEY difference from stateless adapters
    let machine = use_machine::<button::Machine>(core_props);
    
    // 3. Derive attributes reactively from the machine API
    let root_attrs = machine.derive(move |api| {
        attr_map_to_dioxus(api.root_attrs(), &strategy, Some("button-root"))
    });
    
    // 4. Render with machine state
    rsx! {
        button {
            ..root_attrs.read().attrs,
            // ... event handlers ...
        }
    }
}
```

**Key Points for Stateful Adapters:**
1. **`use_machine::<ComponentMachine>(props)`** — creates the state machine with Dioxus reactivity
2. **`machine.derive(|api| ...)`** — creates a reactive memo that updates when machine state changes
3. **Split re-render signals** — only the derived values you read trigger re-renders
4. The machine handles `use_sync_props` internally, so props are synced automatically

---

## 5. THE `use_machine` HOOK — CORE PATTERN

From `spec/foundation/09-adapter-dioxus.md` §2, the `use_machine` hook is the bridge between the core state machine and Dioxus reactivity:

```rust
pub struct UseMachineReturn<M: Machine + 'static> {
    /// Read-only projection of the machine state
    pub state: ReadSignal<M::State>,
    
    /// Send an event — non-reactive, safe to call from handlers
    pub send: Callback<M::Event>,
    
    /// Access the underlying service for context/props reads and derive()
    pub service: Signal<Service<M>>,
    
    /// Monotonically increasing counter for context invalidation tracking
    pub context_version: ReadSignal<u64>,
}

impl<M: Machine> UseMachineReturn<M> {
    /// Create a fine-grained memo that re-computes only when state changes
    pub fn derive<T: Clone + PartialEq + 'static>(
        &self,
        f: impl Fn(&M::Api<'_>) -> T + 'static,
    ) -> Memo<T> {
        // ... creates a memo that tracks both state and context_version ...
    }
    
    /// One-shot, non-reactive read of the API
    pub fn with_api_snapshot<T>(&self, f: impl Fn(&M::Api<'_>) -> T) -> T {
        // ... uses try_write() to avoid deadlocks ...
    }
}
```

**Usage Pattern:**
```rust
let machine = use_machine::<checkbox::Machine>(core_props);

// Reactive: re-computes and triggers re-render only when value changes
let is_checked = machine.derive(|api| api.is_checked());

// One-shot: reads current state without tracking dependency
let current_state = machine.with_api_snapshot(|api| api.state().clone());
```

**Key Safety Points:**
- `derive()` holds a **read lock** on `service` — never call `send()` inside a derive closure
- `with_api_snapshot()` can deadlock if called while `derive()` is evaluating
- `use_sync_props` runs **inside `use_machine`** before returning, so props are synced automatically

---

## 6. ATTRIBUTE CONVERSION: `attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs`

The core `AttrMap` from the state machine must be converted to Dioxus `Vec<Attribute>`:

**From `spec/foundation/09-adapter-dioxus.md` §3:**

```rust
/// Convert an `AttrMap` into Dioxus attributes using the given `StyleStrategy`.
pub fn attr_map_to_dioxus(
    map: AttrMap,
    strategy: &StyleStrategy,
    element_id: Option<&str>,
) -> DioxusAttrResult {
    let AttrMapParts { attrs, styles } = map.into_parts();

    let mut result: Vec<Attribute> = attrs.into_iter()
        .filter_map(|(key, val)| match val {
            AttrValue::String(s) => Some(Attribute::new(
                intern_attr_name(&key), 
                AttributeValue::Text(s), 
                None, 
                false
            )),
            AttrValue::Bool(true) => Some(Attribute::new(
                intern_attr_name(&key), 
                AttributeValue::Text("".into()), 
                None, 
                false
            )),
            AttrValue::Bool(false) | AttrValue::None => None,
        })
        .collect();

    // Handle styles according to strategy: Inline, Cssom, or Nonce
    match strategy {
        StyleStrategy::Inline => {
            // Concatenate styles into a style=" " attribute
        }
        StyleStrategy::Cssom => {
            // Return styles separately for CSSOM application
        }
        StyleStrategy::Nonce(_) => {
            // Inject styles into a nonce-tagged <style> tag
        }
    }

    DioxusAttrResult { attrs: result, cssom_styles, nonce_css_key, nonce_css }
}

/// Shorthand for inline-only attributes (no style handling needed)
pub fn attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(attrs: AttrMap) -> Vec<Attribute> {
    let result = attr_map_to_dioxus(attrs, &StyleStrategy::Inline, None);
    result.attrs
}
```

**Attribute Interning:**
- Dioxus requires attribute names to be `&'static str`
- Common names (`id`, `role`, `aria-*`, `data-ars-*`) are compile-time constants
- Unknown `data-*` names are interned into a thread-safe pool on first use

---

## 7. RE-EXPORT PATTERN: lib.rs and prelude.rs

### In `lib.rs`:
```rust
pub mod utility;
pub use utility::{button, separator, visually_hidden, dismissable, ...};
```

### In `prelude.rs`:
```rust
// Re-export component modules so end users can write:
// `use ars_dioxus::prelude::*; separator::Props, button::Machine`
pub use crate::utility::{
    self, button, client_only, dismissable, error_boundary, separator, 
    visually_hidden, z_index_allocator,
};
```

**Convention:**
- End users reach component types via module qualifiers: `separator::Props`, `button::Variant`
- NEVER flatten into aliases like `SeparatorProps` in the prelude
- The prelude re-exports only **module paths**, not individual types

## 8. COMPLETE SSR TEST EXAMPLE (Separator)

**File: `crates/ars-dioxus/tests/separator.rs`**

```rust
//! SSR tests for the Dioxus Separator adapter.

#![cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]

use ars_dioxus::{
    prelude::Orientation,
    utility::separator::{Separator, SeparatorAsChild},
};
use dioxus::prelude::*;

fn render_app(app: fn() -> Element) -> String {
    let mut vdom = VirtualDom::new(app);
    vdom.rebuild_in_place();
    dioxus_ssr::render(&vdom)
}

#[test]
fn separator_renders_horizontal_semantic_root() {
    fn app() -> Element {
        rsx! {
            Separator { id: "sep-horizontal" }
        }
    }

    let html = render_app(app);

    assert!(
        html.trim_start().starts_with("<hr"),
        "default separator should render an hr root: {html}"
    );

    for fragment in [
        r#"id="sep-horizontal""#,
        r#"data-ars-scope="separator""#,
        r#"data-ars-part="root""#,
        r#"role="separator""#,
        r#"aria-orientation="horizontal""#,
        r#"data-ars-orientation="horizontal""#,
    ] {
        assert!(html.contains(fragment), "missing {fragment}: {html}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn separator_as_child_forwards_attrs_without_wrapper() {
    fn app() -> Element {
        rsx! {
            SeparatorAsChild {
                id: "sep-menu",
                orientation: Orientation::Vertical,
                render: |slot: ars_dioxus::as_child::AsChildRenderProps| rsx! {
                    div { class: "menu-separator", ..slot.attrs }
                },
            }
        }
    }

    let html = render_app(app);

    assert!(
        html.trim_start().starts_with("<div"),
        "as-child should render the callback root directly: {html}"
    );

    for fragment in [
        r#"id="sep-menu""#,
        r#"class="menu-separator""#,
        r#"data-ars-scope="separator""#,
        r#"role="separator""#,
        r#"aria-orientation="vertical""#,
    ] {
        assert!(html.contains(fragment), "missing {fragment}: {html}");
    }

    assert!(!html.contains("<hr"), "unexpected wrapper hr: {html}");
}

#[test]
fn separator_renders_decorative_role_without_orientation_attrs() {
    fn app() -> Element {
        rsx! {
            Separator { id: "sep-decorative", decorative: true }
        }
    }

    let html = render_app(app);

    for fragment in [
        r#"id="sep-decorative""#,
        r#"data-ars-scope="separator""#,
        r#"role="none""#,
    ] {
        assert!(html.contains(fragment), "missing {fragment}: {html}");
    }

    assert!(
        !html.contains("aria-orientation"),
        "decorative separator should omit aria-orientation: {html}"
    );
}
```

**Test Pattern:**
1. Create a **one-off render helper**: `render_app(fn() -> Element) -> String` — uses `VirtualDom::new()` + `rebuild_in_place()` + `dioxus_ssr::render()`
2. Test **both variants**: adapter-owned root and `AsChild`
3. Assert **HTML string fragments**: check for expected attributes, roles, classes, etc.
4. Verify **no wrapper nodes** in AsChild mode
5. Use **#![cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]** — SSR tests only run on non-WASM

## 9. BUTTON TEST EXAMPLE: Stateful Component

**File: `crates/ars-dioxus/tests/button.rs` (excerpt)**

```rust
#[test]
fn button_renders_default_root_and_content_attrs() {
    fn app() -> Element {
        rsx! {
            Button { id: "primary-action", variant: button::Variant::Primary, "Save" }
        }
    }

    let html = render_app(app);

    assert!(html.contains("<button"), "missing button root: {html}");
    assert!(html.contains(r#"id="primary-action""#), "missing explicit id: {html}");
    assert!(html.contains(r#"data-ars-scope="button""#), "missing button scope: {html}");
    assert!(html.contains(r#"data-ars-part="root""#), "missing root part: {html}");
    assert!(html.contains(r#"type="button""#), "missing native button type: {html}");
    assert!(html.contains(r#"data-ars-variant="primary""#), "missing typed variant token: {html}");
    assert!(html.contains(r#"data-ars-size="md""#), "missing default size token: {html}");
    assert!(html.contains(r#"data-ars-part="content""#), "missing content part wrapper: {html}");
}

#[test]
fn button_renders_loading_indicator_and_busy_attrs() {
    fn app() -> Element {
        rsx! {
            Button { id: "loading-action", loading: true, "Save" }
        }
    }

    let html = render_app(app);

    for fragment in [
        r#"aria-busy="true""#,
        r#"aria-disabled="true""#,
        r#"data-ars-part="loading-indicator""#,
        r#"role="status""#,
        r#"aria-live="polite""#,
        r#"aria-label="Loading""#,
        r#"data-ars-loading="true""#,
    ] {
        assert!(html.contains(fragment), "missing {fragment}: {html}");
    }
}
```

**Stateful Test Pattern:**
1. Props are passed directly to the component
2. Machine processes them in `use_machine`
3. All ARIA attributes and data attributes are rendered based on machine state
4. Test asserts both **adapter-internal state** (e.g., loading indicator) and **ARIA semantics**

## 10. SPEC FOUNDATION: Canonical Requirements

From `spec/foundation/09-adapter-dioxus.md`:

### §1.2 Design Principles:
1. **Minimize re-renders** via fine-grained `Signal` splitting
2. **Component re-runs are OK** because VDOM diffing makes them cheap
3. **Copy-able context** via `Signal` (which is `Copy + Clone`)
4. **Multi-platform** via `DioxusPlatform` abstraction

### §2.3 Reactive Props Sync:
- **All prop syncing is `use_sync_props`** — single unified function, not ad-hoc logic
- **Must run before any `derive()` calls** — otherwise deadlock (read lock held)
- `use_machine` calls it internally, so components are safe by construction

### §4 Standard Component Pattern:
- **ALWAYS explicit Props structs** with `#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]`
- Never use bare function parameters for components that accept props
- Zero-prop parts MAY use bare functions (e.g., `fn Backdrop() -> Element`)

### §15 SSR Support:
- All tests run in `#![cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` mode (SSR)
- WASM tests use suffix `_wasm.rs` and run with `wasm-bindgen-test`
- Effects (timers, DOM mutations) are gated behind `#[cfg(not(feature = "ssr"))]`

### §17 Testing:
- **SSR test harness**: `VirtualDom::new()` + `rebuild_in_place()` + `dioxus_ssr::render()`
- **WASM test harness**: Uses `DioxusHarnessBackend` and `DioxusHarnessComponent` trait
- Assert HTML string fragments, not parsed DOM trees

---

## 11. `as_child` PATTERN: Key Implementation Detail

The `as_child` pattern allows consumers to own the root element while the adapter provides attributes:

```rust
/// Props for the consumer to provide to an AsChild variant
#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct SeparatorAsChildProps {
    #[props(optional, into)]
    pub id: Option<String>,
    
    pub orientation: Orientation,
    
    pub decorative: bool,
    
    // THIS is the key: a render callback
    pub render: Callback<AsChildRenderProps, Element>,
}

#[component]
pub fn SeparatorAsChild(props: SeparatorAsChildProps) -> Element {
    let attrs = root_attrs(...);
    
    // Call the consumer's render function with attrs to spread
    props.render.call(AsChildRenderProps { attrs })
}

// Consumer usage:
rsx! {
    SeparatorAsChild {
        id: "sep",
        render: |slot| rsx! {
            // Consumer owns this root and spreads attrs onto it
            div { ..slot.attrs, "Custom separator" }
        },
    }
}
```

**Benefits:**
- No wrapper node in the DOM
- Consumer has full control over the root element
- Adapter still provides all semantic attributes via the callback

## 12. IMPLEMENTATION CHECKLIST FOR NEW ADAPTERS (Heading, Landmark, Highlight)

When implementing a new utility adapter component:

**File Structure:**
- Create `/crates/ars-dioxus/src/utility/{component_name}.rs`
- Add to `/crates/ars-dioxus/src/utility/mod.rs`
- Create `/crates/ars-dioxus/tests/{component_name}.rs` for SSR tests
- Optional: `/crates/ars-dioxus/tests/{component_name}_wasm.rs` for browser tests

**Component Code:**
1. Import from `ars_components::utility::{component}::{Api, Part, Props}`
2. Write a `root_attrs()` helper function
3. Define explicit `Props` structs (with `Clone, PartialEq, Debug`)
4. Define explicit `AsChildProps` structs (with callback)
5. Implement `#[component] fn ComponentName(props: ComponentProps) -> Element`
6. Implement `#[component] fn ComponentAsChild(props: ComponentAsChildProps) -> Element`
7. Use `attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs()` to convert core attrs to Dioxus
8. Spread attrs with `..attrs` syntax in RSX

**For Stateful Components (using machines):**
1. Call `use_machine::<ComponentMachine>(core_props)`
2. Use `machine.derive(|api| ...)` for reactive attributes
3. Wire event handlers to `machine.send` callback
4. Create context struct with `state`, `send`, `service`, `context_version`
5. Use `use_context_provider()` to share context with child parts

**Tests:**
1. Create SSR test file with `#![cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]`
2. Test both main component and `AsChild` variant
3. Test default props and prop variations
4. Assert HTML string fragments containing expected attributes
5. Use pattern: `render_app(fn() -> Element) -> String`

**Re-exports:**
1. Add to `utility/mod.rs`: `pub mod component_name;`
2. Add to `prelude.rs` module list: `pub use crate::utility::component_name;`
3. Document in lib.rs docstring (if top-level)

---

## 13. CRITICAL SAFETY NOTES

### Deadlock Prevention:
- `derive()` holds a **read lock** — never call `send()` inside
- `with_api_snapshot()` can deadlock if called while `derive()` is running
- `use_sync_props` runs BEFORE `derive()` in `use_machine` — safe by construction

### Signal Batching:
- Dioxus batches signal writes during component body execution
- No re-render occurs until the component function returns
- If batching changes in future Dioxus versions, `use_sync_props` must migrate to `use_effect`

### SSR Safety:
- Effects are gated with `#[cfg(not(feature = "ssr"))]`
- DOM APIs (`web_sys`) must not appear in SSR code paths
- All ARIA attributes are computed by `connect()` regardless of platform

### Copy-ability:
- `UseMachineReturn` is `Copy` because all fields are `Copy` in Dioxus
- Context can be passed around without `clone()` overhead
- Never store `Api<'a>` in signals — use `EphemeralRef` to prevent it

144	
145	Leptos may select the semantic tag dynamically or use a fallback generic node with heading role. When heading text can mix document directions, the rendered heading node should set `dir="auto"` so the browser resolves reading order from the content instead of inheriting a misleading page-level direction. Heading level providers and `Section` helpers must publish the incremented `HeadingContext` with `provide_context(...)` rather than relying on prop drilling.

9	# Landmark — Leptos Adapter
10	
11	## 1. Purpose and Adapter Scope
12	
13	This spec maps the core [`Landmark`](../../components/utility/landmark.md) utility to Leptos 0.8.x.
14	
15	## 2. Public Adapter API
16	
17	```rust,no_check
18	#[component] pub fn Landmark(...) -> impl IntoView
19	```
20	
21	## 3. Mapping to Core Component Contract
22	
23	- Props parity: full parity.
24	- Structure parity: single root node with semantic element choice or fallback role.
25	
26	## 4. Part Mapping
27	
28	| Core part / structure | Required? | Adapter rendering target                      | Ownership     | Attr source        | Notes                                                 |
29	| --------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
30	| `Root`                | required  | semantic landmark element or fallback `<div>` | adapter-owned | `api.root_attrs()` | Element selection depends on role and fallback rules. |
31	
32	## 5. Attr Merge and Ownership Rules
33	
34	| Target node   | Core attrs                       | Adapter-owned attrs                                     | Consumer attrs      | Merge order                                                                           | Ownership notes    |
35	| ------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
36	| landmark root | landmark attrs from the core API | fallback role attrs when no native landmark tag is used | consumer root attrs | core semantic element choice and labeling attrs win; `class`/`style` merge additively | adapter-owned root |
37	
38	## 6. Composition / Context Contract
39	
40	No context contract.
41	
42	## 7. Prop Sync and Event Mapping
43	
44	Landmark semantics are render-time concerns.
45	
46	| Adapter prop                | Mode                      | Sync trigger     | Machine event / update path | Visible effect                                   | Notes                       |
47	| --------------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
48	| landmark type / label props | non-reactive adapter prop | render time only | root attr derivation        | determines semantic element or role and labeling | no post-mount sync expected |
49	
50	## 8. Registration and Cleanup Contract
51	
52	- No registration lifecycle exists beyond normal node disposal.
53	
54	## 9. Ref and Node Contract
55	
56	| Target part / node                         | Ref required?                                                                          | Ref owner                                             | Node availability                  | Composition rule                                                 | Notes                                                                              |
57	| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
58	| primary rendered node or provider boundary | no when the component is purely structural or provider-only; otherwise adapter-defined | adapter-owned unless part mapping says consumer-owned | always structural, handle optional | composed only when a consumer-owned node receives the core attrs | Use a live node handle only when the component's interaction contract requires it. |
59	
60	## 10. State Machine Boundary Rules
61	
62	- machine-owned state: all core interaction, accessibility, and controlled-state values defined by the component machine or derived API.
63	- adapter-local derived bookkeeping: minimal ephemeral data such as pointer modality, mount status, or observer handles when the core machine does not model them directly.
64	- forbidden local mirrors: do not fork controlled props, accessibility attrs, or machine-visible state into an unsynchronized local source of truth.
65	- allowed snapshot-read contexts: render-time derivation, event handlers, effects, and cleanup only when reading snapshots does not bypass required machine events.
66	
67	## 11. Callback Payload Contract
68	
69	| Callback                                                               | Payload source | Payload shape | Timing         | Cancelable? | Notes                                                                                                                 |
70	| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------- | -------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
71	| no public adapter-specific callback beyond normalized component events | none           | none          | not applicable | no          | When wrappers expose callbacks, they must preserve the normalized timing documented in `Prop Sync and Event Mapping`. |
72	
73	## 12. Failure and Degradation Rules
74	
75	| Condition                                                                  | Policy             | Notes                                                                             |
76	| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
77	| unsupported platform capability or missing browser-only API during SSR     | degrade gracefully | Render structural output and defer behavior until client-only APIs are available. |
78	| impossible prop combinations not explicitly supported by the core contract | fail fast          | Prefer an explicit contract violation over silently inventing behavior.           |
79	
80	## 13. Identity and Key Policy
81	
82	| Registered or repeated structure   | Identity source | Duplicates allowed? | DOM order must match registration order? | SSR/hydration stability                                                  | Notes                                                                                             |
83	| ---------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
84	| none beyond the component instance | not applicable  | not applicable      | not applicable                           | stable root structure required where the component renders on the server | Use a component-instance identity only for cleanup bookkeeping when no repeated structure exists. |
85	
86	## 14. SSR and Client Boundary Rules
87	
88	- The server must render every structural node required by the part-mapping table unless the component is explicitly provider-only or client-gated.
89	- Client-only listeners, timers, measurements, and node-handle work must wait until hydration or mount.
90	- Any node that participates in hydration-sensitive semantics must preserve the same structural identity across server and client render paths.
91	
92	## 15. Performance Constraints
93	
94	- Attr maps derived from the machine should be memoized or read through adapter derivation helpers instead of rebuilt eagerly on every render.
95	- Listener, timer, and observer registration must be stable across rerenders and must not churn unless the governing configuration actually changes.
96	- Cleanup must release only the resources owned by the current component instance and must avoid repeated quadratic teardown work.
97	
98	## 16. Implementation Dependencies
99	
100	| Dependency                                  | Required?   | Dependency type | Why it must exist first                                                                                         | Notes                                                                 |
101	| ------------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
102	| none beyond the documented utility contract | recommended | conceptual      | The component may still rely on shared adapter patterns even when no specific prerequisite utility is required. | State `not applicable` explicitly if there is no stronger dependency. |
103	
104	## 17. Recommended Implementation Sequence
105	
106	1. Establish the machine/context boundary and confirm the documented part mapping.
107	2. Establish any required refs, provider context, or registration surfaces.
108	3. Derive attrs and render the documented structural nodes.
109	4. Wire prop sync and normalized event handling.
110	5. Add SSR/client-only guards, cleanup, and verify the documented test oracles.
111	
112	## 18. Anti-Patterns
113	
114	- Do not mirror machine-owned state in unsynchronized local adapter state.
115	- Do not bypass the documented attr merge order or replace required structural nodes with equivalent-looking wrappers.
116	- Do not re-register listeners, timers, observers, or registries on every render when the governing configuration has not changed.
117	
118	## 19. Consumer Expectations and Guarantees
119	
120	- Consumers may assume documented adapter-owned structural nodes and attrs remain the canonical implementation surface.
121	- Consumers may assume framework-specific divergence is called out explicitly rather than hidden in generic prose.
122	- Consumers must not assume unspecified fallback behavior, cleanup ordering, or helper ownership beyond what this adapter spec documents.
123	
124	## 20. Platform Support Matrix
125	
126	| Capability / behavior                     | Browser client | SSR          | Notes                                                                                         |
127	| ----------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
128	| documented structural and state semantics | full support   | full support | This utility does not have additional platform variance beyond its existing SSR/client rules. |
129	
130	## 21. Debug Diagnostics and Production Policy
131	
132	| Condition                                                            | Debug build behavior | Production behavior | Notes                                                                               |
133	| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
134	| no component-specific diagnostics beyond documented failure policies | not applicable       | not applicable      | Use the `Failure and Degradation Rules` section as the full runtime policy surface. |
135	
136	## 22. Shared Adapter Helper Notes
137	
138	| Helper concept    | Required?      | Responsibility                                                                          | Reused by      | Notes                                                         |
139	| ----------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
140	| attr merge helper | not applicable | No special helper beyond the documented attr derivation and merge contract is required. | not applicable | Use the normal machine attr derivation path for this utility. |
141	
142	## 23. Framework-Specific Behavior
143	
144	Leptos chooses the root element dynamically according to the role mapping. When the requested landmark has no native semantic element, the adapter should render an explicit `<div role="...">` fallback rather than a vague generic wrapper with implied semantics.
145	
146	## 24. Canonical Implementation Sketch
147	
148	```rust
149	#[component]
150	pub fn Landmark(children: Children) -> impl IntoView {
151	    let api = landmark::Api::new(&landmark::Props::default());
152	    view! { <section {..api.root_attrs()}>{children()}</section> }
153	}
154	```
155	
156	## 25. Reference Implementation Skeleton
157	
158	No expanded skeleton beyond the canonical sketch is required for this utility.
159	
160	## 26. Adapter Invariants
161	
162	- Semantic landmark elements should be preferred over generic nodes with roles whenever the target landmark has a native element.
163	- When no native landmark element applies, the fallback node must be an explicit `<div role="...">` that preserves the requested landmark semantics.
164	- `aria-labelledby` precedence over `aria-label` must remain explicit and stable.
165	
166	## 27. Accessibility and SSR Notes
167	
168	Must preserve `aria-labelledby` precedence and semantic landmark behavior.
169	
170	## 28. Parity Summary and Intentional Deviations
171	
172	Parity summary: full core parity.
173	
174	Intentional deviations: none.
175	
176	## 29. Test Scenarios
177	
178	- root mapping
179	- semantic element vs fallback role
180	- labeling precedence
181	- unsupported or native-less landmark role falls back to explicit `<div role="...">`
182	
183	## 30. Test Oracle Notes
184	
185	| Behavior                               | Preferred oracle type | Notes                                                                                          |
186	| -------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
187	| structural rendering and part presence | rendered structure    | Verify the documented part mapping rather than incidental wrapper details.                     |
188	| accessibility and state attrs          | DOM attrs             | Assert the normalized attrs emitted by the adapter-owned node.                                 |
189	| native-less fallback rendering         | rendered structure    | Assert the adapter renders an explicit `<div>` fallback instead of an implicit wrapper choice. |
190	
191	## 31. Implementation Checklist
192	
193	- [ ] All documented parts and structural nodes are rendered with the correct ownership model.
194	- [ ] Attr merge precedence matches the documented contract.
195	- [ ] Prop sync and event normalization follow the documented machine paths.
196	- [ ] Cleanup releases every resource owned by the component instance.
197	- [ ] Semantic-element preference and explicit `<div role="...">` fallback behavior are verified.
198	- [ ] SSR/client boundary behavior matches the documented structure and test oracles.
199

153	## 23. Framework-Specific Behavior
154	
155	Dioxus may select the semantic tag dynamically or use a fallback generic node with heading role. When heading text can mix document directions, the rendered heading node should set `dir="auto"` so the browser resolves reading order from the content instead of inheriting a misleading page-level direction. Heading level providers and `Section` helpers must publish the incremented `HeadingContext` with `use_context_provider(...)` rather than relying on prop drilling.

146	## 23. Framework-Specific Behavior
147	
148	Leptos renders repeated chunks directly from an iterator. The core sets `dir="auto"` on the root wrapper via `Api::root_attrs()` — adapters do not need to add it. For mixed-direction content where chunk boundaries would re-order surrounding text visually, adapters MAY apply `unicode-bidi: isolate` CSS to chunk nodes (this is a styling concern outside the agnostic core's reach).
149	
150	## 24. Canonical Implementation Sketch
151	
152	```rust,no_check
153	#[component]
154	pub fn Highlight() -> impl IntoView {
155	    let props = highlight::Props::default();
156	    let api = highlight::Api::new(props);
157	    let locale = use_locale();
158	
159	    view! {
160	        <span ..api.root_attrs()>
161	            {api.chunks(&locale).into_iter().map(|chunk| {
162	                let attrs = api.chunk_attrs(chunk.highlighted);
163	                if chunk.highlighted {
164	                    Either::Left(view! { <mark ..attrs>{chunk.text}</mark> })
165	                } else {
166	                    Either::Right(view! { <span ..attrs>{chunk.text}</span> })
167	                }
168	            }).collect_view()}
169	        </span>
170	    }
171	}
172	```
173	
174	## 25. Reference Implementation Skeleton
175	
176	No expanded skeleton beyond the canonical sketch is required for this utility.
177	
178	## 26. Adapter Invariants
179	
180	- Chunk wrappers must remain explicit structural nodes so matched and unmatched content do not lose part identity.
181	- Match consolidation rules must remain stable across rerenders so highlighting does not flicker or split unexpectedly.
182	- Locale-sensitive matching behavior must remain explicit wherever the core contract depends on it.
183	- Text isolation or bidi-sensitive output rules must be preserved wherever highlighted content can span mixed-direction text.
184	
185	## 27. Accessibility and SSR Notes
186	
187	Must preserve `<mark>` semantics and repeated chunk structure. The agnostic core (`highlight_chunks` / `Api::chunks`) already consolidates overlapping and adjacent ranges before returning, so adapters never see back-to-back highlighted chunks and screen readers never get a stutter of "highlighted, highlighted, highlighted" for adjacent fuzzy hits. Adapters MAY layer a summary announcement (e.g., live-region "N characters matched") for very-high-cardinality fuzzy results.
188	
189	## 28. Parity Summary and Intentional Deviations
190	
191	Parity summary: full core rendering parity.
192	
193	Intentional deviations: none.
194	
195	## 29. Test Scenarios
196	
197	- root mapping
198	- repeated chunk mapping
199	- highlighted vs non-highlighted chunk rendering
200	- mixed-direction highlighted content keeps expected root direction and chunk isolation
201	- fuzzy highlighting with many small chunks documents the chosen consolidation behavior
202	
203	## 30. Test Oracle Notes
204	
205	| Behavior                               | Preferred oracle type | Notes                                                                              |
206	| -------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
207	| structural rendering and part presence | rendered structure    | Verify the documented part mapping rather than incidental wrapper details.         |
208	| accessibility and state attrs          | DOM attrs             | Assert the normalized attrs emitted by the adapter-owned node.                     |
209	| bidi handling                          | DOM attrs             | Assert root `dir="auto"` and any documented chunk-level isolation attrs or styles. |
210	| chunk consolidation policy             | rendered structure    | Verify repeated chunk output matches the documented fuzzy-match verbosity policy.  |
211

215	- [ ] Attr merge precedence matches the documented contract.
216	- [ ] Prop sync and event normalization follow the documented machine paths.

220	- [ ] SSR/client boundary behavior matches the documented structure and test oracles.

112	- Listener, timer, and observer registration must be stable across rerenders and must not churn unless the governing configuration actually changes.
113	- Cleanup must release only the resources owned by the current component instance and must avoid repeated quadratic teardown work.
114	
115	## 16. Implementation Dependencies
116	
117	| Dependency                                  | Required?   | Dependency type | Why it must exist first                                                                                         | Notes                                                                 |
118	| ------------------------------------------- | ----------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
119	| none beyond the documented utility contract | recommended | conceptual      | The component may still rely on shared adapter patterns even when no specific prerequisite utility is required. | State `not applicable` explicitly if there is no stronger dependency. |
120	
121	## 17. Recommended Implementation Sequence
122	
123	1. Establish the machine/context boundary and confirm the documented part mapping.
124	2. Establish any required refs, provider context, or registration surfaces.
125	3. Derive attrs and render the documented structural nodes.
126	4. Wire prop sync and normalized event handling.
127	5. Add SSR/client-only guards, cleanup, and verify the documented test oracles.
128	
129	## 18. Anti-Patterns
130	
131	- Do not mirror machine-owned state in unsynchronized local adapter state.
132	- Do not bypass the documented attr merge order or replace required structural nodes with equivalent-looking wrappers.
133	- Do not re-register listeners, timers, observers, or registries on every render when the governing configuration has not changed.
134	
135	## 19. Consumer Expectations and Guarantees
136	
137	- Consumers may assume documented adapter-owned structural nodes and attrs remain the canonical implementation surface.
138	- Consumers may assume framework-specific divergence is called out explicitly rather than hidden in generic prose.
139	- Consumers must not assume unspecified fallback behavior, cleanup ordering, or helper ownership beyond what this adapter spec documents.
140	
141	## 20. Platform Support Matrix
142	
143	| Capability / behavior                     | Web          | Desktop      | Mobile       | SSR          | Notes                                                                                                |
144	| ----------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------ | ------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
145	| documented structural and state semantics | full support | full support | full support | full support | This utility does not have additional platform variance beyond its existing framework and SSR rules. |
146	
147	## 21. Debug Diagnostics and Production Policy
148	
149	| Condition                                                            | Debug build behavior | Production behavior | Notes                                                                               |
150	| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
151	| no component-specific diagnostics beyond documented failure policies | not applicable       | not applicable      | Use the `Failure and Degradation Rules` section as the full runtime policy surface. |
152	
153	## 22. Shared Adapter Helper Notes
154	
155	| Helper concept    | Required?      | Responsibility                                                                          | Reused by      | Notes                                                         |
156	| ----------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
157	| attr merge helper | not applicable | No special helper beyond the documented attr derivation and merge contract is required. | not applicable | Use the normal machine attr derivation path for this utility. |
158	
159	## 23. Framework-Specific Behavior
160	
161	Dioxus renders repeated chunks directly from iterator output. The core sets `dir="auto"` on the root wrapper via `Api::root_attrs()` — adapters do not need to add it. For mixed-direction content where chunk boundaries would re-order surrounding text visually, adapters MAY apply `unicode-bidi: isolate` CSS to chunk nodes (this is a styling concern outside the agnostic core's reach).
162	
163	## 24. Canonical Implementation Sketch
164	
165	```rust,no_check
166	#[component]
167	pub fn Highlight() -> Element {
168	    let props = highlight::Props::default();
169	    let api = highlight::Api::new(props);
170	    let locale = use_locale();
171	
172	    rsx! {
173	        // Spread `Api::root_attrs()` and `Api::chunk_attrs(highlighted)`
174	        // onto the rendered elements (Dioxus 0.7 spread syntax).
175	        span {
176	            ..api.root_attrs(),
177	            {api.chunks(&locale).into_iter().map(|chunk| {
178	                let attrs = api.chunk_attrs(chunk.highlighted);
179	                if chunk.highlighted {
180	                    rsx! { mark { ..attrs, "{chunk.text}" } }
181	                } else {
182	                    rsx! { span { ..attrs, "{chunk.text}" } }
183	                }
184	            })}
185	        }
186	    }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	## 25. Reference Implementation Skeleton
191	
192	No expanded skeleton beyond the canonical sketch is required for this utility.
193	
194	## 26. Adapter Invariants
195	
196	- Chunk wrappers must remain explicit structural nodes so matched and unmatched content do not lose part identity.
197	- Match consolidation rules must remain stable across rerenders so highlighting does not flicker or split unexpectedly.
198	- Locale-sensitive matching behavior must remain explicit wherever the core contract depends on it.
199	- Text isolation or bidi-sensitive output rules must be preserved wherever highlighted content can span mixed-direction text.
200	
201	## 27. Accessibility and SSR Notes
202	
203	Must preserve `<mark>` semantics and repeated chunk structure. The agnostic core (`highlight_chunks` / `Api::chunks`) already consolidates overlapping and adjacent ranges before returning, so adapters never see back-to-back highlighted chunks and screen readers never get a stutter of "highlighted, highlighted, highlighted" for adjacent fuzzy hits. Adapters MAY layer a summary announcement (e.g., live-region "N characters matched") for very-high-cardinality fuzzy results.
204	
205	## 28. Parity Summary and Intentional Deviations
206	
207	Parity summary: full core rendering parity.
208	
209	Intentional deviations: none.
210	
211	## 29. Test Scenarios
212	
213	- root mapping
214	- repeated chunk mapping
215	- highlighted vs non-highlighted chunk rendering
216	- mixed-direction highlighted content keeps expected root direction and chunk isolation
217	- fuzzy highlighting with many small chunks documents the chosen consolidation behavior
218	
219	## 30. Test Oracle Notes
220	
221	| Behavior                               | Preferred oracle type | Notes                                                                              |
222	| -------------------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
223	| structural rendering and part presence | rendered structure    | Verify the documented part mapping rather than incidental wrapper details.         |
224	| accessibility and state attrs          | DOM attrs             | Assert the normalized attrs emitted by the adapter-owned node.                     |
225	| bidi handling                          | DOM attrs             | Assert root `dir="auto"` and any documented chunk-level isolation attrs or styles. |
226	| chunk consolidation policy             | rendered structure    | Verify repeated chunk output matches the documented fuzzy-match verbosity policy.  |
227	
228	## 31. Implementation Checklist
229	
230	- [ ] All documented parts and structural nodes are rendered with the correct ownership model.
231	- [ ] Attr merge precedence matches the documented contract.
232	- [ ] Prop sync and event normalization follow the documented machine paths.
233	- [ ] Cleanup releases every resource owned by the component instance.
234	- [ ] Mixed-direction root and chunk bidi handling is documented and verified when needed.
235	- [ ] Fuzzy-match chunk consolidation policy is explicit where many tiny wrappers would become noisy.
236	- [ ] SSR/client boundary behavior matches the documented structure and test oracles.
237

```
1	//! Leptos `VisuallyHidden` adapter.
2	//!
3	//! Renders the framework-agnostic `VisuallyHidden` attribute contract as either
4	//! an adapter-owned `<span>` root or a consumer-owned root through
5	//! [`VisuallyHiddenAsChild`].
6	
7	pub use ars_components::utility::visually_hidden::{Api, Part, Props};
8	use ars_core::{AttrMap, AttrValue, HtmlAttr};
9	use leptos::{children::TypedChildren, prelude::*, tachys::view::add_attr::AddAnyAttr};
10	
11	use crate::{as_child::AsChildAttrs, attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs};
12	
13	fn root_attr_map(id: Option<String>, is_focusable: bool, as_child: bool) -> AttrMap {
14	    let mut props = Props::new().is_focusable(is_focusable).as_child(as_child);
15	
16	    if let Some(id) = id.clone() {
17	        props = props.id(id);
18	    }
19	
20	    let mut attrs = Api::new(props).root_attrs();
21	
22	    if let Some(id) = id {
23	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, id);
24	    }
25	
26	    attrs
27	}
28	
29	fn root_attrs(
30	    id: Option<String>,
31	    is_focusable: bool,
32	    as_child: bool,
33	) -> Vec<crate::LeptosAttribute> {
34	    attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(root_attr_map(id, is_focusable, as_child))
35	}
36	
37	fn as_child_root_attrs(id: Option<String>, is_focusable: bool) -> Vec<crate::LeptosAttribute> {
38	    use leptos::tachys::html::attribute::any_attribute::IntoAnyAttribute as _;
39	
40	    let mut attrs = root_attr_map(id, is_focusable, true);
41	
42	    if !is_focusable {
43	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Class, AttrValue::None);
44	    }
45	
46	    let mut leptos_attrs = attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(attrs);
47	
48	    if !is_focusable {
49	        leptos_attrs.push(
50	            leptos::tachys::html::class::class(("ars-visually-hidden", true)).into_any_attr(),
51	        );
52	    }
53	
54	    leptos_attrs
55	}
56	
57	/// Leptos VisuallyHidden component rendered as an adapter-owned `<span>` root.
58	#[component]
59	pub fn VisuallyHidden<T>(
60	    /// Optional component instance ID.
61	    #[prop(optional, into)]
62	    id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,
63	
64	    /// Whether the hidden content should become visible when focused.
65	    #[prop(optional)]
66	    is_focusable: bool,
67	
68	    /// Hidden content that remains available to assistive technology.
69	    children: TypedChildren<T>,
70	) -> impl IntoView
71	where
72	    View<T>: IntoView,
73	{
74	    let id = id.map(Oco::into_owned);
75	    let attrs = root_attrs(id, is_focusable, false);
76	    let children = children.into_inner();
77	
78	    view! { <span {..attrs}>{children()}</span> }
79	}
80	
81	/// Leptos VisuallyHidden component that forwards root attrs to one child root.
82	#[component]
83	pub fn VisuallyHiddenAsChild<T>(
84	    /// Optional component instance ID.
85	    #[prop(optional, into)]
86	    id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,
87	
88	    /// Whether the hidden content should become visible when focused.
89	    #[prop(optional)]
90	    is_focusable: bool,
91	
92	    /// Child root that receives the visually-hidden root attrs.
93	    children: TypedChildren<T>,
94	) -> impl IntoView
95	where
96	    View<T>: AddAnyAttr,
97	    <View<T> as AddAnyAttr>::Output<Vec<crate::LeptosAttribute>>: IntoView,
98	{
99	    let id = id.map(Oco::into_owned);
100	
101	    children.into_inner()()
102	        .add_any_attr(AsChildAttrs::from(as_child_root_attrs(id, is_focusable)).into_inner())
103	}
104
```

```
1	//! Dioxus `VisuallyHidden` adapter.
2	//!
3	//! Renders the framework-agnostic `VisuallyHidden` attribute contract as either
4	//! an adapter-owned `<span>` root or a consumer-owned root through
5	//! [`VisuallyHiddenAsChild`].
6	
7	use std::{
8	    collections::HashMap,
9	    sync::{LazyLock, Mutex},
10	};
11	
12	pub use ars_components::utility::visually_hidden::{Api, Part, Props};
13	use ars_core::HtmlAttr;
14	use dioxus::{
15	    dioxus_core::{AttributeValue, Template, TemplateAttribute, TemplateNode, VNode},
16	    prelude::*,
17	};
18	
19	use crate::{
20	    as_child::{AsChildRenderProps, merge_dioxus_attrs},
21	    attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs,
22	};
23	
24	static TEMPLATE_CACHE: LazyLock<Mutex<HashMap<TemplateKey, Template>>> =
25	    LazyLock::new(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
26	
27	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Hash, PartialEq)]
28	struct TemplateKey {
29	    roots: usize,
30	    node_paths: usize,
31	    attr_paths: usize,
32	}
33	
34	fn root_attrs(id: Option<&str>, is_focusable: bool, as_child: bool) -> Vec<Attribute> {
35	    let mut props = Props::new().is_focusable(is_focusable).as_child(as_child);
36	
37	    if let Some(id) = id {
38	        props = props.id(id);
39	    }
40	
41	    let mut attrs = Api::new(props).root_attrs();
42	
43	    if let Some(id) = id {
44	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, id);
45	    }
46	
47	    attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(attrs)
48	}
49	
50	/// Props for the Dioxus [`VisuallyHidden`] component.
51	#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
52	pub struct VisuallyHiddenProps {
53	    /// Optional component instance ID.
54	    #[props(optional, into)]
55	    pub id: Option<String>,
56	
57	    /// Whether the hidden content should become visible when focused.
58	    #[props(default = false)]
59	    pub is_focusable: bool,
60	
61	    /// Hidden content that remains available to assistive technology.
62	    pub children: Element,
63	}
64	
65	/// Props for the Dioxus [`VisuallyHiddenAsChild`] component.
66	#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
67	pub struct VisuallyHiddenAsChildProps {
68	    /// Optional component instance ID.
69	    #[props(optional, into)]
70	    pub id: Option<String>,
71	
72	    /// Whether the hidden content should become visible when focused.
73	    #[props(default = false)]
74	    pub is_focusable: bool,
75	
76	    /// Render callback that owns the child root and spreads `VisuallyHidden` attrs.
77	    pub render: Callback<AsChildRenderProps, Element>,
78	}
79	
80	/// Dioxus `VisuallyHidden` component rendered as an adapter-owned `<span>` root.
81	#[component]
82	pub fn VisuallyHidden(props: VisuallyHiddenProps) -> Element {
83	    let attrs = root_attrs(props.id.as_deref(), props.is_focusable, false);
84	    let children = props.children;
85	
86	    rsx! {
87	        span { ..attrs,{children} }
88	    }
89	}
90	
91	/// Dioxus `VisuallyHidden` component that forwards root attrs to one child root.
92	#[component]
93	pub fn VisuallyHiddenAsChild(props: VisuallyHiddenAsChildProps) -> Element {
94	    let mut attrs = root_attrs(props.id.as_deref(), props.is_focusable, true);
95	    let hidden_class = (!props.is_focusable)
96	        .then(|| take_attr(&mut attrs, "class"))
97	        .flatten();
98	
99	    props
100	        .render
101	        .call(AsChildRenderProps { attrs })
102	        .map(|vnode| merge_root_attrs(vnode, hidden_class))
103	}
104	
105	fn take_attr(attrs: &mut Vec<Attribute>, name: &str) -> Option<Attribute> {
106	    let index = attrs.iter().position(|attr| attr.name == name)?;
107	
108	    Some(attrs.remove(index))
109	}
110	
111	fn merge_root_attrs(vnode: VNode, attr: Option<Attribute>) -> VNode {
112	    let Some(attr) = attr else {
113	        return vnode;
114	    };
115	
116	    let (template, merged_static_class) = merge_static_root_class(vnode.template, &attr);
117	
118	    let dynamic_attrs = if merged_static_class {
119	        vnode.dynamic_attrs.clone()
120	    } else if let Some((first, rest)) = vnode.dynamic_attrs.split_first() {
121	        let first = first.to_vec();
122	        let first = merge_dioxus_attrs(first, vec![attr]).into_boxed_slice();
123	
124	        std::iter::once(first)
125	            .chain(rest.iter().cloned())
126	            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
127	            .into_boxed_slice()
128	    } else {
129	        vnode.dynamic_attrs.clone()
130	    };
131	
132	    VNode::new(
133	        vnode.key.clone(),
134	        template,
135	        vnode.dynamic_nodes.clone(),
136	        dynamic_attrs,
137	    )
138	}
139	
140	fn merge_static_root_class(template: Template, attr: &Attribute) -> (Template, bool) {
141	    if attr.name != "class" {
142	        return (template, false);
143	    }
144	
145	    let key = TemplateKey::from(template);
146	
147	    if let Some(template) = TEMPLATE_CACHE
148	        .lock()
149	        .expect("template cache lock should not be poisoned")
150	        .get(&key)
151	        .copied()
152	    {
153	        return (template, true);
154	    }
155	
156	    let Some((root, rest)) = template.roots.split_first() else {
157	        return (template, false);
158	    };
159	
160	    let (root, merged) = merge_static_class_into_node(*root, attr);
161	
162	    if !merged {
163	        return (template, false);
164	    }
165	
166	    let roots = std::iter::once(root)
167	        .chain(rest.iter().copied())
168	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
169	        .into_boxed_slice();
170	
171	    let template = Template {
172	        roots: Box::leak(roots),
173	        node_paths: template.node_paths,
174	        attr_paths: template.attr_paths,
175	    };
176	
177	    TEMPLATE_CACHE
178	        .lock()
179	        .expect("template cache lock should not be poisoned")
180	        .insert(key, template);
181	
182	    (template, true)
183	}
184	
185	fn merge_static_class_into_node(node: TemplateNode, attr: &Attribute) -> (TemplateNode, bool) {
186	    let TemplateNode::Element {
187	        tag,
188	        namespace,
189	        attrs,
190	        children,
191	    } = node
192	    else {
193	        return (node, false);
194	    };
195	
196	    let mut merged = false;
197	
198	    let attrs = attrs
199	        .iter()
200	        .map(|existing| match existing {
201	            TemplateAttribute::Static {
202	                name: "class",
203	                value,
204	                namespace: None,
205	            } => {
206	                merged = true;
207	
208	                TemplateAttribute::Static {
209	                    name: "class",
210	                    value: leaked_class_tokens(value, attr),
211	                    namespace: None,
212	                }
213	            }
214	
215	            existing => clone_template_attr(existing),
216	        })
217	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
218	        .into_boxed_slice();
219	
220	    (
221	        TemplateNode::Element {
222	            tag,
223	            namespace,
224	            attrs: Box::leak(attrs),
225	            children,
226	        },
227	        merged,
228	    )
229	}
230	
231	const fn clone_template_attr(attr: &TemplateAttribute) -> TemplateAttribute {
232	    match attr {
233	        TemplateAttribute::Static {
234	            name,
235	            value,
236	            namespace,
237	        } => TemplateAttribute::Static {
238	            name,
239	            value,
240	            namespace: *namespace,
241	        },
242	
243	        TemplateAttribute::Dynamic { id } => TemplateAttribute::Dynamic { id: *id },
244	    }
245	}
246	
247	fn leaked_class_tokens(existing: &'static str, attr: &Attribute) -> &'static str {
248	    let AttributeValue::Text(component) = &attr.value else {
249	        return existing;
250	    };
251	
252	    let mut tokens = existing.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>();
253	
254	    for token in component.split_whitespace() {
255	        if !tokens.contains(&token) {
256	            tokens.push(token);
257	        }
258	    }
259	
260	    Box::leak(tokens.join(" ").into_boxed_str())
261	}
262	
263	impl From<Template> for TemplateKey {
264	    fn from(template: Template) -> Self {
265	        Self {
266	            roots: template.roots.as_ptr() as usize,
267	            node_paths: template.node_paths.as_ptr() as usize,
268	            attr_paths: template.attr_paths.as_ptr() as usize,
269	        }
270	    }
271	}
272
```
