1	//! Convenience re-exports for end users of the Leptos adapter.
2	//!
3	//! A single `use ars_leptos::prelude::*;` gives application authors access to
4	//! the components, user-facing traits, and configuration types they need —
5	//! without hunting through individual `ars_*` crates.
6	//!
7	//! # What belongs in the prelude
8	//!
9	//! Only items that **end users** interact with directly:
10	//!
11	//! 1. **Component modules** — as components land (e.g., `button`, `dialog`,
12	//!    `select`), their public module paths are re-exported here so users can
13	//!    write `button::Props`, `dialog::Machine`, etc.
14	//!
15	//! 2. **User-facing traits** — traits that end users call on component outputs
16	//!    (e.g., `Translate` from `ars-i18n` for localised strings). Re-exporting
17	//!    the trait avoids forcing users to add a direct dependency on the
18	//!    subsystem crate just to call a method.
19	//!
20	//! 3. **Configuration types** — types that appear in component props or that
21	//!    users pass to configure behaviour (e.g., `Locale`, `Direction`,
22	//!    `Orientation`, `Selection`).
23	//!
24	//! # What does NOT belong in the prelude
25	//!
26	//! - **Core engine internals** — `Machine`, `Service`, `ConnectApi`,
27	//!   `ComponentPart`, `AttrMap`, `Bindable`, `TransitionPlan`, `PendingEffect`.
28	//!   These are implementation details used by component authors *inside* the
29	//!   adapter crate, not by end users consuming components.
30	//! - **Accessibility primitives** — `AriaRole`, `AriaAttribute`, `ComponentIds`.
31	//!   Wired internally by each component; end users never construct these.
32	//! - **Interaction primitives** — `merge_attrs`, `PressState`, `FocusState`.
33	//!   Internal to component implementations.
34	//! - **Adapter hooks** — `use_machine`, `UseMachineReturn`, `EphemeralRef`.
35	//!   Used by component modules inside the adapter crate, not by end users
36	//!   who consume the ready-made components. (Still publicly accessible via
37	//!   `ars_leptos::use_machine` for advanced users building custom machines.)
38	//! - **Framework re-exports** — `leptos::prelude::*` should be imported
39	//!   separately; we do not re-export Leptos types to avoid version coupling.
40	//!
41	//! # Growth policy
42	//!
43	//! When adding a new item, ask: "Does an end user writing `<Button>` or
44	//! `<Dialog>` in their app need this?" If yes, add it. If only component
45	//! implementors inside this crate need it, keep it as a regular import.
46	
47	// -- User-facing traits --
48	pub use ars_collections::{Key, TabKey};
49	// `ColorMode` is a configuration enum that end users pass to `ArsProvider`
50	// via the `color_mode` prop; it belongs with the configuration types.
51	pub use ars_core::{
52	    ColorMode, I18nRegistries, MessageFn, MessagesRegistry, SafeUrl, UnsafeUrlError,
53	};
54	pub use ars_i18n::{Direction, IntlBackend, Locale, Orientation, ResolvedDirection, Translate};
55	
56	// -- Root provider --
57	// `ArsProvider` is the single root provider every ars-ui application wraps its
58	// tree with. It publishes locale, direction, color mode, disabled/read-only,
59	// portal/root nodes, platform effects, and style strategy via context. See
60	// `spec/leptos-components/utility/ars-provider.md`.
61	pub use crate::ArsProvider;
62	// -- Component modules --
63	//
64	// Consumers reach component types via the module qualifier
65	// (e.g. `dismissable::Props`, `dismissable::Region`, `dismissable::Handle`,
66	// `dismissable::DismissReason`, `dismissable::use_dismissable`); never via
67	// flattened aliases such as `DismissableProps` or `DismissableRegion`.
68	//
69	// The adapter `dismissable` module re-exports the agnostic
70	// `ars_components::utility::dismissable::*` surface, so this single
71	// re-export covers both the framework-agnostic types (`Props`, `Messages`,
72	// `DismissReason`, …) and the Leptos-side wrappers (`Handle`, `Region`,
73	// `RegionProps`, `use_dismissable`).
74	pub use crate::as_child;
75	pub use crate::navigation::{self, tabs};
76	// The `error_boundary` adapter module exposes the `ArsErrorBoundary`
77	// wrapper component spec'd at
78	// `spec/foundation/08-adapter-leptos.md` §17. End users reach it as
79	// `error_boundary::ArsErrorBoundary` after `use ars_leptos::prelude::*;`.
80	pub use crate::utility::{
81	    self, button, client_only, dismissable, error_boundary, separator, visually_hidden,
82	    z_index_allocator,
83	};
84	// -- User-facing helpers --
85	pub use crate::{Translatable, t, use_number_formatter};
86

8	#[test]
9	fn visually_hidden_renders_default_span_with_hidden_attrs() {
10	    let html =
11	        view! { <VisuallyHidden id="vh-default">"Screen reader only"</VisuallyHidden> }.to_html();
12	
13	    assert!(
14	        html.trim_start().starts_with("<span"),
15	        "default root should be a span: {html}"
16	    );
17	
18	    for fragment in [
19	        r#"id="vh-default""#,
20	        r#"data-ars-scope="visually-hidden""#,
21	        r#"data-ars-part="root""#,
22	        r#"class="ars-visually-hidden""#,
23	        "Screen reader only",
24	    ] {
25	        assert!(html.contains(fragment), "missing {fragment}: {html}");
26	    }
27	}
28	
29	#[test]
30	fn visually_hidden_focusable_uses_focusable_data_hook() {
31	    let html = view! {
32	        <VisuallyHidden id="vh-focusable" is_focusable=true>
33	            "Skip to content"
34	        </VisuallyHidden>
35	    }
36	    .to_html();
37	
38	    assert!(
39	        html.contains(r#"data-ars-visually-hidden-focusable"#),
40	        "missing focusable hook: {html}"
41	    );

43	        !html.contains(r#"class="ars-visually-hidden""#),
44	        "focusable variant must not include unconditional hidden class: {html}"
45	    );
46	}

53	        !html.contains("id="),

59	fn visually_hidden_as_child_forwards_attrs_without_wrapper() {
60	    let html = view! {

63	        </VisuallyHiddenAsChild>

68	        html.trim_start().starts_with("<a"),

1	//! `Landmark` component connect API.
2	//!
3	//! `Landmark` is a stateless, framework-agnostic attribute mapper for page
4	//! structure. It maps semantic landmark roles to ARIA role tokens and label
5	//! attributes while leaving actual element selection to framework adapters.
6	
7	use alloc::string::String;
8	
9	use ars_core::{
10	    AriaAttr, AttrMap, ComponentMessages, ComponentPart, ConnectApi, Env, HasId, HtmlAttr, Locale,
11	    MessageFn,
12	};
13	
14	/// The semantic role of a landmark region.
15	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
16	pub enum Role {
17	    /// Page-level banner landmark, usually rendered as `<header>`.
18	    Banner,
19	
20	    /// Navigation landmark, usually rendered as `<nav>`.
21	    Navigation,
22	
23	    /// Main content landmark, usually rendered as `<main>`.
24	    Main,
25	
26	    /// Complementary content landmark, usually rendered as `<aside>`.
27	    Complementary,
28	
29	    /// Page-level content information landmark, usually rendered as `<footer>`.
30	    ContentInfo,
31	
32	    /// Search landmark, rendered as `<search>` or a fallback element.
33	    Search,
34	
35	    /// Form landmark, recognized by assistive technology only when named.
36	    Form,
37	
38	    /// Region landmark, recognized by assistive technology only when named.
39	    Region,
40	}
41	
42	impl Role {
43	    /// Returns the WAI-ARIA role token for this landmark role.
44	    #[must_use]
45	    pub const fn aria_role(self) -> &'static str {
46	        match self {
47	            Self::Banner => "banner",
48	            Self::Navigation => "navigation",
49	            Self::Main => "main",
50	            Self::Complementary => "complementary",
51	            Self::ContentInfo => "contentinfo",
52	            Self::Search => "search",
53	            Self::Form => "form",
54	            Self::Region => "region",
55	        }
56	    }
57	
58	    /// Returns whether this landmark role requires an accessible name to be
59	    /// exposed consistently by assistive technology.
60	    #[must_use]
61	    pub const fn requires_accessible_name(self) -> bool {
62	        matches!(self, Self::Form | Self::Region)
63	    }
64	}
65	
66	/// Props for the `Landmark` component.
67	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, HasId)]
68	pub struct Props {
69	    /// Component instance ID.
70	    pub id: String,
71	
72	    /// The semantic landmark role.
73	    pub role: Role,
74	
75	    /// Optional ID of an external element that labels this landmark.
76	    ///
77	    /// When set, `aria-labelledby` takes precedence over localized
78	    /// `aria-label` output.
79	    pub labelledby_id: Option<String>,
80	}
81	
82	impl Default for Props {
83	    fn default() -> Self {
84	        Self {
85	            id: String::new(),
86	            role: Role::Region,
87	            labelledby_id: None,
88	        }
89	    }
90	}
91	
92	impl Props {
93	    /// Returns fresh landmark props with the documented defaults.
94	    #[must_use]
95	    pub fn new() -> Self {
96	        Self::default()
97	    }
98	
99	    /// Sets the component instance ID.
100	    #[must_use]
101	    pub fn id(mut self, id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
102	        self.id = id.into();
103	        self
104	    }
105	
106	    /// Sets the semantic landmark role.
107	    #[must_use]
108	    pub const fn role(mut self, role: Role) -> Self {
109	        self.role = role;
110	        self
111	    }
112	
113	    /// Sets the ID of an external labelling element.
114	    #[must_use]
115	    pub fn labelledby_id(mut self, id: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
116	        self.labelledby_id = Some(id.into());
117	        self
118	    }
119	
120	    /// Clears any external labelling element ID.
121	    #[must_use]
122	    pub fn unlabelled(mut self) -> Self {
123	        self.labelledby_id = None;
124	        self
125	    }
126	}
127	
128	/// Messages for the `Landmark` component.
129	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
130	pub struct Messages {
131	    /// Accessible name for the landmark region.
132	    ///
133	    /// Form and Region landmarks require a non-empty accessible name to be
134	    /// exposed consistently by assistive technology.
135	    pub label: MessageFn<dyn Fn(&Locale) -> String + Send + Sync>,
136	}
137	
138	impl Default for Messages {
139	    fn default() -> Self {
140	        Self {
141	            label: MessageFn::static_str(""),
142	        }
143	    }
144	}
145	
146	impl ComponentMessages for Messages {}
147	
148	/// Structural parts exposed by the `Landmark` connect API.
149	#[derive(ComponentPart)]
150	#[scope = "landmark"]
151	pub enum Part {
152	    /// The root landmark element.
153	    Root,
154	}
155	
156	/// API for the `Landmark` component.
157	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
158	pub struct Api {
159	    props: Props,
160	    locale: Locale,
161	    messages: Messages,
162	}
163	
164	impl Api {
165	    /// Creates a new API from landmark props, environment, and localized
166	    /// messages.
167	    #[must_use]
168	    pub fn new(props: Props, env: &Env, messages: &Messages) -> Self {
169	        Self {
170	            props,
171	            locale: env.locale.clone(),
172	            messages: messages.clone(),
173	        }
174	    }
175	
176	    /// Returns the underlying landmark props.
177	    #[must_use]
178	    pub const fn props(&self) -> &Props {
179	        &self.props
180	    }
181	
182	    /// Returns the requested semantic landmark role.
183	    #[must_use]
184	    pub const fn role(&self) -> Role {
185	        self.props.role
186	    }
187	
188	    /// Returns the external labelling element ID, when present and non-empty.
189	    #[must_use]
190	    pub fn labelledby_id(&self) -> Option<&str> {
191	        self.non_empty_labelledby_id()
192	    }
193	
194	    /// Returns `true` when adapters should prefer their generic fallback
195	    /// element for the default rendering path.
196	    ///
197	    /// Adapters can still call [`Self::root_attrs`] with
198	    /// `is_native_landmark_element` set to `false` for any role when they render
199	    /// an explicit-role fallback element.
200	    #[must_use]
201	    pub const fn prefers_generic_fallback_element(&self) -> bool {
202	        matches!(self.props.role, Role::Search)
203	    }
204	
205	    /// Resolves the localized accessible label for this landmark.
206	    #[must_use]
207	    pub fn label(&self) -> String {
208	        (self.messages.label)(&self.locale)
209	    }
210	
211	    /// Returns whether this landmark has either `aria-labelledby` or a
212	    /// localized `aria-label` containing non-whitespace text.
213	    #[must_use]
214	    pub fn has_accessible_name(&self) -> bool {
215	        self.non_empty_labelledby_id().is_some() || label_has_text(&self.label())
216	    }
217	
218	    /// Returns whether connecting this landmark should emit the development
219	    /// warning for a required but missing accessible name.
220	    #[must_use]
221	    pub fn missing_accessible_name_warning_needed(&self) -> bool {
222	        self.props.role.requires_accessible_name() && !self.has_accessible_name()
223	    }
224	
225	    /// Returns root attributes for the landmark element.
226	    ///
227	    /// The core always emits stable component data attributes. It emits an
228	    /// explicit ARIA `role` only for fallback elements, and it never
229	    /// emits both `aria-labelledby` and `aria-label`.
230	    #[must_use]
231	    pub fn root_attrs(&self, is_native_landmark_element: bool) -> AttrMap {
232	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
233	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();
234	
235	        attrs
236	            .set(HtmlAttr::Id, &self.props.id)
237	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
238	            .set(part_attr, part_val);
239	
240	        if !is_native_landmark_element {
241	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, self.props.role.aria_role());
242	        }
243	
244	        if let Some(labelledby_id) = self.non_empty_labelledby_id() {
245	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::LabelledBy), labelledby_id);
246	        } else {
247	            let label = self.label();
248	
249	            if label_has_text(&label) {
250	                attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), label);
251	            } else if self.missing_accessible_name_warning_needed() {
252	                warn_missing_accessible_name(self.props.role);
253	            }
254	        }
255	
256	        attrs
257	    }
258	
259	    fn non_empty_labelledby_id(&self) -> Option<&str> {
260	        self.props
261	            .labelledby_id
262	            .as_deref()
263	            .filter(|id| !id.trim().is_empty())
264	    }
265	}
266	
267	fn label_has_text(label: &str) -> bool {
268	    !label.trim().is_empty()
269	}
270	
271	impl ConnectApi for Api {
272	    type Part = Part;
273	
274	    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Self::Part) -> AttrMap {
275	        match part {
276	            Part::Root => self.root_attrs(true),
277	        }
278	    }
279	}
280	
281	#[cfg(feature = "debug")]
282	fn warn_missing_accessible_name(role: Role) {
283	    if role.requires_accessible_name() {
284	        log::warn!(
285	            "landmark: role '{}' requires an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby)",
286	            role.aria_role()
287	        );
288	    }
289	}
290	
291	#[cfg(all(
292	    debug_assertions,
293	    not(feature = "debug"),
294	    feature = "std",
295	    not(all(
296	        target_arch = "wasm32",
297	        not(any(target_os = "emscripten", target_os = "wasi"))
298	    ))
299	))]
300	fn warn_missing_accessible_name(role: Role) {
301	    if role.requires_accessible_name() {
302	        eprintln!(
303	            "landmark: role '{}' requires an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby)",
304	            role.aria_role()
305	        );
306	    }
307	}
308	
309	#[cfg(not(any(
310	    feature = "debug",
311	    all(
312	        debug_assertions,
313	        feature = "std",
314	        not(all(
315	            target_arch = "wasm32",
316	            not(any(target_os = "emscripten", target_os = "wasi"))
317	        ))
318	    )
319	)))]
320	const fn warn_missing_accessible_name(_role: Role) {}

322	#[cfg(test)]
323	mod tests {

353	            (Role::Complementary, "complementary"),

711	                        .push(record.args().to_string());
712	                }

716	        }
717

724	            log::set_max_level(log::LevelFilter::Warn);

1	//! `Heading` component connect API.
2	//!
3	//! `Heading` is a stateless, framework-agnostic attribute mapper for semantic
4	//! headings. It resolves a heading level from explicit props or from
5	//! [`HeadingContext`], and emits fallback ARIA attributes when an adapter cannot
6	//! render a native `<h1>` through `<h6>` element.
7

11	use ars_core::{AriaAttr, AttrMap, ComponentPart, ConnectApi, HasId, HtmlAttr};

16	    /// Component instance ID.
17	    pub id: String,
18	
19	    /// Explicit heading level override. When absent, the nearest
20	    /// [`HeadingContext`] supplies the resolved level.
21	    pub level: Option<Level>,
22	}
23	
24	impl Props {

27	    pub fn new() -> Self {
28	        Self::default()
29	    }

32	    #[must_use]

34	        self.id = id.into();

55	#[repr(u8)]
56	pub enum Level {
57	    /// First-level heading.
58	    One = 1,
59	
60	    /// Second-level heading.
61	    Two = 2,
62	
63	    /// Third-level heading.
64	    Three = 3,
65	
66	    /// Fourth-level heading.
67	    Four = 4,
68	
69	    /// Fifth-level heading.
70	    Five = 5,
71	
72	    /// Sixth-level heading, the maximum HTML heading level.
73	    Six = 6,
74	}
75	
76	impl Level {
77	    /// Converts a numeric level into a [`Level`], clamping values below one to
78	    /// [`Level::One`] and values above six to [`Level::Six`].
79	    #[must_use]
80	    pub const fn from_u8(value: u8) -> Self {
81	        match value {
82	            0 | 1 => Self::One,
83	            2 => Self::Two,
84	            3 => Self::Three,
85	            4 => Self::Four,
86	            5 => Self::Five,
87	            _ => Self::Six,
88	        }
89	    }
90

94	        self as u8
95	    }
96	}

215	#[derive(ComponentPart)]
216	#[scope = "heading"]
217	pub enum Part {

222	/// API for the `Heading` component.
223	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
224	pub struct Api {
225	    props: Props,
226	    ctx: HeadingContext,
227	}
228	
229	impl Api {
230	    /// Creates a new API from heading props and the nearest heading context.
231	    #[must_use]
232	    pub const fn new(props: Props, ctx: HeadingContext) -> Self {
233	        Self { props, ctx }
234	    }
235	
236	    /// Returns the underlying heading props.
237	    #[must_use]
238	    pub const fn props(&self) -> &Props {
239	        &self.props
240	    }
241	
242	    /// Returns the heading context used by this API.
243	    #[must_use]
244	    pub const fn context(&self) -> &HeadingContext {
245	        &self.ctx
246	    }
247	
248	    /// Returns the component instance ID.
249	    #[must_use]
250	    pub fn id(&self) -> &str {
251	        &self.props.id
252	    }
253	
254	    /// Returns the resolved heading level, preferring the explicit prop over
255	    /// the inherited context.
256	    #[must_use]
257	    pub const fn resolved_level(&self) -> Level {
258	        if let Some(level) = self.props.level {
259	            level
260	        } else {
261	            self.ctx.level
262	        }
263	    }
264	
265	    /// Returns root attributes for either a native heading element or an ARIA
266	    /// fallback element.
267	    ///
268	    /// Native `<h1>` through `<h6>` elements already expose the heading role and
269	    /// level, so `role` and `aria-level` are only emitted for non-semantic
270	    /// fallback elements.
271	    #[must_use]
272	    pub fn root_attrs(&self, is_native_heading_element: bool) -> AttrMap {
273	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
274	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();
275	
276	        attrs
277	            .set(HtmlAttr::Id, &self.props.id)
278	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
279	            .set(part_attr, part_val);
280	
281	        if !is_native_heading_element {
282	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, "heading").set(
283	                HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Level),
284	                self.resolved_level().to_string(),
285	            );
286	        }
287	
288	        attrs
289	    }
290	}
291	
292	impl ConnectApi for Api {
293	    type Part = Part;
294	
295	    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Self::Part) -> AttrMap {
296	        match part {
297	            Part::Root => self.root_attrs(true),
298	        }
299	    }
300	}

1	//! `Highlight` component — text substring matching with Unicode-aware case folding.
2	//!
3	//! `Highlight` is a stateless utility that splits a text into alternating
4	//! highlighted / non-highlighted chunks based on one or more search queries.
5	//! It supports three match strategies (`Contains`, `StartsWith`, `Fuzzy`),
6	//! locale-aware Unicode case mapping via ICU4X `CaseMapper` (handles Turkic
7	//! dotted/dotless I, German eszett, Greek final sigma, Lithuanian dotted I,
8	//! and other CLDR-supplied language-tailored mappings), and multi-query
9	//! merging that consolidates both overlapping **and** adjacent ranges so
10	//! adapters never see back-to-back highlighted chunks.
11	//!
12	//! The component has no state machine. Adapters render each returned
13	//! `HighlightChunk` as a `<mark>` (`highlighted == true`) or `<span>`
14	//! (`highlighted == false`). The agnostic-core consists of `Props`,
15	//! `MatchStrategy`, `HighlightChunk`, the `Part` enum, the `Api` attribute
16	//! mapper, and the `highlight_chunks` standalone computation.
17	//!
18	//! This module is gated on `feature = "i18n"`: the locale-aware contract on
19	//! `Props::ignore_case = true` is part of the spec, so the module is only
20	//! compiled when `ars-i18n/icu4x` is enabled.
21	//!
22	//! See `spec/components/utility/highlight.md` for the authoritative contract.
23	
24	use alloc::{borrow::ToOwned as _, string::String, vec, vec::Vec};
25	
26	use ars_core::{AttrMap, ComponentPart, ConnectApi, HtmlAttr};
27	use ars_i18n::Locale;
28	
29	/// Props for the [`Highlight`](crate::utility::highlight) component.
30	///
31	/// `Highlight` does not carry a DOM `id` — chunk output is a sequence of
32	/// adapter-rendered children, not a single identifiable element — so [`Props`]
33	/// does not derive [`HasId`](ars_core::HasId) like other stateless utilities.
34	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
35	pub struct Props {
36	    /// The search queries to highlight. Supports a single query string or
37	    /// multiple queries to highlight simultaneously (e.g., multiple search
38	    /// terms). When multiple queries are provided, all matches from all
39	    /// queries are highlighted; overlapping ranges are merged into a single
40	    /// highlighted chunk. An empty vec, or a vec where every entry is empty,
41	    /// produces a single non-highlighted chunk containing the full text.
42	    pub query: Vec<String>,
43	
44	    /// The full text to search within.
45	    pub text: String,
46	
47	    /// When `true` (default), matching is case-insensitive via Unicode case
48	    /// folding — `ars_i18n::case_fold` with the [`Locale`] passed to
49	    /// [`highlight_chunks`] / [`Api::chunks`]. When `false`, byte-exact
50	    /// matching is used (no normalisation pass; the locale parameter is
51	    /// ignored).
52	    pub ignore_case: bool,
53	
54	    /// The strategy used to match the query against the text. Defaults to
55	    /// [`MatchStrategy::Contains`].
56	    pub match_strategy: MatchStrategy,
57	}
58	
59	impl Default for Props {
60	    fn default() -> Self {
61	        Self {
62	            query: Vec::new(),
63	            text: String::new(),
64	            ignore_case: true,
65	            match_strategy: MatchStrategy::Contains,
66	        }
67	    }
68	}
69	
70	impl Props {
71	    /// Returns fresh [`Props`] with the documented defaults — equivalent
72	    /// to [`Default::default`], offered as the entry point for the
73	    /// builder chain.
74	    #[must_use]
75	    pub fn new() -> Self {
76	        Self::default()
77	    }
78	
79	    /// Sets the query list. Accepts any iterable of `Into<String>`, so
80	    /// callers can pass `["foo"]`, `vec!["foo".to_string(), "bar".into()]`,
81	    /// `&["foo", "bar"][..]`, etc.
82	    #[must_use]
83	    pub fn query<I, S>(mut self, query: I) -> Self
84	    where
85	        I: IntoIterator<Item = S>,
86	        S: Into<String>,
87	    {
88	        self.query = query.into_iter().map(Into::into).collect();
89	        self
90	    }
91	
92	    /// Sets the text to search within.
93	    #[must_use]
94	    pub fn text(mut self, text: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
95	        self.text = text.into();
96	        self
97	    }
98	
99	    /// Sets the case-sensitivity flag.
100	    #[must_use]
101	    pub const fn ignore_case(mut self, value: bool) -> Self {
102	        self.ignore_case = value;
103	        self
104	    }
105	
106	    /// Sets the match strategy.
107	    #[must_use]
108	    pub const fn match_strategy(mut self, value: MatchStrategy) -> Self {
109	        self.match_strategy = value;
110	        self
111	    }
112	}
113	
114	/// The strategy used to match the query against the text.
115	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
116	pub enum MatchStrategy {
117	    /// Highlight every occurrence of the query within the text. The default
118	    /// — the most permissive strategy, matching Ark UI's default.
119	    #[default]
120	    Contains,
121	
122	    /// Highlight only the leading run of the text when it starts with the
123	    /// query (after case folding, if `ignore_case` is `true`).
124	    StartsWith,
125	
126	    /// Subsequence match: highlight each individual query character within
127	    /// the text in order, allowing arbitrary gaps.
128	    ///
129	    /// All query characters must be present (in order, not necessarily
130	    /// contiguous). When the full subsequence is found, each matched
131	    /// character contributes its own one-char highlighted range. When any
132	    /// query character cannot be located, **no fuzzy ranges are emitted
133	    /// for that query** (all-or-nothing) — partial matches would highlight
134	    /// characters that don't represent the query and confuse the user.
135	    Fuzzy,
136	}
137	
138	/// One contiguous run of the original text, tagged as highlighted or not.
139	///
140	/// `text` borrows from [`Props::text`] (the lifetime is tied to the props
141	/// passed to [`highlight_chunks`] / [`Api::chunks`]); the chunk vector is
142	/// owned by the caller. Adapters render highlighted chunks as `<mark>` and
143	/// non-highlighted chunks as `<span>` per the component anatomy.
144	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
145	pub struct HighlightChunk<'a> {
146	    /// The slice of the source text covered by this chunk.
147	    pub text: &'a str,
148	
149	    /// Whether the adapter should wrap this chunk in `<mark>`.
150	    pub highlighted: bool,
151	}
152	
153	/// DOM parts of the `Highlight` component.
154	///
155	/// Only [`Part::Root`] is a static anatomy slot. The per-chunk
156	/// `<mark>` / `<span>` elements are emitted dynamically per
157	/// [`HighlightChunk`], parametric on the runtime `highlighted` boolean — a
158	/// value that [`ConnectApi::part_attrs`] (which takes a `Part` by value, no
159	/// payload) cannot express. Adapters call [`Api::chunk_attrs`] per chunk
160	/// instead. See `spec/components/utility/highlight.md` §2 for the rendered
161	/// shape.
162	#[derive(ComponentPart)]
163	#[scope = "highlight"]
164	pub enum Part {
165	    /// The root `<span>` that wraps the chunk children.
166	    Root,
167	}
168	
169	/// Attribute-mapper API for the `Highlight` component.
170	///
171	/// Constructed via [`Api::new`] from [`Props`] and queried via
172	/// [`Api::root_attrs`] / [`Api::chunk_attrs`] for adapter-rendered DOM
173	/// attributes, or [`Api::chunks`] / the standalone [`highlight_chunks`]
174	/// function for the chunk sequence itself.
175	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
176	pub struct Api {
177	    props: Props,
178	}
179	
180	impl Api {
181	    /// Wraps the given props in an `Api`. The props are stored verbatim and
182	    /// can be read back via [`Api::props`] or the typed accessors.
183	    #[must_use]
184	    pub const fn new(props: Props) -> Self {
185	        Self { props }
186	    }
187	
188	    /// Returns a reference to the underlying [`Props`].
189	    #[must_use]
190	    pub const fn props(&self) -> &Props {
191	        &self.props
192	    }
193	
194	    /// Returns the configured query list.
195	    #[must_use]
196	    pub fn query(&self) -> &[String] {
197	        &self.props.query
198	    }
199	
200	    /// Returns the configured source text.
201	    #[must_use]
202	    pub fn text(&self) -> &str {
203	        &self.props.text
204	    }
205	
206	    /// Returns whether matching is case-insensitive.
207	    #[must_use]
208	    pub const fn ignore_case(&self) -> bool {
209	        self.props.ignore_case
210	    }
211	
212	    /// Returns the configured match strategy.
213	    #[must_use]
214	    pub const fn match_strategy(&self) -> MatchStrategy {
215	        self.props.match_strategy
216	    }
217	
218	    /// Attributes for the root `<span>` wrapper.
219	    ///
220	    /// Emits `data-ars-scope="highlight"` + `data-ars-part="root"` (via
221	    /// `Part::Root.data_attrs()`) plus `dir="auto"` so the browser picks
222	    /// the correct `BiDi` paragraph direction from the first strong character
223	    /// in the highlighted text (see spec §3.2). No ARIA attributes — the
224	    /// semantic `<mark>` elements in the chunk children carry the
225	    /// highlighting semantics for assistive technology.
226	    #[must_use]
227	    pub fn root_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
228	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
229	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();
230	
231	        attrs
232	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
233	            .set(part_attr, part_val)
234	            .set(HtmlAttr::Dir, "auto");
235	
236	        attrs
237	    }
238	
239	    /// Attributes for one chunk element.
240	    ///
241	    /// Emits `data-ars-part="highlight-chunk"` and
242	    /// `data-ars-highlighted="true"|"false"` per `highlighted`. The
243	    /// underlying element (`<mark>` vs `<span>`) is chosen by the adapter
244	    /// based on the same boolean.
245	    #[must_use]
246	    pub fn chunk_attrs(&self, highlighted: bool) -> AttrMap {
247	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
248	
249	        attrs
250	            .set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-part"), "highlight-chunk")
251	            .set(
252	                HtmlAttr::Data("ars-highlighted"),
253	                if highlighted { "true" } else { "false" },
254	            );
255	
256	        attrs
257	    }
258	
259	    /// Computes the chunk sequence for the configured props at the given
260	    /// locale. Thin convenience around [`highlight_chunks`] — the standalone
261	    /// function takes the same arguments and is the spec-defined entry point.
262	    #[must_use]
263	    pub fn chunks<'a>(&'a self, locale: &Locale) -> Vec<HighlightChunk<'a>> {
264	        highlight_chunks(&self.props, locale)
265	    }
266	}
267	
268	impl ConnectApi for Api {
269	    type Part = Part;
270	
271	    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Part) -> AttrMap {
272	        match part {
273	            Part::Root => self.root_attrs(),
274	        }
275	    }
276	}
277	
278	/// Splits the configured text into alternating highlighted / non-highlighted
279	/// chunks under the given locale.
280	///
281	/// # Examples
282	///
283	/// ```
284	/// use ars_components::utility::highlight::{highlight_chunks, HighlightChunk, Props};
285	/// use ars_i18n::Locale;
286	///
287	/// let props = Props::new().query(["world"]).text("Hello world!");
288	/// let locale = Locale::parse("en-US").expect("en-US must parse");
289	///
290	/// let chunks = highlight_chunks(&props, &locale);
291	///
292	/// assert_eq!(
293	///     chunks,
294	///     vec![
295	///         HighlightChunk { text: "Hello ", highlighted: false },
296	///         HighlightChunk { text: "world", highlighted: true },
297	///         HighlightChunk { text: "!", highlighted: false },
298	///     ]
299	/// );
300	/// ```

{\n        <Landmark id=\"search\" role=Role::Search messages=messages(\"Site search\")>\n            \"form\"\n        </Landmark>\n    }.to_html();\n    assert!(html.trim_start().starts_with(\"<div\"));\n    assert!(html.contains(r#\"role=\"search\"\"#));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn landmark_labelledby_takes_precedence_over_aria_label() {\n    let html = view! {\n        <Landmark id=\"r\" role=Role::Region labelledby_id=\"ext\" messages=messages(\"ignored\")>\n            \"x\"\n        </Landmark>\n    }.to_html();\n    assert!(html.contains(r#\"aria-labelledby=\"ext\"\"#));\n    assert!(!html.contains(r#\"aria-label=\"ignored\"\"#), \"labelledby must suppress aria-label: {html}\");\n}\n\n// Repeat one test per native role (Banner→header, Main→main, Complementary→aside,\n// ContentInfo→footer, Form→form, Region→section) — assert tag, data-ars-scope, and\n// either aria-label or absence-of-aria-label-when-missing.\n```\n\n### SSR tests — Highlight (`crates/ars-leptos/tests/highlight.rs`)\n\n```rust\n#![cfg(all(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"), feature = \"ssr\"))]\nuse ars_leptos::utility::highlight::{Highlight, MatchStrategy};\nuse leptos::prelude::*;\n\n#[test]\nfn highlight_wraps_match_in_mark() {\n    let html = view! {\n        <Highlight query=vec![\"world\".into()] text=\"Hello world!\".into() />\n    }.to_html();\n    for f in [\n        r#\"data-ars-scope=\"highlight\"\"#,\n        r#\"data-ars-part=\"root\"\"#,\n        r#\"dir=\"auto\"\"#,\n        r#\"<mark\"#,\n        r#\"data-ars-part=\"highlight-chunk\"\"#,\n        r#\"data-ars-highlighted=\"true\"\"#,\n        \">world<\",\n    ] {\n        assert!(html.contains(f), \"missing {f}: {html}\");\n    }\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn highlight_non_matched_chunks_use_span() {\n    let html = view! {\n        <Highlight query=vec![\"world\".into()] text=\"Hello world!\".into() />\n    }.to_html();\n    assert!(html.contains(r#\"data-ars-highlighted=\"false\"\"#));\n    assert!(html.matches(\"<span\").count() >= 2, \"should contain root span + unmatched chunk spans: {html}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn highlight_empty_query_renders_single_unmatched_chunk() {\n    let html = view! { <Highlight query=Vec::<String>::new() text=\"Hello\".into() /> }.to_html();\n    assert!(!html.contains(\"<mark\"));\n    assert!(html.contains(\"Hello\"));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn highlight_ignore_case_default_matches_uppercase_query() {\n    let html = view! {\n        <Highlight query=vec![\"WORLD\".into()] text=\"Hello world!\".into() />\n    }.to_html();\n    assert!(html.contains(\"<mark\"), \"case-insensitive match expected: {html}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn highlight_starts_with_strategy_only_matches_prefix() {\n    let html = view! {\n        <Highlight\n            query=vec![\"world\".into()]\n            text=\"Hello world!\".into()\n            match_strategy=MatchStrategy::StartsWith\n        />\n    }.to_html();\n    // \"world\" is not a prefix of \"Hello world!\", so no <mark>.\n    assert!(!html.contains(\"<mark\"), \"StartsWith should not match mid-string: {html}\");\n}\n```\n\n### Wasm tests (Leptos)\n\n`heading_wasm.rs`, `landmark_wasm.rs`, `highlight_wasm.rs` — mount each component into a real DOM and assert the rendered element's attributes / tag name match the SSR output. Use the existing harness pattern from `crates/ars-leptos/tests/visually_hidden_wasm.rs` (read once to confirm; mount with `mount_to_body(|| view! { … })` and query via `web_sys::window().document().query_selector(…)`). Three tests per file covers the SSR-hydration-stability acceptance criterion (matches separator/visually_hidden precedent).\n\n### Dioxus tests\n\nUse the helper convention from `crates/ars-dioxus/tests/visually_hidden.rs`:\n\n```rust\nfn render_app(app: fn() -> Element) -> String {\n    let mut vdom = VirtualDom::new(app);\n    vdom.rebuild_in_place();\n    dioxus_ssr::render(&vdom)\n}\n```\n\nMirror the Leptos SSR test list, adapted to Dioxus rsx syntax (`Heading { id: \"title\", \"Hello\" }` etc.). Same wasm-test scope using `crates/ars-dioxus/tests/visually_hidden_wasm.rs` as the template.\n\n## Step-by-Step Execution Order\n\nRecommend executing per-component in this sequence to keep the diff reviewable and tests green at every commit. Each \"phase\" maps to one TDD cycle (red → green → refactor → commit) — every commit must `cargo check -p <crate>` clean.\n\n1. **Phase A — Leptos Heading + providers** (issue #324, half-scope)\n   1. Add module + prelude wiring stubs (`pub mod heading;` + tuple update) so the test files compile against re-exports.\n   2. Write `tests/heading.rs` (SSR) — 7 tests as above. Run `cargo test -p ars-leptos --features ssr heading`. Confirm tests FAIL.\n   3. Implement `src/utility/heading.rs` (Heading + HeadingLevelProvider + Section). Run the test command again — all pass.\n   4. Write `tests/heading_wasm.rs` (3 wasm tests). Run `cargo test -p ars-leptos --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features web heading_wasm`. Pass.\n   5. Commit message: `feat(leptos): add Heading, HeadingLevelProvider, Section adapters (#324)`. **No commit yet — wait for the user's approval per workspace convention.**\n\n2. **Phase B — Leptos Landmark** (issue #324, half-scope)\n   1. Add `pub mod landmark;` + prelude.\n   2. Write `tests/landmark.rs` (SSR; one assertion per role + labelledby precedence + missing-name fallback). Confirm FAIL.\n   3. Implement `src/utility/landmark.rs`. Pass.\n   4. Write `tests/landmark_wasm.rs`.\n\n3. **Phase C — Leptos Highlight** (issue #328)\n   1. Add `pub mod highlight;` + prelude.\n   2. Write `tests/highlight.rs` (SSR; matches, non-matches, empty query, ignore_case, StartsWith). Confirm FAIL.\n   3. Implement `src/utility/highlight.rs`. Pass.\n   4. Write `tests/highlight_wasm.rs`.\n\n4. **Phase D — Dioxus Heading + providers** (issue #419, half-scope)\n5. **Phase E — Dioxus Landmark** (issue #419, half-scope)\n6. **Phase F — Dioxus Highlight** (issue #421)\n\nPhases D-F mirror A-C 1:1 with Dioxus syntax.\n\n7. **Phase G — Post-implementation audit (MANDATORY)** — Invoke the `post-implementation-audit` skill (CLAUDE.md §7) on the six new component files + their test files. Run all three audits sequentially:\n   - **a)** spec/implementation drift against the six adapter spec files in `spec/leptos-components/utility/` and `spec/dioxus-components/utility/`,\n   - **b)** ≥ 2 rounds of \"anything else missing?\",\n   - **c)** test-coverage audit for unit/snapshot/proptest/spec-conformance/llvm-cov.\n   - Every finding lands in this PR — no deferral.\n\n8. **Phase H — Validation (run sequentially, each must be green)**\n   - `cargo test -p ars-leptos --features ssr` — SSR tests pass.\n   - `cargo test -p ars-leptos --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features web` — wasm tests pass (requires `wasm-pack` if not already installed via `cargo install wasm-pack --version 0.13.1`; matches the `a11y-audit` job convention).\n   - `cargo test -p ars-dioxus` — SSR + native tests pass.\n   - `cargo test -p ars-dioxus --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --features web` — wasm tests pass.\n   - `cargo xci --profile fast` (alias `cargo xci-fast`) from repo root — covers fmt, clippy, unit, integration, adapter, spec-compile-snippets, error-variant-coverage, mutual-exclusion, snapshot-count. **Must pass before pushing.**\n\n9. **Phase I — Commit + push (only after user approval)** — Single commit with co-author footer, then `gh pr create` targeting `main` with body including `Closes #324`, `Closes #328`, `Closes #419`, `Closes #421`. No snapshot files are expected from this work, but if any `.snap` files appear, add the `snapshot-reviewed` label.\n\n10. **Phase J — Wait for Codex review (MANDATORY)** — Invoke the `waiting-for-codex-review` skill, address any threads with the same rigor as `post-implementation-audit`, repush, re-comment `@codex review`, loop until Codex leaves 👍.\n\n## Verification End-to-End\n\nAfter Phase H is green, run the following spot-checks before declaring the work ready for user review:\n\n```bash\n# 1. Spec snippets compile (every code block in spec/leptos-components/utility/{heading,landmark,highlight}.md and the Dioxus equivalents).\ncargo test -p xtask spec_compile_snippets\n\n# 2. Per-crate coverage threshold check on ars-leptos and ars-dioxus.\ncargo llvm-cov --workspace \\\n  --exclude ars-leptos --exclude ars-dioxus \\\n  --exclude ars-test-harness-leptos --exclude ars-test-harness-dioxus \\\n  --exclude ars-derive --exclude xtask \\\n  --lcov --output-path lcov.info\n# (Adapter coverage lands via the CI wasm-coverage job — locally we just confirm native lcov merges and the existing thresholds still pass.)\n\n# 3. Browse the rendered components in a dev shell (manual smoke test) — use one of the\n#    existing harness binaries or hand-write a tiny example app under `examples/` if needed.\n#    Not strictly required for stateless utilities since SSR + wasm tests already assert\n#    the rendered output, but recommended as a final sanity pass.\n\n# 4. Confirm no public items lack docs and there are no clippy warnings.\ncargo clippy -p ars-leptos --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings\ncargo clippy -p ars-dioxus --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings\n```\n\nExpected outcomes:\n- All `cargo test` invocations report **0 failed**.\n- `cargo xci-fast` exits 0.\n- `cargo clippy` exits 0 (workspace policy: zero warnings).\n- `spec compile snippets` exits 0 (the canonical implementation sketches in the adapter specs already compile against the agnostic core; nothing new is needed there).\n\n## Risks / Edge Cases to Watch\n\n- **Locale signal mid-life updates** — Leptos `use_locale()` returns a signal; `Landmark::Api::new(props, env, messages)` snapshots the locale once. If the user changes locale post-mount, the rendered `aria-label` will not update unless we move the `Api` construction into a `Memo`. For this PR's scope (stateless utility, parity with the canonical sketches), one-shot construction is correct per spec §7 \"render-time only, no post-mount sync expected\". If a downstream component needs reactive locale, we revisit then — not now.\n- **Heading context default** — When `use_context::<HeadingContext>()` returns `None`, default to `HeadingContext::new()` (Level::One). Do NOT panic.\n- **Highlight chunk borrow** — `Api::chunks(&locale)` returns chunks borrowing from `props.text`. The current `props` lives inside the function; clone each `chunk.text` to an owned `String` before constructing the view (cheap — most chunks are short and we are not in a hot path).\n- **Dioxus rsx returns under `match`** — Dioxus 0.7 supports returning `rsx! { … }` from each arm directly as `Element`. No need for unifying types.\n- **Locale type asymmetry** — `ars_leptos::use_locale()` returns `Signal<Locale>` (call `.get()` to get the value); `ars_dioxus::use_locale()` returns a `Locale` directly (confirm by reading `crates/ars-dioxus/src/provider.rs` during Phase D and adjust if needed — `feedback_framework_versions.md` warns that adapter helpers diverge).\n- **Search role** — `<search>` is intentionally NOT used; the agnostic core's `prefers_generic_fallback_element()` already signals this; we honor it by rendering `<div role=\"search\">`.\n- **No snapshot files expected** — These adapters render plain HTML attribute strings, so `.to_html()` and `dioxus_ssr::render` assertions use direct string matching. No `insta` fixtures should be created. If any `.snap` files appear in the diff, re-examine — they likely indicate accidental adoption of snapshot tests in adapter crates (those belong in the agnostic core).\n"

  "plan": "# Implement Tasks #324, #328, #419, #421 — Heading / Landmark / Highlight adapters (Leptos + Dioxus)\n\n## Context\n\nFour GitHub issues — all 2-point adapter tasks — need to be implemented:\n\n- **#324** (Leptos): Heading + Landmark adapter components.\n- **#328** (Leptos): Highlight adapter component.\n- **#419** (Dioxus): Heading + Landmark adapter components.\n- **#421** (Dioxus): Highlight adapter component.\n\nAll upstream dependencies are merged:\n\n- #202 (Heading + Landmark agnostic core) — closed.\n- #204 (Highlight agnostic core) — closed.\n- #190 / #193 (Leptos / Dioxus `ArsProvider` + reactive props) — closed.\n- #191 / #194 (Leptos / Dioxus adapter utilities — emit, event mapping, nonce collector, safe listeners) — closed.\n\nWhy this matters: these three utilities are foundational structural primitives (semantic headings, page landmarks, text-match highlight). Without them, downstream components that compose Heading/Landmark/Highlight (Dialog titles, Toast regions, Combobox highlighting, AlertDialog headings) keep accruing TODOs in their adapter specs. Shipping them now unblocks several of the open stateless-utility adapter tasks (#322 Group, #323 Field/Fieldset, #325 keyboard, etc.).\n\n**Per user decision:** one combined PR (closes all four issues), both SSR + wasm tests, and ship `HeadingLevelProvider` + `Section` alongside `Heading` so the spec's \"nested heading-level inheritance must flow through published `HeadingContext`\" invariant is testable end-to-end in this PR.\n\n## Scope\n\nFor each adapter (Leptos + Dioxus), implement:\n\n1. **`heading`** module\n   - `Heading` component — renders `<h1>` … `<h6>` based on resolved level (props override > context > default Level::One). Native heading elements only — no fallback `<div role=\"heading\">` since we can always pick an h-tag.\n   - `HeadingLevelProvider` component — provider-only, publishes a starting `HeadingContext` via framework context.\n   - `Section` component — provider-only, publishes the incremented `HeadingContext` for descendants.\n2. **`landmark`** module\n   - `Landmark` component — renders semantic element per `Role`: `<header>` / `<nav>` / `<main>` / `<aside>` / `<footer>` / `<form>` / `<section>` for non-Search roles, and `<div role=\"search\">` fallback for `Search` (matches `Api::prefers_generic_fallback_element()`). Localized `aria-label` resolved via `use_locale()` + adapter-passed `messages`.\n3. **`highlight`** module\n   - `Highlight` component — renders `<span>` root + iterates `Api::chunks(&locale)`, emitting `<mark>` for highlighted chunks and `<span>` for unmatched. Locale resolved from optional `locale` prop or `use_locale()` provider.\n\nNo `AsChild` variants in this PR — the adapter specs do not call for them on these three utilities (the agnostic Props have no `as_child` field), and the canonical implementation sketches in each spec render the semantic element directly without a render callback.\n\n## File Map\n\nFiles to create:\n\n```\ncrates/ars-leptos/src/utility/heading.rs        (~250 lines)\ncrates/ars-leptos/src/utility/landmark.rs       (~200 lines)\ncrates/ars-leptos/src/utility/highlight.rs      (~180 lines)\ncrates/ars-leptos/tests/heading.rs              (SSR; ~10 tests)\ncrates/ars-leptos/tests/heading_wasm.rs         (wasm; ~3 tests)\ncrates/ars-leptos/tests/landmark.rs             (SSR; ~12 tests)\ncrates/ars-leptos/tests/landmark_wasm.rs        (wasm; ~3 tests)\ncrates/ars-leptos/tests/highlight.rs            (SSR; ~8 tests)\ncrates/ars-leptos/tests/highlight_wasm.rs       (wasm; ~3 tests)\n\ncrates/ars-dioxus/src/utility/heading.rs        (~260 lines)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/src/utility/landmark.rs       (~210 lines)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/src/utility/highlight.rs      (~190 lines)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/tests/heading.rs              (SSR; ~10 tests)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/tests/heading_wasm.rs         (wasm; ~3 tests)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/tests/landmark.rs             (SSR; ~12 tests)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/tests/landmark_wasm.rs        (wasm; ~3 tests)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/tests/highlight.rs            (SSR; ~8 tests)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/tests/highlight_wasm.rs       (wasm; ~3 tests)\n```\n\nFiles to modify:\n\n```\ncrates/ars-leptos/src/utility/mod.rs            (add `pub mod heading; pub mod landmark; pub mod highlight;`)\ncrates/ars-leptos/src/prelude.rs                (add to utility re-export list)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/src/utility/mod.rs            (add same three modules)\ncrates/ars-dioxus/src/prelude.rs                (add to utility re-export list)\n```\n\nNo `Cargo.toml` changes needed — `ars-i18n` (for `Locale`), `ars-components`, and `ars-core` are already dependencies of both adapter crates. The Highlight module is feature-gated `i18n` in `ars-components`; the existing adapter crates already enable that feature.\n\nNo spec changes anticipated — both adapter specs are stable and we are implementing to the documented contract.\n\n## Patterns Reused (Do Not Reinvent)\n\n- `crate::attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs` / `crate::attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs` — convert `AttrMap` to spreadable framework attrs. (Already used by `separator.rs` and `visually_hidden.rs` in both adapters.)\n- `crate::use_locale()` — read the locale from `ArsContext`. Both adapters expose this via `provider.rs`.\n- `provide_context(...)` (Leptos) / `use_context_provider(|| ...)` (Dioxus) — publish `HeadingContext` for descendants.\n- `use_context::<HeadingContext>()` (Leptos) / `try_consume_context::<HeadingContext>()` (Dioxus) — read inherited level, defaulting to `HeadingContext::new()` (Level::One) when absent.\n- `leptos::either::{Either, EitherOf6, EitherOf8}` — fan-out for dynamic Leptos element tags (h1-h6 for Heading, six native + fallback `<div>` for Landmark).\n- `ars_components::utility::{heading, landmark, highlight}::{Api, Part, Props, …}` — agnostic core; re-export from the adapter module so end-users can write `heading::Level::Three`, `landmark::Role::Navigation`, `highlight::MatchStrategy::Contains`, etc.\n- Existing test recipes — Leptos uses `view! { … }.to_html()` for SSR, Dioxus uses `VirtualDom::new(app) + rebuild_in_place() + dioxus_ssr::render(&vdom)` (copy the helper from `tests/visually_hidden.rs`). Wasm tests use `wasm_bindgen_test_configure!(run_in_browser);` and either the existing `ars-test-harness-leptos::render(…)` / `ars-test-harness-dioxus::render(…)` for mount/state, or — for stateless utilities — direct DOM assertions on a manually mounted node.\n\n## Component-by-Component Implementation\n\n### 1. `ars-leptos` — `heading` module\n\nRe-export the agnostic surface and provide three components:\n\n```rust\npub use ars_components::utility::heading::{\n    Api, HeadingContext, Level, Part, Props,\n    heading_level_provider, section,\n};\n\n#[component]\npub fn Heading(\n    #[prop(optional, into)] id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,\n    #[prop(optional)] level: Option<Level>,\n    children: Children,\n) -> impl IntoView {\n    let ctx = use_context::<HeadingContext>().unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut props = Props::new();\n    if let Some(id) = id.as_ref() {\n        props = props.id(id.to_string());\n    }\n    if let Some(level) = level {\n        props = props.level(level);\n    }\n    let api = Api::new(props, ctx);\n    let resolved = api.resolved_level();\n    let attrs = attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs(true));\n\n    match resolved {\n        Level::One   => EitherOf6::A(view! { <h1 {..attrs}>{children()}</h1> }),\n        Level::Two   => EitherOf6::B(view! { <h2 {..attrs}>{children()}</h2> }),\n        Level::Three => EitherOf6::C(view! { <h3 {..attrs}>{children()}</h3> }),\n        Level::Four  => EitherOf6::D(view! { <h4 {..attrs}>{children()}</h4> }),\n        Level::Five  => EitherOf6::E(view! { <h5 {..attrs}>{children()}</h5> }),\n        Level::Six   => EitherOf6::F(view! { <h6 {..attrs}>{children()}</h6> }),\n    }\n}\n\n#[component]\npub fn HeadingLevelProvider(level: Level, children: Children) -> impl IntoView {\n    let provider_props = heading_level_provider::Props::new().level(level);\n    let ctx = heading_level_provider::context_for(&provider_props);\n    provide_context(ctx);\n    children()\n}\n\n#[component]\npub fn Section(children: Children) -> impl IntoView {\n    let parent = use_context::<HeadingContext>().unwrap_or_default();\n    provide_context(section::context_for(&parent));\n    children()\n}\n```\n\nNotes:\n- Heading always passes `is_native_heading_element = true` because we can always emit a real `<h{1..6}>` — there is no need for the `role=\"heading\" aria-level=N` fallback path in a Leptos web adapter.\n- When the user provides no `id`, the core emits `id=\"\"`. Strip the empty id before converting to attrs (mirrors how `separator.rs::root_attrs` handles `id`).\n\n### 2. `ars-leptos` — `landmark` module\n\n```rust\npub use ars_components::utility::landmark::{Api, Messages, Part, Props, Role};\n\n#[component]\npub fn Landmark(\n    #[prop(optional, into)] id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,\n    #[prop(optional)] role: Option<Role>,\n    #[prop(optional, into)] labelledby_id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,\n    #[prop(optional, into)] messages: Option<Messages>,\n    children: Children,\n) -> impl IntoView {\n    let resolved_role = role.unwrap_or(Role::Region);\n    let mut props = Props::new().role(resolved_role);\n    if let Some(id) = id.as_ref() { props = props.id(id.to_string()); }\n    if let Some(lb) = labelledby_id.as_ref() {\n        props = props.labelledby_id(lb.to_string());\n    }\n    let messages = messages.unwrap_or_default();\n    let env = ars_core::Env { locale: use_locale().get(), ..ars_core::Env::default() };\n    let api = Api::new(props, &env, &messages);\n    let is_native = !api.prefers_generic_fallback_element();\n    let attrs = attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs(is_native));\n\n    if !is_native {\n        Either::Left(view! { <div {..attrs}>{children()}</div> })\n    } else {\n        Either::Right(match resolved_role {\n            Role::Banner        => EitherOf7::A(view! { <header  {..attrs}>{children()}</header> }),\n            Role::Navigation    => EitherOf7::B(view! { <nav     {..attrs}>{children()}</nav> }),\n            Role::Main          => EitherOf7::C(view! { <main    {..attrs}>{children()}</main> }),\n            Role::Complementary => EitherOf7::D(view! { <aside   {..attrs}>{children()}</aside> }),\n            Role::ContentInfo   => EitherOf7::E(view! { <footer  {..attrs}>{children()}</footer> }),\n            Role::Form          => EitherOf7::F(view! { <form    {..attrs}>{children()}</form> }),\n            Role::Region        => EitherOf7::G(view! { <section {..attrs}>{children()}</section> }),\n            Role::Search        => unreachable!(\"Search role is handled by prefers_generic_fallback_element()\"),\n        })\n    }\n}\n```\n\nNotes:\n- Locale comes from `use_locale()`. We need the resolved `Locale` value (not the signal) to construct `Env`. The agnostic API stores it eagerly, so non-reactive read is acceptable for the initial implementation. (Locale changes mid-life will not retrigger label resolution — that matches the agnostic-core contract: `Api::new` snapshots the locale at construction.)\n- `messages` defaults to `Messages::default()` (empty label). For the spec's \"Form and Region require accessible name\" path, callers pass `Messages { label: MessageFn::static_str(\"…\") }` or wire `use_messages()`.\n- `is_native_landmark_element` is `false` only when `Api::prefers_generic_fallback_element()` is true (currently only `Role::Search`).\n\n### 3. `ars-leptos` — `highlight` module\n\n```rust\npub use ars_components::utility::highlight::{\n    Api, HighlightChunk, MatchStrategy, Part, Props,\n};\n\n#[component]\npub fn Highlight(\n    #[prop(optional, into)] query: Vec<String>,\n    #[prop(optional, into)] text: String,\n    #[prop(optional)] ignore_case: Option<bool>,\n    #[prop(optional)] match_strategy: Option<MatchStrategy>,\n    #[prop(optional)] locale: Option<Locale>,\n) -> impl IntoView {\n    let props = Props::new()\n        .query(query)\n        .text(text)\n        .ignore_case(ignore_case.unwrap_or(true))\n        .match_strategy(match_strategy.unwrap_or_default());\n    let api = Api::new(props);\n    let locale = locale.unwrap_or_else(|| use_locale().get());\n\n    let root_attrs = attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs());\n    let chunks = api.chunks(&locale)\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|chunk| {\n            let chunk_attrs = attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(api.chunk_attrs(chunk.highlighted));\n            let text = chunk.text.to_string();\n            if chunk.highlighted {\n                Either::Left(view! { <mark {..chunk_attrs}>{text}</mark> })\n            } else {\n                Either::Right(view! { <span {..chunk_attrs}>{text}</span> })\n            }\n        })\n        .collect_view();\n\n    view! { <span {..root_attrs}>{chunks}</span> }\n}\n```\n\nNotes:\n- `api.chunks(&locale)` returns chunks borrowing from `props.text`. We own `props` inside the call so the chunks live long enough; copy each `chunk.text` into an owned `String` before constructing the view.\n- The root `dir=\"auto\"` comes from `api.root_attrs()` already — do not duplicate.\n\n### 4-6. `ars-dioxus` — Same three modules\n\nDioxus is structurally identical, with these differences:\n\n- Use **explicit `#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]` structs** for every component (workspace convention; see `feedback_dioxus_explicit_props.md`).\n- Use **`try_use_context::<HeadingContext>()`** to read inherited context (returns `Option<HeadingContext>`; matches the convention used throughout `crates/ars-dioxus/src/provider.rs`, `nonce.rs`, and `platform.rs`).\n- Use `use_context_provider(|| ctx)` for publishing context.\n- Match arms return `rsx! { … }` directly — Dioxus's `Element` is the universal return type, no `EitherOf*` needed.\n- Read locale via the existing `crate::use_locale()` helper. Both `ars_leptos::use_locale()` and `ars_dioxus::use_locale()` return `Signal<Locale>`. Read the current value with `.get()` (Leptos) or `.read().clone()` (Dioxus) — see `crates/ars-dioxus/src/provider.rs:418` for the canonical \"use prop if present, else snapshot from signal\" pattern.\n\nHeading skeleton:\n\n```rust\n#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct HeadingProps {\n    #[props(optional, into)] pub id: Option<String>,\n    #[props(optional)]       pub level: Option<Level>,\n    pub children: Element,\n}\n\n#[component]\npub fn Heading(props: HeadingProps) -> Element {\n    let ctx = try_use_context::<HeadingContext>().unwrap_or_default();\n    let mut core_props = Props::new();\n    if let Some(id) = props.id.as_deref() { core_props = core_props.id(id); }\n    if let Some(level) = props.level     { core_props = core_props.level(level); }\n    let api = Api::new(core_props, ctx);\n    let attrs = attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs(true));\n    let children = props.children;\n\n    match api.resolved_level() {\n        Level::One   => rsx! { h1 { ..attrs, {children} } },\n        Level::Two   => rsx! { h2 { ..attrs, {children} } },\n        Level::Three => rsx! { h3 { ..attrs, {children} } },\n        Level::Four  => rsx! { h4 { ..attrs, {children} } },\n        Level::Five  => rsx! { h5 { ..attrs, {children} } },\n        Level::Six   => rsx! { h6 { ..attrs, {children} } },\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct HeadingLevelProviderProps {\n    pub level: Level,\n    pub children: Element,\n}\n\n#[component]\npub fn HeadingLevelProvider(props: HeadingLevelProviderProps) -> Element {\n    let provider_props = heading_level_provider::Props::new().level(props.level);\n    use_context_provider(|| heading_level_provider::context_for(&provider_props));\n    rsx! { {props.children} }\n}\n\n#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]\npub struct SectionProps { pub children: Element }\n\n#[component]\npub fn Section(props: SectionProps) -> Element {\n    let parent = try_use_context::<HeadingContext>().unwrap_or_default();\n    use_context_provider(|| section::context_for(&parent));\n    rsx! # Implement Tasks #324, #328, #419, #421 — Heading / Landmark / Highlight adapters (Leptos + Dioxus)

## Context

Four GitHub issues — all 2-point adapter tasks — need to be implemented:

- **#324** (Leptos): Heading + Landmark adapter components.
- **#328** (Leptos): Highlight adapter component.
- **#419** (Dioxus): Heading + Landmark adapter components.
- **#421** (Dioxus): Highlight adapter component.

All upstream dependencies are merged:

- #202 (Heading + Landmark agnostic core) — closed.
- #204 (Highlight agnostic core) — closed.
- #190 / #193 (Leptos / Dioxus `ArsProvider` + reactive props) — closed.
- #191 / #194 (Leptos / Dioxus adapter utilities — emit, event mapping, nonce collector, safe listeners) — closed.

Why this matters: these three utilities are foundational structural primitives (semantic headings, page landmarks, text-match highlight). Without them, downstream components that compose Heading/Landmark/Highlight (Dialog titles, Toast regions, Combobox highlighting, AlertDialog headings) keep accruing TODOs in their adapter specs. Shipping them now unblocks several of the open stateless-utility adapter tasks (#322 Group, #323 Field/Fieldset, #325 keyboard, etc.).

**Per user decision:** one combined PR (closes all four issues), both SSR + wasm tests, and ship `HeadingLevelProvider` + `Section` alongside `Heading` so the spec's "nested heading-level inheritance must flow through published `HeadingContext`" invariant is testable end-to-end in this PR.

## Scope

For each adapter (Leptos + Dioxus), implement:

1. **`heading`** module
   - `Heading` component — renders `<h1>` … `<h6>` based on resolved level (props override > context > default Level::One). Native heading elements only — no fallback `<div role="heading">` since we can always pick an h-tag.
   - `HeadingLevelProvider` component — provider-only, publishes a starting `HeadingContext` via framework context.
   - `Section` component — provider-only, publishes the incremented `HeadingContext` for descendants.
2. **`landmark`** module
   - `Landmark` component — renders semantic element per `Role`: `<header>` / `<nav>` / `<main>` / `<aside>` / `<footer>` / `<form>` / `<section>` for non-Search roles, and `<div role="search">` fallback for `Search` (matches `Api::prefers_generic_fallback_element()`). Localized `aria-label` resolved via `use_locale()` + adapter-passed `messages`.
3. **`highlight`** module
   - `Highlight` component — renders `<span>` root + iterates `Api::chunks(&locale)`, emitting `<mark>` for highlighted chunks and `<span>` for unmatched. Locale resolved from optional `locale` prop or `use_locale()` provider.

No `AsChild` variants in this PR — the adapter specs do not call for them on these three utilities (the agnostic Props have no `as_child` field), and the canonical implementation sketches in each spec render the semantic element directly without a render callback.

## Patterns Reused (Do Not Reinvent)

- `crate::attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs` / `crate::attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs` — convert `AttrMap` to spreadable framework attrs. (Already used by `separator.rs` and `visually_hidden.rs` in both adapters.)
- `crate::use_locale()` — read the locale from `ArsContext`. Both adapters expose this via `provider.rs`.
- `provide_context(...)` (Leptos) / `use_context_provider(|| ...)` (Dioxus) — publish `HeadingContext` for descendants.
- `use_context::<HeadingContext>()` (Leptos) / `try_consume_context::<HeadingContext>()` (Dioxus) — read inherited level, defaulting to `HeadingContext::new()` (Level::One) when absent.
- `leptos::either::{Either, EitherOf6, EitherOf8}` — fan-out for dynamic Leptos element tags (h1-h6 for Heading, six native + fallback `<div>` for Landmark).
- `ars_components::utility::{heading, landmark, highlight}::{Api, Part, Props, …}` — agnostic core; re-export from the adapter module so end-users can write `heading::Level::Three`, `landmark::Role::Navigation`, `highlight::MatchStrategy::Contains`, etc.
- Existing test recipes — Leptos uses `view! { … }.to_html()` for SSR, Dioxus uses `VirtualDom::new(app) + rebuild_in_place() + dioxus_ssr::render(&vdom)` (copy the helper from `tests/visually_hidden.rs`). Wasm tests use `wasm_bindgen_test_configure!(run_in_browser);` and either the existing `ars-test-harness-leptos::render(…)` / `ars-test-harness-dioxus::render(…)` for mount/state, or — for stateless utilities — direct DOM assertions on a manually mounted node.

## Component-by-Component Implementation

### 1. `ars-leptos` — `heading` module

Re-export the agnostic surface and provide three components:

```rust
pub use ars_components::utility::heading::{
    Api, HeadingContext, Level, Part, Props,
    heading_level_provider, section,
};

#[component]
pub fn Heading(
    #[prop(optional, into)] id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,
    #[prop(optional)] level: Option<Level>,
    children: Children,
) -> impl IntoView {
    let ctx = use_context::<HeadingContext>().unwrap_or_default();
    let mut props = Props::new();
    if let Some(id) = id.as_ref() {
        props = props.id(id.to_string());
    }
    if let Some(level) = level {
        props = props.level(level);
    }
    let api = Api::new(props, ctx);
    let resolved = api.resolved_level();
    let attrs = attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs(true));

    match resolved {
        Level::One   => EitherOf6::A(view! { <h1 {..attrs}>{children()}</h1> }),
        Level::Two   => EitherOf6::B(view! { <h2 {..attrs}>{children()}</h2> }),
        Level::Three => EitherOf6::C(view! { <h3 {..attrs}>{children()}</h3> }),
        Level::Four  => EitherOf6::D(view! { <h4 {..attrs}>{children()}</h4> }),
        Level::Five  => EitherOf6::E(view! { <h5 {..attrs}>{children()}</h5> }),
        Level::Six   => EitherOf6::F(view! { <h6 {..attrs}>{children()}</h6> }),
    }
}

#[component]
pub fn HeadingLevelProvider(level: Level, children: Children) -> impl IntoView {
    let provider_props = heading_level_provider::Props::new().level(level);
    let ctx = heading_level_provider::context_for(&provider_props);
    provide_context(ctx);
    children()
}

#[component]
pub fn Section(children: Children) -> impl IntoView {
    let parent = use_context::<HeadingContext>().unwrap_or_default();
    provide_context(section::context_for(&parent));
    children()
}
```

Notes:
- Heading always passes `is_native_heading_element = true` because we can always emit a real `<h{1..6}>` — there is no need for the `role="heading" aria-level=N` fallback path in a Leptos web adapter.
- When the user provides no `id`, the core emits `id=""`. Strip the empty id before converting to attrs (mirrors how `separator.rs::root_attrs` handles `id`).

### 2. `ars-leptos` — `landmark` module

```rust
pub use ars_components::utility::landmark::{Api, Messages, Part, Props, Role};

#[component]
pub fn Landmark(
    #[prop(optional, into)] id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,
    #[prop(optional)] role: Option<Role>,
    #[prop(optional, into)] labelledby_id: Option<Oco<'static, str>>,
    #[prop(optional, into)] messages: Option<Messages>,
    children: Children,
) -> impl IntoView {
    let resolved_role = role.unwrap_or(Role::Region);
    let mut props = Props::new().role(resolved_role);
    if let Some(id) = id.as_ref() { props = props.id(id.to_string()); }
    if let Some(lb) = labelledby_id.as_ref() {
        props = props.labelledby_id(lb.to_string());
    }
    let messages = messages.unwrap_or_default();
    let env = ars_core::Env { locale: use_locale().get(), ..ars_core::Env::default() };
    let api = Api::new(props, &env, &messages);
    let is_native = !api.prefers_generic_fallback_element();
    let attrs = attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs(is_native));

    if !is_native {
        Either::Left(view! { <div {..attrs}>{children()}</div> })
    } else {
        Either::Right(match resolved_role {
            Role::Banner        => EitherOf7::A(view! { <header  {..attrs}>{children()}</header> }),
            Role::Navigation    => EitherOf7::B(view! { <nav     {..attrs}>{children()}</nav> }),
            Role::Main          => EitherOf7::C(view! { <main    {..attrs}>{children()}</main> }),
            Role::Complementary => EitherOf7::D(view! { <aside   {..attrs}>{children()}</aside> }),
            Role::ContentInfo   => EitherOf7::E(view! { <footer  {..attrs}>{children()}</footer> }),
            Role::Form          => EitherOf7::F(view! { <form    {..attrs}>{children()}</form> }),
            Role::Region        => EitherOf7::G(view! { <section {..attrs}>{children()}</section> }),
            Role::Search        => unreachable!("Search role is handled by prefers_generic_fallback_element()"),
        })
    }
}
```

Notes:
- Locale comes from `use_locale()`. We need the resolved `Locale` value (not the signal) to construct `Env`. The agnostic API stores it eagerly, so non-reactive read is acceptable for the initial implementation. (Locale changes mid-life will not retrigger label resolution — that matches the agnostic-core contract: `Api::new` snapshots the locale at construction.)
- `messages` defaults to `Messages::default()` (empty label). For the spec's "Form and Region require accessible name" path, callers pass `Messages { label: MessageFn::static_str("…") }` or wire `use_messages()`.
- `is_native_landmark_element` is `false` only when `Api::prefers_generic_fallback_element()` is true (currently only `Role::Search`).

### 3. `ars-leptos` — `highlight` module

```rust
pub use ars_components::utility::highlight::{
    Api, HighlightChunk, MatchStrategy, Part, Props,
};

#[component]
pub fn Highlight(
    #[prop(optional, into)] query: Vec<String>,
    #[prop(optional, into)] text: String,
    #[prop(optional)] ignore_case: Option<bool>,
    #[prop(optional)] match_strategy: Option<MatchStrategy>,
    #[prop(optional)] locale: Option<Locale>,
) -> impl IntoView {
    let props = Props::new()
        .query(query)
        .text(text)
        .ignore_case(ignore_case.unwrap_or(true))
        .match_strategy(match_strategy.unwrap_or_default());
    let api = Api::new(props);
    let locale = locale.unwrap_or_else(|| use_locale().get());

    let root_attrs = attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs());
    let chunks = api.chunks(&locale)
        .into_iter()
        .map(|chunk| {
            let chunk_attrs = attr_map_to_leptos_inline_attrs(api.chunk_attrs(chunk.highlighted));
            let text = chunk.text.to_string();
            if chunk.highlighted {
                Either::Left(view! { <mark {..chunk_attrs}>{text}</mark> })
            } else {
                Either::Right(view! { <span {..chunk_attrs}>{text}</span> })
            }
        })
        .collect_view();

    view! { <span {..root_attrs}>{chunks}</span> }
}
```

Notes:
- `api.chunks(&locale)` returns chunks borrowing from `props.text`. We own `props` inside the call so the chunks live long enough; copy each `chunk.text` into an owned `String` before constructing the view.
- The root `dir="auto"` comes from `api.root_attrs()` already — do not duplicate.

### 4-6. `ars-dioxus` — Same three modules

Dioxus is structurally identical, with these differences:

- Use **explicit `#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]` structs** for every component (workspace convention; see `feedback_dioxus_explicit_props.md`).
- Use **`try_use_context::<HeadingContext>()`** to read inherited context (returns `Option<HeadingContext>`; matches the convention used throughout `crates/ars-dioxus/src/provider.rs`, `nonce.rs`, and `platform.rs`).
- Use `use_context_provider(|| ctx)` for publishing context.
- Match arms return `rsx! { … }` directly — Dioxus's `Element` is the universal return type, no `EitherOf*` needed.
- Read locale via the existing `crate::use_locale()` helper. Both `ars_leptos::use_locale()` and `ars_dioxus::use_locale()` return `Signal<Locale>`. Read the current value with `.get()` (Leptos) or `.read().clone()` (Dioxus) — see `crates/ars-dioxus/src/provider.rs:418` for the canonical "use prop if present, else snapshot from signal" pattern.

Heading skeleton:

```rust
#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct HeadingProps {
    #[props(optional, into)] pub id: Option<String>,
    #[props(optional)]       pub level: Option<Level>,
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn Heading(props: HeadingProps) -> Element {
    let ctx = try_use_context::<HeadingContext>().unwrap_or_default();
    let mut core_props = Props::new();
    if let Some(id) = props.id.as_deref() { core_props = core_props.id(id); }
    if let Some(level) = props.level     { core_props = core_props.level(level); }
    let api = Api::new(core_props, ctx);
    let attrs = attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs(true));
    let children = props.children;

    match api.resolved_level() {
        Level::One   => rsx! { h1 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Two   => rsx! { h2 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Three => rsx! { h3 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Four  => rsx! { h4 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Five  => rsx! { h5 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Six   => rsx! { h6 { ..attrs, {children} } },
    }
}

#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct HeadingLevelProviderProps {
    pub level: Level,
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
pub fn HeadingLevelProvider(props: HeadingLevelProviderProps) -> Element {
    let provider_props = heading_level_provider::Props::new().level(props.level);
    use_context_provider(|| heading_level_provider::context_for(&provider_props));
    rsx! { {props.children} }
}

#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct SectionProps { pub children: Element }

#[component]
pub fn Section(props: SectionProps) -> Element {
    let parent = try_use_context::<HeadingContext>().unwrap_or_default();
    use_context_provider(|| section::context_for(&parent));
    rsx! { {props.children} }
}
```

Landmark/Highlight follow the same Leptos shape with Dioxus syntax. See the visually_hidden.rs / separator.rs Dioxus modules for the explicit-Props convention and `attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs` usage.
