1	# Adapter Component Delivery Workflow
2	
3	This document defines the end-to-end workflow for implementing adapter-level
4	components. It exists so agents can deliver a component without rediscovering
5	the surrounding obligations every time.
6	
7	Use this workflow for any issue that adds or materially changes a component in
8	`crates/ars-leptos` or `crates/ars-dioxus`.
9	
10	## Source Of Truth
11	
12	Start from the assigned GitHub issue, not from an epic. The issue acceptance
13	criteria define the delivery scope.
14	
15	Before editing code, read:
16	
17	- the framework-agnostic component spec under `spec/components/<category>/`;
18	- the matching adapter spec under `spec/leptos-components/<category>/` or
19	  `spec/dioxus-components/<category>/`;
20	- the relevant adapter foundation spec:
21	  `spec/foundation/08-adapter-leptos.md` or
22	  `spec/foundation/09-adapter-dioxus.md`;
23	- `docs/implementation/adapter-contract.md`;
24	- `examples/widgets-ownership.md`.
25	
26	When touching Leptos or Dioxus code or specs, load the repo skill for that
27	framework before relying on framework APIs.
28	
29	## Required Deliverables
30	
31	An adapter component task is not complete when only the adapter component
32	compiles. It must update every surface that consumers, tests, and reviewers use.
33	
34	For each implemented component, include the applicable items below in the same
35	PR.
36	
37	### Adapter Crate
38	
39	- Add or update the component implementation in
40	  `crates/ars-leptos/src/<category>/<component>.rs` or
41	  `crates/ars-dioxus/src/<category>/<component>.rs`.
42	- Add the module to the category `mod.rs`.
43	- Re-export the component through `crates/ars-leptos/src/prelude.rs` or
44	  `crates/ars-dioxus/src/prelude.rs` when the component is user-facing.
45	- Keep both adapter preludes symmetric when both adapters expose the component.
46	- Update adapter `Cargo.toml` feature wiring if the component needs an
47	  `ars-components` feature to be reachable.
48	- Preserve the adapter layering: adapter crates may render framework views and
49	  browser integration, but component behavior belongs in `ars-components`.
50	
51	### Adapter Tests
52	
53	- Add or update framework-specific adapter tests under:
54	  - `crates/ars-leptos/tests/`
55	  - `crates/ars-dioxus/tests/`
56	- Follow the file naming and parity expectations enforced by
57	  `cargo xtask lint adapter-parity`.
58	- Cover the component's required props, attributes, ARIA output, state
59	  synchronization, callbacks, disabled/read-only states, and as-child behavior
60	  where applicable.
61	- Add browser-backed wasm tests for behavior that requires a real DOM: focus,
62	  keyboard navigation, pointer events, layout, clipboard, file upload,
63	  drag/drop, media queries, observers, portal behavior, or cleanup of browser
64	  resources.
65	- Add snapshot tests only when a stable rendered structure is part of the review
66	  surface. Inspect snapshots before marking the work ready; PRs that touch
67	  `.snap` files must receive the `snapshot-reviewed` label.
68	
69	### E2E Fixtures And Harnesses
70	
71	Add the component to the browser E2E fixture when it has browser-observable
72	behavior or when reviewers need a cross-adapter browser proof.
73	
74	Update both fixtures when both adapters exist:
75	
76	- `crates/ars-e2e/fixtures/leptos/src/main.rs`
77	- `crates/ars-e2e/fixtures/dioxus/src/main.rs`
78	
79	Then add or update the matching E2E harness module:
80	
81	- `crates/ars-e2e/src/<category>/<component>.rs`
82	- `crates/ars-e2e/src/<category>/mod.rs`
83	- `crates/ars-e2e/src/lib.rs` only if this is the first component in a new
84	  category.
85	- `xtask/src/e2e.rs`, `xtask/src/main.rs`, and `crates/ars-e2e/src/main.rs`
86	  when this is the first E2E-covered component in a category that does not yet
87	  have an E2E subcommand.
88	
89	E2E harnesses should verify what unit or SSR tests cannot prove reliably:
90	
91	- axe accessibility checks on the mounted fixture;
92	- keyboard and pointer interaction in a real browser;
93	- focus movement and visible focus indicators;
94	- ARIA roles, names, and live text visible to the browser;
95	- portal, overlay, positioning, scroll lock, or z-index behavior;
96	- browser-native form, disabled, file, clipboard, or drag/drop semantics;
97	- adapter parity for the same visible scenario across Leptos and Dioxus.
98	
99	If a component is purely static and already has strong adapter tests, state why
100	no E2E fixture change is needed in the PR.
101	
102	### Widgets Examples
103	
104	Add a visual/demo entry to every applicable widgets example crate:
105	
106	- `examples/widgets-leptos`
107	- `examples/widgets-dioxus`
108	- `examples/widgets-leptos-css`
109	- `examples/widgets-dioxus-css`
110	- `examples/widgets-leptos-tailwind`
111	- `examples/widgets-dioxus-tailwind`
112	
113	Use the category module that matches the component:
114	
115	- `src/categories/input.rs`
116	- `src/categories/selection.rs`
117	- `src/categories/overlay.rs`
118	- `src/categories/navigation.rs`
119	- `src/categories/date_time.rs`
120	- `src/categories/data_display.rs`
121	- `src/categories/layout.rs`
122	- `src/categories/specialized.rs`
123	- `src/categories/utility.rs`
124	
125	Do not put category-specific example text in root `WidgetsText`. Add it to the
126	category-local text enum such as `UtilityText`, `NavigationText`, or
127	`InputText`.
128	
129	Only edit `main.rs`, `text.rs`, or `categories/mod.rs` when the top-level spec
130	category list itself changes.
131	
132	### Specification Updates
133	
134	Update the relevant spec in the same PR if implementation reveals drift.
135	
136	- Shared behavior belongs in `spec/foundation/` or `spec/shared/`.
137	- Adapter-specific behavior belongs in
138	  `spec/foundation/08-adapter-leptos.md`,
139	  `spec/foundation/09-adapter-dioxus.md`, or the per-component adapter spec.
140	- Do not leave spec drift as a follow-up.
141	
142	## Implementation Order
143	
144	Use this order unless the issue explicitly says otherwise:
145	
146	1. Move the issue to **In Progress** on the GitHub Project board.
147	2. Read the issue acceptance criteria and the specs listed above.
148	3. Add or update focused adapter tests first.
149	4. Implement the adapter component code.
150	5. Wire modules, prelude exports, and feature flags.
151	6. Add or update E2E fixtures and E2E harness modules.
152	7. Add or update widgets examples in the matching category modules.
153	8. Update specs if the intended contract changed.
154	9. Run focused tests and checks for the edited component.
155	10. Invoke `.agents/skills/post-implementation-audit/SKILL.md`.
156	11. Fix every audit finding in the same PR.
157	12. Present the result for user review before committing.
158	
159	## Validation Checklist
160	
161	Run the exact commands named by the issue. In addition, use the applicable
162	checks below.
163	
164	For Leptos adapter code:
165	
166	```bash
167	cargo check -p ars-leptos
168	cargo test -p ars-leptos --test <component>
169	```
170	
171	For Dioxus adapter code:
172	
173	```bash
174	cargo check -p ars-dioxus
175	cargo test -p ars-dioxus --test <component>
176	```
177	
178	For browser-backed adapter tests, use the repo browser-test environment
179	documented in `AGENTS.md` when running wasm tests locally.
180	
181	For E2E changes:
182	
183	```bash
184	cargo check -p ars-e2e
185	cargo xtask e2e <category> --adapter leptos
186	cargo xtask e2e <category> --adapter dioxus
187	```
188	
189	Today the supported E2E categories are `navigation` and `utility`. If a task
190	adds the first E2E-covered component for another category, add the matching
191	category subcommand before documenting the validation command as available.
192	
193	For widgets examples:
194	
195	```bash
196	cd examples
197	cargo check -p widgets-leptos -p widgets-dioxus \
198	  -p widgets-leptos-css -p widgets-dioxus-css \
199	  -p widgets-leptos-tailwind -p widgets-dioxus-tailwind
200	```
201	
202	For workspace gates before publishing:
203	
204	```bash
205	cargo fmt --all --check
206	cargo xtask lint adapter-parity
207	cargo xci-fast
208	```
209	
210	Run full `cargo xci` instead of `cargo xci-fast` when the change is broad,
211	touches feature-flag interactions, or modifies shared adapter infrastructure.
212	
213	## PR Closeout
214	
215	Before asking for review:
216	
217	- confirm all required deliverables above are either implemented or explicitly
218	  marked N/A with a reason;
219	- include the issue auto-close keyword in the PR body;
220	- list spec refs and validation commands in the PR body;
221	- attach `snapshot-reviewed` if `.snap` files changed;
222	- invoke `.agents/skills/waiting-for-codex-review/SKILL.md` after every push;
223	- keep the issue, PR, and Project board state aligned with the actual work.
224	
225	Do not close the issue until the PR is merged, CI is green, and Codex review has
226	left a thumbs-up.
227	
```

1	//! Browser E2E harness for the `Separator` component.
2	
3	use thirtyfour::prelude::*;
4	
5	pub use crate::fixtures::Adapter;
6	use crate::{
7	    Error,
8	    utility::{assert_attr, element_by_id, open_utility_panel},
9	};
10	
11	/// Runs the `Separator` browser assertions inside the Utility fixture panel.
12	///
13	/// # Errors
14	///
15	/// Returns an error when `WebDriver` cannot find the fixture nodes or an
16	/// assertion fails.
17	pub async fn run_separator_flow(
18	    driver: &WebDriver,
19	    url: &str,
20	    adapter: Adapter,
21	) -> Result<(), Error> {
22	    open_utility_panel(driver, url).await?;
23	
24	    let prefix = id_prefix(adapter);
25	
26	    let horizontal = element_by_id(driver, &format!("{prefix}-separator-horizontal")).await?;
27	
28	    assert_attr(&horizontal, "data-ars-scope", "separator").await?;
29	    assert_attr(&horizontal, "data-ars-part", "root").await?;
30	    assert_attr(&horizontal, "role", "separator").await?;
31	    assert_attr(&horizontal, "aria-orientation", "horizontal").await?;
32	    assert_attr(&horizontal, "data-ars-orientation", "horizontal").await?;
33	
34	    let vertical = element_by_id(driver, &format!("{prefix}-separator-vertical")).await?;
35	
36	    assert_attr(&vertical, "role", "separator").await?;
37	    assert_attr(&vertical, "aria-orientation", "vertical").await?;
38	    assert_attr(&vertical, "data-ars-orientation", "vertical").await?;
39	
40	    let as_child = element_by_id(driver, &format!("{prefix}-separator-as-child")).await?;
41	
42	    let tag = as_child.tag_name().await?;
43	
44	    assert_expected_tag(
45	        &tag,
46	        "div",
47	        "SeparatorAsChild root must stay consumer-owned",
48	    )?;
49	
50	    assert_attr(&as_child, "data-ars-scope", "separator").await?;
51	    assert_attr(&as_child, "data-ars-part", "root").await?;
52	    assert_attr(&as_child, "role", "separator").await?;
53	    assert_attr(&as_child, "aria-orientation", "vertical").await?;
54	    assert_attr(&as_child, "data-ars-orientation", "vertical").await?;
55	
56	    let decorative = element_by_id(driver, &format!("{prefix}-separator-decorative")).await?;
57	
58	    assert_attr(&decorative, "data-ars-scope", "separator").await?;
59	    assert_attr(&decorative, "data-ars-part", "root").await?;
60	    assert_attr(&decorative, "role", "none").await?;
61	
62	    if decorative.attr("aria-orientation").await?.is_some() {
63	        return Err(Error::Assertion(
64	            "decorative Separator must omit aria-orientation".to_string(),
65	        ));
66	    }
67	
68	    Ok(())
69	}
70	
71	const fn id_prefix(adapter: Adapter) -> &'static str {
72	    match adapter {
73	        Adapter::Leptos => "leptos-fixture",
74	        Adapter::Dioxus => "dioxus-fixture",
75	    }
76	}
77	
78	fn assert_expected_tag(actual: &str, expected: &str, context: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {
79	    if actual == expected {
80	        Ok(())
81	    } else {
82	        Err(Error::Assertion(format!(
83	            "{context} {expected}, got {actual:?}"
84	        )))
85	    }
86	}
87

98

101	    }

60	/// Returns an error when the example server, `ChromeDriver`, `WebDriver` session,
61	/// or browser assertions fail.
62	pub async fn run(options: Options) -> Result<(), Error> {
63	    let adapter = options.adapter;
64	
65	    let session = start_fixture_session(FixtureOptions {
66	        adapter,
67	        port: options.port,
68	        webdriver_url: options.webdriver_url,
69	        no_server: options.no_server,
70	        headless: options.headless,
71	    })
72	    .await?;
73	
74	    let run = async {
75	        button::run_button_flow(&session.driver, &session.url, adapter).await?;
76	        visually_hidden::run_visually_hidden_flow(&session.driver, &session.url, adapter).await?;
77	        separator::run_separator_flow(&session.driver, &session.url, adapter).await?;
78	        client_only::run_client_only_flow(&session.driver, &session.url, adapter).await?;
79	        z_index_allocator::run_z_index_allocator_flow(&session.driver, &session.url, adapter)
80	            .await?;
81	        dismissable::run_dismissable_flow(&session.driver, &session.url).await?;
82	        error_boundary::run_error_boundary_flow(&session.driver, &session.url).await
83	    }
84	    .await;
85	
86	    let quit = session.quit().await;
87	
88	    run?;
89	    quit?;
90	
91	    Ok(())
92	}

164	pub(crate) async fn dispatch_pointer_sequence(
165	    driver: &WebDriver,
166	    element: &WebElement,
167	) -> Result<(), Error> {
168	    driver
169	        .execute(
170	            r#"
171	            const el = arguments[0];
172	            for (const type of ["pointerdown", "pointerup", "click"]) {
173	                const init = {
174	                    bubbles: true,
175	                    cancelable: true,
176	                    composed: true,
177	                    pointerType: "mouse",
178	                    pointerId: 1,
179	                    isPrimary: true,
180	                    button: 0,
181	                    buttons: type === "pointerdown" ? 1 : 0
182	                };
183	                const event = type === "click"
184	                    ? new MouseEvent(type, init)
185	                    : new PointerEvent(type, init);
186	                el.dispatchEvent(event);
187	            }
188	            "#,
189	            vec![element.to_json()?],
190	        )
191	        .await?;
192	
193	    Ok(())
194	}

196	async fn visible_tab(driver: &WebDriver, label: &str) -> Result<WebElement, Error> {
197	    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(15);
198	
199	    let mut last_error = None;
200	
201	    while Instant::now() < deadline {
202	        match visible_tab_now(driver, label).await {
203	            Ok(Some(tab)) => return Ok(tab),
204	            Ok(None) => time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await,
205	            Err(error) => {
206	                last_error = Some(error.to_string());
207	                time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
208	            }
209	        }
210	    }
211	
212	    Err(Error::Timeout(format!(
213	        "timed out waiting for visible category tab {label:?}; last WebDriver error: {}",
214	        last_error.unwrap_or_else(|| "none".to_string())
215	    )))
216	}
217	
218	async fn visible_tab_now(driver: &WebDriver, label: &str) -> Result<Option<WebElement>, Error> {
219	    let tabs = driver.find_all(By::Css("[role='tab']")).await?;
220	
221	    for tab in tabs {
222	        let text = tab.text().await?;
223	
224	        if text.contains(label) && tab.is_displayed().await? {
225	            return Ok(Some(tab));
226	        }
227	    }
228	
229	    Ok(None)
230	}
231	
232	async fn wait_for_text(driver: &WebDriver, text: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {
233	    let found = driver
234	        .execute(
235	            "return document.body && document.body.innerText.includes(arguments[0]);",
236	            vec![Value::String(text.to_string())],
237	        )
238	        .await?;
239	
240	    if found.json().as_bool() == Some(true) {
241	        Ok(())
242	    } else {
243	        Err(Error::Assertion(format!(
244	            "expected page text to contain {text:?}"
245	        )))
246	    }
247	}

1	//! Browser E2E harness for the `VisuallyHidden` component.
2	
3	use thirtyfour::prelude::*;
4	
5	pub use crate::fixtures::Adapter;
6	use crate::{
7	    Error,
8	    utility::{assert_attr, assert_bool_attr, open_utility_panel},
9	};
10	
11	/// Runs the `VisuallyHidden` browser assertions inside the Utility fixture panel.
12	///
13	/// # Errors
14	///
15	/// Returns an error when `WebDriver` cannot find the fixture nodes or an
16	/// assertion fails.
17	pub async fn run_visually_hidden_flow(
18	    driver: &WebDriver,
19	    url: &str,
20	    adapter: Adapter,
21	) -> Result<(), Error> {
22	    open_utility_panel(driver, url).await?;
23	
24	    let prefix = id_prefix(adapter);
25	
26	    let hidden = hidden_element_by_id(driver, &format!("{prefix}-visually-hidden-label")).await?;
27	
28	    assert_attr(&hidden, "data-ars-scope", "visually-hidden").await?;
29	    assert_attr(&hidden, "data-ars-part", "root").await?;
30	
31	    let class = hidden.attr("class").await?;
32	
33	    if class_token_present(class.as_deref(), "ars-visually-hidden") {
34	        // Expected default hidden class.
35	    } else {
36	        return Err(Error::Assertion(format!(
37	            "default VisuallyHidden root must include ars-visually-hidden, got {class:?}"
38	        )));
39	    }
40	
41	    let focusable = hidden_element_by_id(driver, &format!("{prefix}-focusable-skip")).await?;
42	
43	    assert_attr(&focusable, "data-ars-scope", "visually-hidden").await?;
44	    assert_attr(&focusable, "data-ars-part", "root").await?;
45	    assert_bool_attr(&focusable, "data-ars-visually-hidden-focusable").await?;
46	
47	    let as_child =
48	        hidden_element_by_id(driver, &format!("{prefix}-visually-hidden-as-child")).await?;
49	
50	    let tag = as_child.tag_name().await?;
51	
52	    assert_expected_tag(
53	        &tag,
54	        "span",
55	        "VisuallyHiddenAsChild root must stay consumer-owned",
56	    )?;
57	
58	    assert_attr(&as_child, "data-ars-scope", "visually-hidden").await?;
59	    assert_attr(&as_child, "data-ars-part", "root").await?;
60	
61	    Ok(())
62	}

Browser E2E harness for the `Heading` component.\n\nuse thirtyfour::prelude::*;\n\npub use crate::fixtures::Adapter;\nuse crate::{\n    Error,\n    utility::{assert_attr, element_by_id, open_utility_panel},\n};\n\n/// Runs the `Heading` browser assertions inside the Utility fixture panel.\n///\n/// Verifies that:\n///\n/// - default `Heading` renders `<h1>` with the documented `data-ars-*` attrs;\n/// - an explicit `level=Three` renders `<h3>`;\n/// - `HeadingLevelProvider` publishes the starting level to descendants;\n/// - `Section` increments the inherited level.\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Returns an error when `WebDriver` cannot find the fixture nodes or an\n/// assertion fails.\npub async fn run_heading_flow(\n    driver: &WebDriver,\n    url: &str,\n    adapter: Adapter,\n) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    open_utility_panel(driver, url).await?;\n\n    let prefix = id_prefix(adapter);\n\n    let default = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-default\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &default.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h1\",\n        \"default Heading must render an h1 root\",\n    )?;\n    assert_attr(&default, \"data-ars-scope\", \"heading\").await?;\n    assert_attr(&default, \"data-ars-part\", \"root\").await?;\n    assert_no_attr(&default, \"role\").await?;\n    assert_no_attr(&default, \"aria-level\").await?;\n\n    let level_three = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-level-three\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &level_three.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h3\",\n        \"explicit level=Three must render an h3 root\",\n    )?;\n\n    let provided = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-provided\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &provided.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h2\",\n        \"HeadingLevelProvider must publish Level::Two\",\n    )?;\n\n    let section_child = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-section\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &section_child.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h3\",\n        \"Section must increment the inherited level\",\n    )?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nconst fn id_prefix(adapter: Adapter) -> &'static str {\n    match adapter {\n        Adapter::Leptos => \"leptos-fixture\",\n        Adapter::Dioxus => \"dioxus-fixture\",\n    }\n}\n\nfn assert_expected_tag(actual: &str, expected: &str, context: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    if actual.eq_ignore_ascii_case(expected) {\n        Ok(())\n    } else {\n        Err(Error::Assertion(format!(\n            \"{context}: expected {expected}, got {actual:?}\"\n        )))\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn assert_no_attr(element: &WebElement, name: &str) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    if element.attr(name).await?.is_none() {\n        Ok(())\n    } else {\n        Err(Error::Assertion(format!(\n            \"expected {name:?} to be absent on element {:?}\",\n            element.attr(\"id\").await?.unwrap_or_default()\n        )))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn assert_expected_tag_compares_case_insensitively() {\n        assert!(assert_expected_tag(\"H1\", \"h1\", \"tag check\").is_ok());\n        assert!(assert_expected_tag(\"h2\", \"h2\", \"tag check\").is_ok());\n\n        let err = assert_expected_tag(\"h3\", \"h1\", \"tag check\").expect_err(\"mismatch should fail\");\n\n        assert!(err.to_string().contains(\"expected h1\"));\n        assert!(err.to_string().contains(\"\\\"h3\\\"\"));\n    }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "//! Browser E2E harness for the `Highlight` component.\n\nuse thirtyfour::prelude::*;\n\npub use crate::fixtures::Adapter;\nuse crate::{\n    Error,\n    utility::{assert_attr, element_by_id, open_utility_panel},\n};\n\n/// Runs the `Highlight` browser assertions inside the Utility fixture panel.\n///\n/// Verifies that:\n///\n/// - the root `<span>` carries `data-ars-scope=\"highlight\"`,\n///   `data-ars-part=\"root\"`, and `dir=\"auto\"`;\n/// - matched text is wrapped in `<mark data-ars-highlighted=\"true\">`;\n/// - unmatched text is wrapped in `<span data-ars-highlighted=\"false\">`.\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Returns an error when `WebDriver` cannot find the fixture nodes or an\n/// assertion fails.\npub async fn run_highlight_flow(\n    driver: &WebDriver,\n    url: &str,\n    adapter: Adapter,\n) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    open_utility_panel(driver, url).await?;\n\n    let host = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{}-highlight-host\", id_prefix(adapter))).await?;\n\n    let root = host.find(By::Css(\"span[data-ars-scope='highlight']\")).await?;\n\n    assert_attr(&root, \"data-ars-part\", \"root\").await?;\n    assert_attr(&root, \"dir\", \"auto\").await?;\n\n    let mark = root\n        .find(By::Css(\"mark[data-ars-highlighted='true']\"))\n        .await?;\n\n    assert_attr(&mark, \"data-ars-part\", \"highlight-chunk\").await?;\n\n    let mark_text = mark.text().await?;\n\n    if mark_text != \"highlighted\" {\n        return Err(Error::Assertion(format!(\n            \"highlighted chunk must contain 'highlighted', got {mark_text:?}\"\n        )));\n    }\n\n    let unmatched = root\n        .find(By::Css(\"span[data-ars-highlighted='false']\"))\n        .await?;\n\n    assert_attr(&unmatched, \"data-ars-part\", \"highlight-chunk\").await?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nconst fn id_prefix(adapter: Adapter) -> &'static str {\n    match adapter {\n        Adapter::Leptos => \"leptos-fixture\",\n        Adapter::Dioxus => \"dioxus-fixture\",\n    }\n}\n"
}

fn adapter_parity_report(
    components: &BTreeSet<String>,
    leptos_counts: &BTreeMap<String, usize>,
    dioxus_counts: &BTreeMap<String, usize>,
    tolerance: usize,
) -> (String, Vec<String>) {
    let mut output = String::from("Component | Leptos | Dioxus | Delta | Status\n");

    output.push_str("----------|--------|--------|-------|-------\n");

    let mut failures = Vec::new();

    for component in components {
        let leptos = leptos_counts.get(component).copied().unwrap_or(0);

        let dioxus = dioxus_counts.get(component).copied().unwrap_or(0);

        let delta = leptos.abs_diff(dioxus);

        let status = if leptos == 0 && dioxus == 0 {
            "SKIP"
        } else if leptos == 0 || dioxus == 0 {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{component}: both adapters must have tests, leptos={leptos}, dioxus={dioxus}"
            ));
            "FAIL"
        } else if delta > tolerance {
            failures.push(format!(
                "{component}: leptos={leptos}, dioxus={dioxus}, delta={delta}, tolerance={tolerance}"
            ));
            "FAIL"
        } else {
            "OK"
        };

fn adapter_test_counts(
    dir: &Path,
    known_components: &BTreeSet<String>,
) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, usize>, Error> {
    if !dir.exists() {
        return Ok(BTreeMap::new());
    }

    let test_attr = Regex::new(r"#\[\s*(?:wasm_bindgen_)?test\s*\]")?;

    let files = collect_files(dir, |path| {
        path.file_name()
            .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
            .is_some_and(|name| {
                (name.starts_with("test_") && name.ends_with(".rs"))
                    || COMPONENT_NAMED_ADAPTER_TEST_FILES
                        .iter()

1	---
2	name: post-implementation-audit
3	description: MANDATORY after every implementation task — runs three sequential audits on the new code (spec/impl drift, iterative "anything missing?", test coverage) and lands every finding in the same PR before the user-review step. Invoke as soon as an implementation task's named tests pass, OR when any of these phrases appears: "ready to present", "implementation is complete", "named tests pass", "before opening the PR", "ready for review". Skipping this audit leaves spec drift, untested defensive code, missing conventions, and silent contract violations in the merged PR.
4	---
5	
6	# Post-implementation audit
7	
8	This skill is the bridge between *"the named tests pass"* and *"the user reviews the diff"*. It exists because the initial implementation of any task is usually correct on its surface acceptance criteria but quietly drifts from the spec, leaves untested defensive code, ships APIs that diverge from convention, or carries a fold-vs-lowercase mistake that won't surface until production. Running these audits before user-review collapses three reviewer round-trips into one.
9	
10	The skill is mandatory per CLAUDE.md "Development Workflow" step 7 — run it after implementing any user-requested task (feature, bug fix, refactor) and before presenting the final result for user review.
11	
12	## Quick flow
13	
14	The audit is strictly linear — no branching, just a loop in Phase 2:
15	
16	```
17	Phase 1 (spec/impl drift audit)
18	   └─→ land all Phase 1 findings
19	        └─→ Phase 2 (iterative "anything missing?")
20	              ├─→ Round 1: surface findings → land all
21	              ├─→ Round 2: surface findings → land all
22	              └─→ keep looping until 2 consecutive clean rounds (minimum 2 rounds total)
23	                   └─→ Phase 3 (test coverage)
24	                        └─→ land all Phase 3 findings
25	                             └─→ Final verification suite
26	                                  └─→ Hand off to user (CLAUDE.md step 8)
27	```
28	
29	The body below walks through each phase in order. Read top-to-bottom; the structure mirrors the execution order.
30	
31	## Operating principle: no deferral
32	
33	**Every recommendation each audit phase produces lands in *this* PR.** Don't open follow-up issues. Don't TODO-flag. Don't promise a future PR or a future sprint. Don't quietly skip a finding because it feels like scope creep.
34	
35	If a finding is genuinely out of scope (e.g., requires a workspace-wide refactor touching 50+ files), surface it explicitly to the user with that reasoning visible — but the default is to land everything. This constraint is what makes the audit valuable: a deferred finding is a guarantee that the original implementation's bias survives into `main`, where it costs ten times as much to undo.
36	
37	The user will tell you "land it all". Anticipate that, and just do it.
38	
39	## Three sequential phases
40	
41	Run the phases **in order**. Each phase fully completes (audit → land all findings → re-verify) before the next begins.
42	
43	---
44	
45	### Phase 1 — spec/implementation drift audit
46	
47	Compare the implementation against the authoritative spec (`spec/components/<category>/<component>.md` plus any foundation specs it transitively depends on) section-by-section. For every drift, propose the **best outcome independent of which side is currently right**. Sometimes the spec wins, sometimes the impl wins, sometimes the right answer is neither.
48	
49	The canonical entry-prompt for this phase (use this wording when the user asks you to start the audit explicitly):
50	
51	> "Now let's do an audit on how well our new code follows our spec. Do an in-depth check for spec drift and suggest recommendations for each finding. In those recommendations, disregard both the spec and the current implementation as defaults — the recommendation should be the best outcome possible. Sometimes that's the spec, sometimes the implementation, sometimes a mix, sometimes a totally different thing."
52	
53	#### Precondition: both files must exist
54	
55	Before reading anything, verify the touched implementation has a corresponding spec file at `spec/components/<category>/<name>.md` (or the relevant `spec/foundation/` path for foundation-layer changes). If the spec is missing, **stop the audit and surface this to the user** — an unspecced module is a planning failure that should be resolved (write the spec, or split the change) before auditing, not papered over by this skill. Likewise, if the implementation file referenced by the issue is missing or empty, surface that as a precondition failure rather than auditing against an empty diff.
56	
57	#### Procedure
58	
59	1. Read the spec file end-to-end (use `Read` with no offset/limit so you have the whole thing).
60	2. Read the implementation file end-to-end (same).
61	3. Walk every public surface declared in the spec — every struct, enum, function, method, derive list, default value, constant, public re-export. For each:
62	   - Does the spec define it? Does the impl match exactly?
63	   - Are there extras in the impl not in the spec? Are they justified?
64	   - Are there spec items the impl skipped? Are they critical?
65	   - **Does the spec's prose match the impl's actual behavior?** This is the silent-contract-violation class — words that mean something specific in the spec but were implemented as something close-but-different (e.g., "case folding" in the spec but `to_lowercase` in the impl).
66	4. For each finding, write up:
67	   - What the spec says, with line numbers
68	   - What the impl does, with line numbers
69	   - Why it drifted (often a tradeoff the implementer made under acceptance-criteria pressure)
70	   - **Best-outcome recommendation** — independent of which side is currently right
71	5. Group findings by severity (High / Medium / Low) and present as a table to the user.
72	6. Land all of them. Update the spec where the impl is right, update the impl where the spec is right, do both where neither was right, change *only* the spec wording (and add tests proving the new wording) when the contract was subtly wrong all along.
73	
74	#### Special case: both the spec and the implementation are wrong
75	
76	A small fraction of drift findings are *not* "one side is right, the other drifted" — both sides are incorrect, incomplete, or built on a flawed premise. This is rare but real (the task #204 eszett case is an example: the spec implied `ß ↔ ss` equivalence, the impl used `to_lowercase`, but neither matched the actual TR21 case-folding semantics needed). Handle this case differently from routine drift:
77	
78	1. **Escalate to the user via `AskUserQuestion`** — don't unilaterally pick a "best outcome" when no precedent exists. A both-wrong case is a real design decision, not a routine drift fix; the user owns the call.
79	2. **Once the user picks a direction**, land *all three* together in this same PR: the new spec wording, the new implementation, and the tests proving the new design. Skipping any of the three leaves a different kind of drift behind.
80	3. **Write the test first** (TDD per CLAUDE.md), watch it fail under the old code, then change the impl, then update the spec to describe what the new tests assert.
81	
82	#### Output table format
83	
84	| Finding ID | Severity | What spec says | What impl does | Best outcome | Where to land |
85	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
86	| H1 | High | … | … | … | spec §X / impl `path:line` |
87	
88	End with a disposition summary: *"N spec-only changes, M impl-only changes, K both, Q status-quo-was-correct."*
89	
90	---
91	
92	### Phase 2 — iterative "anything else missing?" passes
93	
94	Once Phase 1 findings are landed, the next blind spot is the surface Phase 1 didn't look at: adapter specs, feature flags, prelude exports, framework wiring, foundation patterns that deserve promotion, catalog/manifest entries. This phase is **iterative** — keep asking "anything else?" until two consecutive rounds find nothing new.
95	
96	The canonical entry-prompt (one per round):
97	
98	> "Any other improvement that we might still be missing?"
99	
100	#### Surfaces to actively check each round
101	
102	This is a non-exhaustive checklist. Each round, walk through it explicitly:
103	
104	- **Adapter specs** at `spec/leptos-components/<category>/<component>.md` and `spec/dioxus-components/<category>/<component>.md` — do they describe the new core surface accurately? Are their canonical implementation sketches up-to-date with the actual `Api` / function signatures? Do they reference the right helper methods (e.g., `Api::root_attrs()`) instead of hardcoded data attribute strings?
105	- **Adapter feature wiring** in `crates/ars-leptos/Cargo.toml` and `crates/ars-dioxus/Cargo.toml` — does the adapter's `icu4x` / `web-intl` feature need to enable any new `ars-components/<feature>` flag for the new code to be reachable?
106	- **Adapter `prelude.rs`** — does the new public API need to flow through? (Only if an adapter wrapper exists for the new component; if not, defer to the adapter task.)
107	- **Workspace `spec/manifest.toml`** and **`foundation/02-component-catalog.md`** — is the new component registered and statused? (For brand-new components only.)
108	- **Foundation specs** (`spec/foundation/00-*` through `spec/foundation/11-*`) — does the new code expose a missing shared abstraction worth promoting? CLAUDE.md `spec/CLAUDE.md` says: *"If an adapter-specific implementation exposes a missing shared abstraction, promote that abstraction into the appropriate foundation/shared spec."*
109	- **New crate dependencies** — was the user notified per CLAUDE.md's "Do not add a new dependency crate without explicit user approval first" rule? Did the implementation add `i18n`-style feature flags that warrant a CLAUDE.md note?
110	- **`.cargo/mutants.toml`** — are any new equivalent mutations documented with justifications? (Phase 3 will validate this; surface it here if a mutation that *should* be equivalent isn't documented yet.)
111	
112	#### Termination
113	
114	Stop when:
115	
116	- Two consecutive rounds surface no new findings, **OR**
117	- Three rounds have been completed and the remaining findings are honestly out-of-scope (genuine workspace-wide refactors that would derail this PR).
118	
119	Do **not** stop after one clean round — the second round nearly always surfaces items the first ignored because they felt out-of-scope. With the "no deferral" rule active, they're back in scope.
120	
121	#### Output per round
122	
123	A list of findings with the same "best outcome" framing as Phase 1, plus an explicit statement at the end: *"That's everything I can find this round. Want me to do another?"* — knowing the answer will be yes for at least one more round.
124	
125	---
126	
127	### Phase 3 — test coverage audit
128	
129	By this point the code is convention-aligned and well-specced. Now check the **test surface** — both depth (line / branch / mutation coverage) and breadth (does every test type that *should* exist for this kind of change exist?).
130	
131	The canonical entry-prompt:
132	
133	> "How good is our test coverage here, by looking at the code paths, checking the coverage report and considering the many kinds of tests that we are intending to have (including snapshot tests, proptests, and e2e tests)? Can it be improved?"
134	
135	#### Test types and what each catches
136	
137	| Test type | What it catches | How to assess for the new code |
138	|---|---|---|
139	| **Unit tests** (inline `#[cfg(test)]`) | Logic + edge cases on the named acceptance criteria | List every public API + every edge case the spec describes; cross-reference with the test list |
140	| **Snapshot tests** (insta) | `AttrMap` / chunk-output shape regressions | Check coverage of every anatomy part and every output-affecting prop / state / context branch |
141	| **Property tests** (proptest) | Invariant violations across the input space | Check that invariants are non-trivial (roundtrip, idempotence, no-adjacent-X, etc.) and the input strategy is broad enough to actually exercise edge locales / multi-byte / large inputs |
142	| **Mutation tests** (cargo-mutants) | Tests that *exist* but don't actually constrain behavior | Run `cargo mutants -p <crate> -f <file>` and triage every `MISSED`; this is mandatory for every new or materially changed framework-agnostic component |
143	| **Doc tests** | Public-API examples broken by future changes | Check `///` blocks for at least one `# Examples` block on the canonical entry point |
144	| **Spec-conformance tests** | Anatomy drift between spec and impl | Check `crates/ars-components/tests/spec_conformance/*.rs` for an entry covering the new component's `Part` enum and public API/attribute contract; this is mandatory for every new framework-agnostic component |
145	| **Code coverage** (cargo llvm-cov + xtask wasm path) | Unreachable / under-tested code; threshold drift | Use the right command for the crate (see "Procedure" below) — bare `cargo llvm-cov` does **not** measure adapter wasm code paths. Always finish with `cargo xtask coverage check-all --file <lcov>` to enforce the same thresholds CI does. |
146	| **E2E / browser tests** (wasm-bindgen-test) | DOM-level behavior in the adapter | N/A for agnostic-core changes. Required when the change touches `ars-leptos`, `ars-dioxus`, `ars-dom`, or `ars-i18n` (`web-intl` path); these run via `cargo xtask test` or the adapter test-harness crates and execute in a browser via `wasm-bindgen-test`. Treat coverage from the wasm path (`cargo xtask coverage wasm`) as the source of truth for these — not the host-target llvm-cov number. |
147	
148	#### Procedure
149	
150	1. **Coverage report.** The command depends on which crate the change touches — this workspace measures host-target and wasm32 paths separately because adapter code (`ars-leptos`, `ars-dioxus`, `ars-dom`, the `ars-i18n` `web-intl` path, the adapter test harnesses) has `target_arch = "wasm32"` / `feature = "web"` code that bare host-target `cargo llvm-cov` cannot reach.
151	
152	   **For native-only crates** (`ars-components`, `ars-collections`, `ars-core`, `ars-forms`, `ars-interactions`, `ars-a11y`, `xtask`):
153	   ```bash
154	   cargo llvm-cov test -p <crate> --features <relevant> --lib --no-fail-fast --text -- <module>::
155	   ```
156	
157	   **For adapter crates / `web-intl` paths** (`ars-leptos`, `ars-dioxus`, `ars-dom`, `ars-test-harness-leptos`, `ars-test-harness-dioxus`, or `ars-i18n` when the change is in the `web-intl` feature gate):
158	   ```bash
159	   cargo xtask coverage wasm \
160	     --package <crate> \
161	     --feature <feat1> --feature <feat2> \
162	     --file wasm.lcov.info
163	   ```
164	   (`--feature` is singular and repeatable, NOT `--features` — it mirrors cargo's `--feature` convention; use `--no-default-features` to drop defaults.) This uses `wasm-bindgen-test`'s experimental coverage recipe with LLVM 22 / `clang-22` (the same recipe CI nightly runs via `cargo xtask ci coverage`). The bare `cargo llvm-cov` command will silently report `0.00%` for the wasm-gated code paths, which is *not* the same as having no coverage — it means *unmeasured*. Don't trust low numbers on adapter crates from the native path.
165	
166	   **For a change that touches both native and wasm paths** (e.g., a new ars-i18n helper consumed from both backends, or a refactor in `ars-dom` that affects native callers):
167	   ```bash
168	   # Generate the native lcov (workspace, excluding wasm-only crates):
169	   cargo llvm-cov --workspace \
170	     --exclude ars-leptos --exclude ars-dioxus \
171	     --exclude ars-test-harness-leptos --exclude ars-test-harness-dioxus \
172	     --exclude ars-derive --exclude xtask \
173	     --lcov --output-path native.lcov.info
174	
175	   # Generate the wasm lcov for each adapter target you touched:
176	   cargo xtask coverage wasm --package <wasm-package> --feature <feat> --file wasm.lcov.info
177	
178	   # Merge without double-counting duplicate lines (each `--file` adds an input):
179	   cargo xtask coverage merge \
180	     --file native.lcov.info \
181	     --file wasm.lcov.info \
182	     --output merged.lcov.info
183	
184	   # Enforce per-crate spec-defined thresholds (same gate CI runs):
185	   cargo xtask coverage check-all --file merged.lcov.info
186	   ```
187	
188	   The per-crate thresholds (line% / branch%) are encoded in `xtask::coverage::default_thresholds()` and include the wasm targets. `cargo xtask coverage check-all` is the same gate CI enforces, so a green local run guarantees green CI on the coverage step.
189	
190	   Read the per-line annotated output from the `--text` invocations. Every `^0` marker is an unhit branch — investigate each one. Categorize as: real test gap / equivalent defensive guard / unreachable dead code. **Expected non-gaps:** no-op callback closures in tests (e.g., `|_| {}`) are intentionally uncovered and not a real gap — CLAUDE.md calls this out explicitly.
191	
192	   **Not measured by either path:** `ars-derive` (proc-macro, runs in the compiler — exercised indirectly via `crates/ars-core/tests/derive_contract.rs`). Don't expect coverage numbers here.
193	
194	2. **Mutation testing.** Run:
195	   ```bash
196	   cargo mutants -p <crate> -f <file>
197	   ```
198	   For framework-agnostic component work in `ars-components`, run this against the component's source file, usually:
199	   ```bash
200	   cargo mutants -p ars-components -f crates/ars-components/src/<category>/<component>/mod.rs
201	   ```
202	   Use the actual file path for single-file modules.
203	
204	   For each `MISSED` line, decide:
205	   - **Real test gap** → add a test that kills the mutation (often a positive-direction assertion the existing tests skipped).
206	   - **Equivalent mutation** → add a regex to `.cargo/mutants.toml` `exclude_re` with a written justification explaining *why* the mutation cannot change observable behavior.
207	   - **Defensive code that's truly unreachable** → consider deleting the code. This is often the cleanest fix and is the right answer for unreachable post-filter guards.
208	
209	3. **Test-type breadth audit.** Walk the table above. For each test type, ask: *"Does this kind of change need this kind of test, and do we have one?"* Examples:
210	   - New framework-agnostic component with an anatomy table → spec-conformance test required
211	   - New or materially changed framework-agnostic component → targeted cargo-mutants run required before handoff
212	   - New public function → doc test with `# Examples` required
213	   - New invariants on a computation pipeline → proptest invariants strongly recommended
214	   - New `AttrMap` helpers → snapshot tests for each branch required
215	
216	4. **Cumulative assessment.** Present the before/after metrics in a table:
217	
218	| Metric | Before this phase | After this phase |
219	|---|---|---|
220	| Lines covered | x% | y% |
221	| Mutations caught | x/total | y/total |
222	| Unit tests | N | M |
223	| Doc tests | N | M |
224	| Spec-conformance test | yes/no | yes/no |
225	
226	#### Output
227	
228	A list of gaps with concrete reproducers (specific test inputs that trigger the missed branch). For each gap, classify the disposition (real-gap-add-test / equivalent-mutation-skip / dead-code-remove). End with a clear *"land all"* and the verification commands to confirm.
229	
230	#### Anti-pattern: chasing 100% line coverage
231	
232	The goal is **not** "100% line coverage at any cost". The goal is *"no surviving mutations, no unreachable defensive code, every test type that should exist does exist"*. A 99% line-coverage report with all mutations caught is a stronger position than a 100% line-coverage report with three surviving mutations. If the last 1% of uncovered code is a genuinely unreachable defensive guard, document it in `mutants.toml` and move on.
233	
234	---
235	
236	## After the three phases
237	
238	Run the full verification suite one final time before handing off to the user:
239	
240	```bash
241	# 1. Unit + integration tests, both feature-on and feature-off variants
242	cargo test -p <crate> --features <relevant> --all-targets
243	cargo test -p <crate> --lib                       # without the optional features
244	
245	# 2. Workspace clippy (must be -D warnings clean)
246	cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --exclude ars-i18n -- -D warnings
247	
248	# 3. Backend matrices for any feature-gated code
249	cargo clippy -p ars-i18n --no-default-features --features std,icu4x --all-targets -- -D warnings
250	cargo clippy -p ars-i18n --no-default-features --features std,web-intl --all-targets -- -D warnings
251	
252	# 4. Docs build (0 new warnings on the changed crate)
253	cargo doc -p <crate> --no-deps --all-features
254	
255	# 5. Spec validation + snippet check
256	cargo xtask spec validate
257	cargo test -p xtask --test spec_corpus_compile_snippets
258	
259	# 6. Snapshot orphan check
260	cargo insta test --workspace --features <relevant> --unreferenced=reject
261	
262	# 7. Mutation re-run (must be 0 missed)
263	cargo mutants -p <crate> -f <file>
264	
265	# 8. Coverage thresholds — uses the same gate CI enforces. The recipe
266	#    depends on which crate the change touches: native-only changes can
267	#    use `cargo llvm-cov ... --lcov`; changes that touch adapter code or
268	#    `web-intl` paths require `cargo xtask coverage wasm` + `merge` first
269	#    (see Phase 3 above). Then:
270	cargo xtask coverage check-all --file lcov.info
271	
272	# 9. Adapter builds reachable with feature wiring
273	cargo build -p ars-leptos --features icu4x
274	cargo build -p ars-dioxus --features icu4x,web
275	```
276	
277	Then write **one consolidated user summary** covering all three phases' findings + the verification table. Hand off for user review per CLAUDE.md workflow step 8 (which was the old step 7 before this skill was inserted).
278	
279	## Anti-patterns
280	
281	- **Deferring** any finding ("we can fix that in a follow-up"). This is the rule the user set explicitly. Breaking it makes the audit ceremonial.
282	- **Loading the user with options mid-phase.** Make a clear best-outcome recommendation. Only escalate to `AskUserQuestion` when there's a genuine judgment call the user must make (e.g., behavior choices with real tradeoffs, not implementation details).
283	- **Skipping rounds of Phase 2** because the first round was clean. The second round nearly always finds something the first ignored.
284	- **Treating coverage % as the goal.** The goal is mutation-killed and breadth-complete, not a number.
285	- **Inventing cosmetic edits** the audits didn't surface. If a phase doesn't find a real finding, don't fabricate one — say "this round found nothing" and proceed.
286	- **Re-running tests after every micro-edit** during a phase. Land a batch of related findings, then verify, then move on.
287	- **Forgetting to update the named-tests file** when a new test exposes a real bug fixed in the same phase. The fix and the test land together.
288	
289	## What this skill is not
290	
291	- A code-review skill. Code review (style, naming, simplification) belongs to `pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer` and runs after the PR is opened.
292	- A pre-implementation skill. Before implementing, `feature-dev:feature-dev` and `superpowers:writing-plans` handle planning.
293	- A way to revisit acceptance criteria. The acceptance criteria are fixed by the GitHub issue. This skill assumes they're already met.
294	
295	## Worked example — task #204
296	
297	The flow this skill encodes was validated on GitHub issue #204 (`task: Implement Highlight agnostic core`). The initial implementation passed all 8 named acceptance-criterion tests on first try. Then:
298	
299	- **Phase 1** surfaced 16 drift findings, including a silent contract violation (the spec said *"Unicode case folding"* but the impl used `to_lowercase` — they aren't equivalent: under `to_lowercase`, query `"ss"` does not match text `"ß"`, violating the spec's explicit eszett contract). Fix: add `ars_i18n::case_fold`, switch the matching pipeline, rewrite the German test to assert the actual three-direction equivalence.
300	- **Phase 2 round 1** surfaced 4 more items (adapter spec alignment, adapter feature wiring, roundtrip invariant test, proptest invariants).
301	- **Phase 2 round 2** surfaced 3 more (a `case_fold` vs `to_lowercase` semantic gap, foundation/10 parametric-anatomy concept, cargo-mutants scout).
302	- **Phase 3** surfaced 4 coverage gaps (dead `continue` branch, `merge_ranges` else branch, fold-expansion partial-match defense, spec-conformance test). Pushed line coverage from 98.67% to 99.91% with all 57 mutations caught.
303	
304	The cumulative effect: PR landed with one user review pass instead of three, and the spec contract (`ß ↔ ss`) is actually true instead of cosmetically true. That's the value this skill creates.
305	
```

  "old_string": "/// Runs the `Heading` browser assertions inside the Utility fixture panel.\n///\n/// Verifies that:\n///\n/// - default `Heading` renders `<h1>` with the documented `data-ars-*` attrs;\n/// - an explicit `level=Three` renders `<h3>`;\n/// - `HeadingLevelProvider` publishes the starting level to descendants;\n/// - `Section` increments the inherited level.\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Returns an error when `WebDriver` cannot find the fixture nodes or an\n/// assertion fails.\npub async fn run_heading_flow(\n    driver: &WebDriver,\n    url: &str,\n    adapter: Adapter,\n) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    open_utility_panel(driver, url).await?;\n\n    let prefix = id_prefix(adapter);\n\n    let default = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-default\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &default.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h1\",\n        \"default Heading must render an h1 root\",\n    )?;\n    assert_attr(&default, \"data-ars-scope\", \"heading\").await?;\n    assert_attr(&default, \"data-ars-part\", \"root\").await?;\n    assert_no_attr(&default, \"role\").await?;\n    assert_no_attr(&default, \"aria-level\").await?;\n\n    let level_three = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-level-three\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &level_three.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h3\",\n        \"explicit level=Three must render an h3 root\",\n    )?;\n\n    let provided = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-provided\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &provided.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h2\",\n        \"HeadingLevelProvider must publish Level::Two\",\n    )?;\n\n    let section_child = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-section\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &section_child.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h3\",\n        \"Section must increment the inherited level\",\n    )?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Runs the `Heading` browser assertions inside the Utility fixture panel.\n///\n/// The fixture nests its Heading demos under the panel's `<h2>` section\n/// heading, so it starts the provider at `Level::Three` to keep the page-wide\n/// hierarchy axe-clean (h1 → h2 → h3 → h4). Verifies that:\n///\n/// - an explicit `level=Three` renders `<h3>` with the documented\n///   `data-ars-*` attrs and no redundant `role`/`aria-level`;\n/// - `HeadingLevelProvider` publishes the starting level (`Three`) to\n///   descendants → `<h3>`;\n/// - `Section` increments the inherited level (`Three → Four`) → `<h4>`.\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Returns an error when `WebDriver` cannot find the fixture nodes or an\n/// assertion fails.\npub async fn run_heading_flow(\n    driver: &WebDriver,\n    url: &str,\n    adapter: Adapter,\n) -> Result<(), Error> {\n    open_utility_panel(driver, url).await?;\n\n    let prefix = id_prefix(adapter);\n\n    let level_three = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-level-three\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &level_three.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h3\",\n        \"explicit level=Three must render an h3 root\",\n    )?;\n    assert_attr(&level_three, \"data-ars-scope\", \"heading\").await?;\n    assert_attr(&level_three, \"data-ars-part\", \"root\").await?;\n    assert_no_attr(&level_three, \"role\").await?;\n    assert_no_attr(&level_three, \"aria-level\").await?;\n\n    let provided = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-provided\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &provided.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h3\",\n        \"HeadingLevelProvider must publish Level::Three to descendants\",\n    )?;\n\n    let section_child = element_by_id(driver, &format!(\"{prefix}-heading-section\")).await?;\n\n    assert_expected_tag(\n        &section_child.tag_name().await?,\n        \"h4\",\n        \"Section must increment Level::Three to Level::Four\",\n    )?;\n\n    Ok(())\n}"
}

fn run_coverage() -> Result<(), Error> {
    preflight_llvm_cov()?;

    preflight_nextest()?;

    coverage::preflight_nightly().map_err(Error::Coverage)?;

    let coverage_dir = Path::new("target").join("coverage");

    fs::create_dir_all(&coverage_dir).map_err(Error::Io)?;

    let native_lcov = coverage_dir.join("native.lcov");

    let merged_lcov = PathBuf::from("lcov.info");

    // Generate native lcov via cargo-llvm-cov + cargo-nextest.
    cargo(
        Step::Coverage,
        &[
            "+nightly",
            "llvm-cov",
            "nextest",
            "--branch",
            "--workspace",
            "--lcov",
            "--output-path",
            native_lcov.to_str().expect("valid utf-8 path"),
            "--no-fail-fast",
        ],
    )?;

    let mut reports = vec![native_lcov];

    for target in coverage::default_wasm_coverage_targets() {
        let wasm_lcov = coverage_dir.join(format!("{}-wasm.lcov", target.package));

        coverage::generate_wasm_lcov(&coverage::WasmCoverageOptions {
            package: target.package.to_owned(),
            output: wasm_lcov.clone(),
            features: target
                .features
                .iter()
                .map(|feature| (*feature).to_owned())
                .collect(),
            no_default_features: target.no_default_features,
            extra_test_args: Vec::new(),
        })
        .map_err(Error::Coverage)?;

        reports.push(wasm_lcov);
    }

    coverage::merge_files(&reports, &merged_lcov).map_err(Error::Coverage)?;

    // Check thresholds programmatically (reuses coverage module).
    let thresholds = coverage::default_thresholds();

    match coverage::check_all(&merged_lcov, &thresholds) {
        Ok(output) => {
            eprint!("{output}");
            Ok(())
        }
        Err(e) => Err(Error::Coverage(e)),
    }
}

fn run_test_stage(step: Step, stage: test::Stage) -> Result<(), Error> {

}

> DEVELOPER

Doesn't our adapter level components need to be able to receive some html global attributes like classes and ids to be styled with CSS or tailwind for example? Actual question, don't change any code yet?

> AGENT

Good question — let me give you an honest answer without changing code.

## Current state of the three new components

Looking at the props I shipped:

| Component | Accepts | Does NOT accept |
|---|---|---|
| `Heading` (Leptos & Dioxus) | `id`, `level`, `children` | `class`, `style`, any other global HTML attr |
| `Landmark` | `id`, `role`, `labelledby_id`, `messages`, `locale`, `children` | `class`, `style`, etc. |
| `Highlight` | `query`, `text`, `ignore_case`, `match_strategy`, `locale` | `class`, `style`, `children` (this one renders its own content) |

So **no** — none of them accept arbitrary HTML global attributes today.

## How users CAN style them now

The components do emit stable `data-ars-scope` + `data-ars-part` attributes on every part. So users can write CSS that targets those:

```css
[data-ars-scope="heading"][data-ars-part="root"] {
    color: rebeccapurple;
    margin-block: 1.5rem;
}

[data-ars-scope="highlight"] mark[data-ars-highlighted="true"] {
    background: #fef08a;
    color: #422006;
}
```

This is the workspace's canonical pattern — see `SEPARATOR_STYLE` at `examples/widgets-leptos/src/categories/utility.rs:213-235` for the exact precedent. It works fine for plain CSS, Sass, CSS Modules, etc.

## Where the gap bites

The pattern breaks down for **utility-class systems like Tailwind**, where the natural ergonomic is to pass class tokens directly on the element. Today a user writing:

```rust
<Heading class="text-4xl font-bold">"Hello"</Heading>
```

…would get a Leptos / Dioxus compile error: "no such prop `class`". They'd have to either:

1. Wrap it: `<div class="text-4xl font-bold"><Heading>...</Heading></div>` — but that adds a wrapper `<div>`, defeating the semantic `<h1>` root, and the class is on the wrong element for things like `text-4xl` that need to be on the actual `<h1>`.
2. Use the data-attribute selector and configure Tailwind's `@layer components` directive — extra ceremony.
3. Drop into raw HTML — defeats the point of the component.

## What the spec says

The Leptos & Dioxus adapter specs for all three components have an "Attr Merge and Ownership Rules" section. For Heading (`spec/leptos-components/utility/heading.md:35-37`):

> **Consumer attrs:** consumer root attrs.
> **Merge order:** core level, role, and labeling semantics win; **`class`/`style` merge additively**.

So the spec **does** anticipate consumer-supplied `class`/`style` merging into the root. My implementations skipped that surface entirely. Same gap exists for the already-shipped `Separator` and `VisuallyHidden` non-AsChild variants — they don't accept arbitrary attrs either. The workspace has been collectively kicking this can down the road.

## What other component libraries do

- **Radix / shadcn**: every primitive accepts arbitrary HTML attrs via `...rest` and merges them.
- **Ark UI**: explicit props + an "asChild" slot for custom roots.
- **Headless UI**: `as` prop + spread.
- **React Aria**: explicit slot pattern with a `Provider` for styled rendering.

The pattern we *do* use here is "**`AsChild` variants for consumer-controlled roots**" — e.g., `SeparatorAsChild`, `VisuallyHiddenAsChild`, `ButtonAsChild` all let the consumer own the root element and spread their own attrs onto it. For `Heading`/`Landmark`/`Highlight` I deliberately did **not** ship AsChild variants because the spec sketches don't show them, but the spec also expects class/style merging — so the workspace contract is internally inconsistent on these three.

## Concrete options (no code change yet)

1. **Add `class` (and maybe `style`) pass-through props** — smallest surface, covers Tailwind ergonomics directly. The agnostic core supports it: `AttrMap` already merges class tokens additively when you call `merge_attrs` with a consumer-supplied class.

2. **Add `AsChild` variants** — matches the rest of the codebase's escape-hatch convention. Heaviest implementation; trades component count for full DOM control. Pre-empts every future "but what about `aria-*` / `style` / `data-*`?" follow-up.

3. **Add a single `attrs: AttrMap` (or `Vec<Attribute>`) prop** — most general; one prop accepts anything, gets merged via existing `merge_attrs`. But user ergonomics are worse than `class=…`.

4. **Defer** — keep using `data-ars-scope` selectors, document the Tailwind story as "use plain CSS or `@apply`". This is the status quo; honest but ugly for Tailwind users.

My recommendation if you want to ship a clean PR: **option 1** for `class` + `style` (the two attrs Tailwind/CSS users universally need) on all three components, since it satisfies the spec's "additively merge" line without exploding the component count. AsChild variants can come as a separate task if you decide later that's the better convention.

Want to discuss before I touch anything?

> DEVELOPER

Dioxus has some GlobalAttributes or something like that for this use case, does Leptos has something similar too?

> AGENT

Yes — both frameworks have an answer for this, though the ergonomics differ.

## Dioxus 0.7 — `extends = GlobalAttributes`

The Dioxus pattern (from `dioxus-html`):

```rust
#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct MyProps {
    #[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)]
    attrs: Vec<Attribute>,
    pub children: Element,
}

#[component]
fn MyComponent(props: MyProps) -> Element {
    rsx! { div { ..props.attrs, {props.children} } }
}
```

At the call site, callers can pass any HTML global attribute and Dioxus collects them into the `attrs: Vec<Attribute>` field:

```rust
rsx! {
    MyComponent {
        class: "text-4xl font-bold",
        id: "my-heading",
        style: "color: rebeccapurple",
        aria_label: "section title",
        "data-testid": "heading-1",
        "Hello"
    }
}
```

You can also `extends = [GlobalAttributes, ...other-attr-sets]` (e.g., for elements that need both globals and `<button>`-specific attrs).

## Leptos 0.8 — `attr:` prefix + `AddAnyAttr`

Leptos doesn't have a direct equivalent of `GlobalAttributes` in the props struct, but it has a **runtime mechanism** that achieves the same goal: any component whose return type implements `AddAnyAttr` (which is true for almost all view types, including `view! { <h1>...</h1> }`) accepts `attr:foo=value` from the call site, and Leptos splats those onto the component's root element.

```rust
view! {
    <Heading attr:class="text-4xl font-bold" attr:id="my-heading">
        "Hello"
    </Heading>
}
```

This works **without** the `Heading` component author needing to declare `class`/`id`/`style` props — the framework forwards them automatically. The catch: every attr must be prefixed with `attr:`. There's no implicit pass-through like Dioxus's "any unknown attribute → goes into the attrs bag."

You can also use `{..something}` to spread a pre-built attribute collection: `view! { <Heading {..my_attrs} /> }`.

The signature requirement: the return type of `Heading(...)` must implement `AddAnyAttr`. The view types produced by the `view!` macro do — `EitherOf6<View<H1>, View<H2>, ...>` should too because `AddAnyAttr` is implemented for `EitherOf*` when all branches implement it. **Worth verifying for our `Heading` with the EitherOf6 dispatch** before relying on it.

## Practical implications for our three components

| Need | Leptos answer | Dioxus answer |
|---|---|---|
| `<Comp class="foo">` ergonomic | **Doesn't work** today; would need a `class` prop, OR caller writes `attr:class="foo"` | **Doesn't work** today; need `extends = GlobalAttributes` in props |
| `<Comp attr:class="foo">` | **Works automatically** if the return type implements `AddAnyAttr` | N/A — Dioxus doesn't have `attr:` prefix |
| Spread an attribute bundle | `<Comp {..bag} />` (already supported) | `..props.attrs` inside `rsx!` (needs prop declared) |
| Tailwind in user code | Adequate via `attr:class=...` | Requires Dioxus prop changes |

So:

- **Leptos** — the components likely already accept `attr:class="..."` for free as long as `EitherOf6`/`EitherOf7` (used by Heading/Landmark) implement `AddAnyAttr`. We'd just need to confirm and document it. No code change required for the basic pass-through path.
- **Dioxus** — there is no zero-code escape hatch. To match the Leptos UX, each Dioxus `Props` struct would need `#[props(extends = GlobalAttributes)] attrs: Vec<Attribute>` plus `..props.attrs` on the rendered element.

If we want symmetry between the two adapters, the Dioxus side requires code changes; the Leptos side might "just work" via `attr:` (pending verification on the `EitherOf6` AddAnyAttr impl). If you want full symmetry where users write the *same* prop syntax in both frameworks (`<Heading class="…">` without the `attr:` prefix), then both adapters need explicit `class`/`style` props.

2	//!
3	//! The slot receives converted Dioxus attributes from a hosting component and
4	//! passes them to an explicit render callback. The callback owns the root
5	//! element and must spread the provided attrs onto that root. This avoids
6	//! arbitrary `VNode` template mutation, which is not a stable Dioxus composition
7	//! surface.

16	    /// Dioxus attributes produced by the hosting component, ready to spread

19	}

43	    /// Render callback that owns the single root element and spreads the
44	    /// provided attrs onto it.
45	    pub render: Callback<AsChildRenderProps, Element>,
46	}

48	impl Debug for AsChildSlotProps {
49	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {

//! Dioxus `Heading` adapter.
//!
//! Renders the framework-agnostic [`Heading`](ars_components::utility::heading)
//! attribute contract as a semantic `<h1>`–`<h6>` element whose level resolves
//! from explicit props or the inherited [`HeadingContext`]. Ships alongside
//! [`HeadingLevelProvider`] and [`Section`] provider components so descendants
//! receive an updated `HeadingContext` without prop drilling.

pub use ars_components::utility::heading::{
    Api, HeadingContext, Level, Part, Props, heading_level_provider, section,
};
use ars_core::{AttrValue, HtmlAttr};
use dioxus::prelude::*;

use crate::attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs;

fn inherited_context() -> HeadingContext {
    try_use_context::<HeadingContext>().unwrap_or_default()
}

/// Props for the Dioxus [`Heading`] component.
#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct HeadingProps {
    /// Optional component instance ID.
    #[props(optional, into)]
    pub id: Option<String>,

    /// Explicit heading level override; when absent, the nearest
    /// [`HeadingContext`] supplies the resolved level.
    #[props(optional)]
    pub level: Option<Level>,

    /// Heading content rendered inside the resolved tag.
    pub children: Element,
}

/// Dioxus `Heading` component.
///
/// Renders a semantic `<h1>`–`<h6>` element whose level is resolved from the
/// explicit `level` prop, the nearest [`HeadingContext`] published by
/// [`HeadingLevelProvider`] or [`Section`], or [`Level::One`] when no provider
/// is in scope.
#[component]
pub fn Heading(props: HeadingProps) -> Element {
    let ctx = inherited_context();

    let mut core_props = Props::new();

    if let Some(id) = props.id.as_deref() {
        core_props = core_props.id(id);
    }

    if let Some(level) = props.level {
        core_props = core_props.level(level);
    }

    let api = Api::new(core_props, ctx);

    let resolved = api.resolved_level();

    let mut attrs = api.root_attrs(true);

    if props.id.is_none() {
        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, AttrValue::None);
    }

    let attrs = attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(attrs);

    let children = props.children;

    match resolved {
        Level::One => rsx! { h1 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Two => rsx! { h2 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Three => rsx! { h3 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Four => rsx! { h4 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Five => rsx! { h5 { ..attrs, {children} } },
        Level::Six => rsx! { h6 { ..attrs, {children} } },
    }
}

/// Props for the Dioxus [`HeadingLevelProvider`] component.
#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct HeadingLevelProviderProps {
    /// Starting heading level to publish to descendants.
    pub level: Level,

    /// Descendants that should observe the published [`HeadingContext`].
    pub children: Element,
}
```

1	//! Dioxus `Landmark` adapter.
2	//!
3	//! Renders the framework-agnostic [`Landmark`](ars_components::utility::landmark)
4	//! attribute contract as a semantic landmark element selected from the
5	//! configured [`Role`], falling back to `<div role="…">` when no native
6	//! landmark element applies (currently only [`Role::Search`]).
7	
8	pub use ars_components::utility::landmark::{Api, Messages, Part, Props, Role};
9	use ars_core::{AttrValue, Env, HtmlAttr, Locale};
10	use dioxus::prelude::*;
11	
12	use crate::{attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs, resolve_locale, use_messages};
13	
14	/// Props for the Dioxus [`Landmark`] component.
15	#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
16	pub struct LandmarkProps {
17	    /// Optional component instance ID.
18	    #[props(optional, into)]
19	    pub id: Option<String>,
20	
21	    /// Semantic landmark role. Defaults to [`Role::Region`].
22	    #[props(default = Role::Region)]
23	    pub role: Role,
24	
25	    /// Optional ID of an external element that labels this landmark. When set
26	    /// and non-empty, `aria-labelledby` takes precedence over the localized
27	    /// `aria-label`.
28	    #[props(optional, into)]
29	    pub labelledby_id: Option<String>,
30	
31	    /// Localized messages bundle. When omitted, the adapter resolves messages
32	    /// from the [`ArsProvider`](crate::ArsProvider) message registry, falling
33	    /// back to [`Messages::default`] (empty label).
34	    #[props(optional)]
35	    pub messages: Option<Messages>,
36	
37	    /// Locale override for resolving the `aria-label`. When absent, the
38	    /// surrounding [`ArsProvider`](crate::ArsProvider) locale is used.
39	    #[props(optional)]
40	    pub locale: Option<Locale>,
41	
42	    /// Children rendered inside the landmark element.
43	    pub children: Element,
44	}
45	
46	/// Dioxus `Landmark` component.
47	///
48	/// Renders a semantic landmark element (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`,
49	/// `<aside>`, `<footer>`, `<form>`, `<section>`) for the requested [`Role`],
50	/// or an explicit `<div role="search">` fallback when
51	/// [`Api::prefers_generic_fallback_element`] returns `true`. Resolves the
52	/// localized `aria-label` from `messages` (or the provider's message
53	/// registry when omitted) using the optional `locale` override or the
54	/// surrounding [`ArsProvider`](crate::ArsProvider) locale.
55	#[component]
56	pub fn Landmark(props: LandmarkProps) -> Element {
57	    let mut core_props = Props::new().role(props.role);
58	
59	    if let Some(id) = props.id.as_deref() {
60	        core_props = core_props.id(id);
61	    }
62	
63	    if let Some(labelledby) = props.labelledby_id.as_deref() {
64	        core_props = core_props.labelledby_id(labelledby);
65	    }
66	
67	    let resolved_locale = resolve_locale(props.locale.as_ref());
68	    let resolved_messages =
69	        use_messages::<Messages>(props.messages.as_ref(), Some(&resolved_locale));
70	    let env = Env {
71	        locale: resolved_locale,
72	        ..Env::default()
73	    };
74	    let api = Api::new(core_props, &env, &resolved_messages);
75	    let is_native = !api.prefers_generic_fallback_element();
76	    let mut attrs = api.root_attrs(is_native);
77	
78	    if props.id.is_none() {
79	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, AttrValue::None);
80	    }
81	
82	    let attrs = attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(attrs);
83	    let children = props.children;
84	
85	    if !is_native {
86	        return rsx! { div { ..attrs, {children} } };
87	    }
88	
89	    match props.role {
90	        Role::Banner => rsx! { header { ..attrs, {children} } },
91	        Role::Navigation => rsx! { nav { ..attrs, {children} } },
92	        Role::Main => rsx! { main { ..attrs, {children} } },
93	        Role::Complementary => rsx! { aside { ..attrs, {children} } },
94	        Role::ContentInfo => rsx! { footer { ..attrs, {children} } },
95	        Role::Form => rsx! { form { ..attrs, {children} } },
96	        Role::Region => rsx! { section { ..attrs, {children} } },
97	        Role::Search => {
98	            unreachable!("Role::Search is handled by Api::prefers_generic_fallback_element()")
99	        }
100	    }
101	}
102	
```

1	//! Dioxus `Highlight` adapter.
2	//!
3	//! Renders the framework-agnostic [`Highlight`](ars_components::utility::highlight)
4	//! attribute contract as a `<span>` root that wraps alternating
5	//! highlighted / non-highlighted chunks. Highlighted chunks render as
6	//! `<mark>`; non-highlighted chunks render as `<span>`. Locale resolves
7	//! from the optional `locale` prop or the surrounding
8	//! [`ArsProvider`](crate::ArsProvider) context.
9	
10	pub use ars_components::utility::highlight::{Api, HighlightChunk, MatchStrategy, Part, Props};
11	use ars_i18n::Locale;
12	use dioxus::prelude::*;
13	
14	use crate::{attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs, use_locale};
15	
16	/// Props for the Dioxus [`Highlight`] component.
17	#[derive(Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
18	pub struct HighlightProps {
19	    /// Search queries to highlight. An empty or all-empty input emits a
20	    /// single non-highlighted chunk covering the full text.
21	    pub query: Vec<String>,
22	
23	    /// Source text to split into highlighted / non-highlighted chunks.
24	    #[props(into)]
25	    pub text: String,
26	
27	    /// When `true` (default), matching is case-insensitive via locale-aware
28	    /// Unicode case folding.
29	    #[props(default = true)]
30	    pub ignore_case: bool,
31	
32	    /// Match strategy. Defaults to [`MatchStrategy::Contains`].
33	    #[props(default = MatchStrategy::Contains)]
34	    pub match_strategy: MatchStrategy,
35	
36	    /// Optional locale override. When absent, the locale is sourced from the
37	    /// surrounding [`ArsProvider`](crate::ArsProvider) context.
38	    #[props(optional)]
39	    pub locale: Option<Locale>,
40	}
41	
42	/// Dioxus `Highlight` component.
43	///
44	/// Splits `text` into chunks according to the configured `query`,
45	/// `ignore_case`, and `match_strategy`, rendering each chunk as either a
46	/// `<mark>` (highlighted) or `<span>` (unmatched). The root `<span>`
47	/// receives `data-ars-scope="highlight"`, `data-ars-part="root"`, and
48	/// `dir="auto"` from the agnostic core.
49	#[component]
50	pub fn Highlight(props: HighlightProps) -> Element {
51	    let core_props = Props::new()
52	        .query(props.query)
53	        .text(props.text)
54	        .ignore_case(props.ignore_case)
55	        .match_strategy(props.match_strategy);
56	
57	    let api = Api::new(core_props);
58	    let locale = props.locale.unwrap_or_else(|| use_locale().read().clone());
59	
60	    let root_attrs = attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs());
61	
62	    let chunks = api.chunks(&locale).into_iter().map(|chunk| {
63	        let chunk_attrs = attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(api.chunk_attrs(chunk.highlighted));
64	        let text = chunk.text.to_owned();
65	
66	        if chunk.highlighted {
67	            rsx! { mark { ..chunk_attrs, "{text}" } }
68	        } else {
69	            rsx! { span { ..chunk_attrs, "{text}" } }
70	        }
71	    });
72	
73	    rsx! {
74	        span { ..root_attrs,
75	            {chunks}
76	        }
77	    }
78	}
79

2	//!
3	//! Gates children until effects run on the client while preserving SSR fallback
4	//! markup and avoiding adapter-owned wrapper nodes.

6	pub use ars_components::utility::client_only::Props;

9	/// Props for the Dioxus [`ClientOnly`] component.
10	#[derive(dioxus::prelude::Props, Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
11	pub struct ClientOnlyProps {
12	    /// Optional fallback rendered during SSR and before client mount.
13	    #[props(optional)]
14	    pub fallback: Option<Element>,
15	
16	    /// Client-only children rendered after mount.
17	    pub children: Element,
18	}
19	
20	/// Dioxus logical boundary that renders children only after client mount.
21	#[component]
22	pub fn ClientOnly(props: ClientOnlyProps) -> Element {
23	    let mut mounted = use_signal(|| false);
24	
25	    use_effect(move || mounted.set(true));
26	
27	    if mounted() {
28	        rsx! {
29	            {props.children}
30	        }
31	    } else {
32	        rsx! {
33	            {props.fallback}
34	        }
35	    }
36	}

463	    let boundaries_fallback = use_signal(Vec::<String>::new);
464	
465	    let boundaries = inside_boundaries.unwrap_or_else(|| ReadSignal::from(boundaries_fallback));
466	
467	    let provider_locale = resolve_locale(None);

469	        .as_ref()
470	        .map_or(provider_locale, |locale| locale.read().clone());
471	
472	    let resolved_messages = use_messages(messages.as_ref(), Some(&resolved_locale));
473	    let dismiss_label =
474	        dismiss_label.unwrap_or_else(|| (resolved_messages.dismiss_label)(&resolved_locale));

478	    let root_attrs = attr_map_to_dioxus_inline_attrs(api.root_attrs());
479

481	    let start_attrs = inline_attrs.clone();
482	    let end_attrs = inline_attrs;
483	
484	    let mut root_ref = use_signal(|| None::<Rc<MountedData>>);
485	
486	    let handle = use_dismissable(ReadSignal::from(root_ref), props, boundaries);
487	    let root_id = handle.overlay_id.cloned();
488	
489	    rsx! {
490	        div {
491	            id: root_id,
492	            onmounted: move |evt| {
493	                root_ref.set(Some(evt.data()));
494	            },
495	            ..root_attrs,

497	                onclick: move |_| {
498	                    handle.dismiss.call(());
499	                },

504	                onclick: move |_| {
505	                    handle.dismiss.call(());
506	                },
507	                ..end_attrs,
508	            }
509	        }
510	    }
511	}
